tickets.title: Generalize find-omissions preflight stub resolution into a reusable conver tool
tickets.background:
### Goal
Provide a reusable, project-agnostic tool that atomically (1) creates resolving tickets for NOT_RESOLVED `[::STUB::]` markers and (2) rewrites the on-disk marker keys to the new ticket keys, so the `/find-omissions` preflight gate (`validate-no-external-excuses.js --fail-on-excuse`) converges to exit 0.

### Purpose
During the siprs `/find-omissions` preflight, 63 stub markers referenced completed (R1) tickets. Each was code-verified NOT_RESOLVED. The mechanical create+rewrite was done by one-off `/tmp` scripts hardcoded to siprs paths and the 63-marker data. This ticket generalizes that flow into a single atomic script inside `~/shyme/zasso/tools/conver` with full test coverage, so any project can run the same preflight cleanup.

### Motivation
The `/find-omissions` Step 1 gate will be re-run across projects (siprs, conver, others). A reusable tool removes ad-hoc scripting and guarantees atomic all-or-nothing behavior, eliminating the window where 'tickets created but marker keys stale' fails the validator. The two-phase commit makes the write path safe and reviewable via `--no-write`.

### Constraints
Script additions/modifications are limited to `~/shyme/zasso/tools/conver` (the ticket itself is tracked in siprs Tickets.json per user decision). Reuse existing conver modules (`createResolvingTicket`, `extractTicketKey`, `findTicket`) — no reimplementation. No new dependencies. TDD red-green-refactor is mandatory; tests live in conver and must fully guarantee behavior.
scope: **Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
- [File/module path] `~/shyme/zasso/tools/conver/.claude/scripts/tickets/batch-create-resolving-tickets.js`

- [Action: add] New CommonJS script exporting `createResolvingTickets`, `parseArgs`, `main`; reuses `createResolvingTicket` (create-resolving-ticket.js) and `extractTicketKey`/`findTicket` (validate-no-external-excuses.js).

- [What specifically changes] The tool reads a marker manifest, resolves sourceKeys/titles, validates all marker lines on disk, then atomically writes Tickets.json and rewrites marker lines; outputs a rewrite map.

- [Before → After] Before: manual per-marker `create-resolving-ticket.js` CLI + manual file edits (one-off). After: one command `echo '<manifest-json>' | node batch-create-resolving-tickets.js [--no-write]` (manifest via stdin; Tickets.json is always ./Tickets.json; source root is cwd) does the whole preflight resolution atomically.
- [API contract change] New module API `createResolvingTickets({ticketsData, manifest, sourceRoot, noWrite}) -> {success, data?, rewriteMap?, errors?}`; additive only.
- [Data schema change] New manifest schema `[{file, line, content, sourceKey?, seed?: {title?, scope?, background?}}]`; new rewrite-map schema `[{file, line, oldKey, newKey, newContent}]`.
- [Config/env change] New CLI arg `--no-write` only. Tickets.json is always `./Tickets.json`, the source root is cwd, and the manifest is piped via stdin. No env vars.
- [Dependency added/removed] None — Node built-ins `fs`/`path` plus the existing conver ticket modules.
**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
- [Excluded item] siprs `.claude/scripts/tickets/*` and any non-conver file — Why: user constraint; the tool is a conver-local reusable asset consumed by `/find-omissions`.

- [Excluded item] Changes to `/find-omissions` workflow logic (`get-next-check-target-ticket.js`, `add-omission-ticket.js`, `phasify-omissions.js`) — Why: they already consume the resulting Tickets.json; only the preflight create+rewrite step is being tooled.
**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**

- [Affected component] conver `.claude/scripts/tickets/` modules — Nature: the tool imports `createResolvingTicket`/`extractTicketKey`/`findTicket`; no behavior change to them. Response: N (additive import).
- [Affected component] conver `tests/` + `Makefile` — Nature: new test file + fixtures; new Makefile target. Response: N (additive).
- [Affected component] `/find-omissions` preflight runs in other projects — Nature: they can adopt the tool's manifest workflow; existing manual flow remains valid. Response: N (optional adoption).
**find-omissions.md integration (mandatory):**

- [File/module path] `~/shyme/zasso/tools/conver/.claude/commands/find-omissions.md` — Action: modify — Step 1 preflight section rewritten from the manual per-marker `create-resolving-ticket.js` CLI + `update-ticket.js` rewrite instructions to the manifest-driven `batch-create-resolving-tickets.js` flow (manifest format, `--no-write` review step, `validate-no-external-excuses` loop condition).
- [Out of scope] start-ticket / resolve-ticket / split-to-tickets command-file changes — deferred to a follow-up ticket (recorded in Notes as the reuse plan).
testUnit: UT: [Normal] createResolvingTicketsFromManifest — fixture manifest of 2 entries (one with explicit sourceKey+seed, one without) run against a fixture Tickets.json + fixture source files produces: (a) 2 new tickets appended to the max real phase with status `todo` and no `completedAt`/`startedAt`; (b) each ticket carries `stubs[]` = [{file, line, content}]; (c) each `stubs[].content` references the ticket's own new key `P{phase}-{id}`. Covers C002 postcondition (written once), C006 postcondition+invariant.

UT: [Normal] autoExtractSourceKey — manifest entry without `sourceKey` but with content `// [::STUB::] P4-2: ... -- Implement ...` resolves `sourceKey` to `P4-2` via `extractTicketKey`. Covers C001 postcondition.

UT: [Normal] autoDeriveTitle — manifest entry without `seed.title` derives a non-empty title from the marker plan text after `--` (fallback to the reason text), satisfying createResolvingTicket's non-empty-title precondition. Covers C001 postcondition.

UT: [Normal] rewriteMapProduced — a successful run produces an in-memory rewrite map (one entry per marker: `{file, line, oldKey, newKey, newContent}` where `newContent` begins `// [::STUB::] <newKey>:` or `// TODO: [::STUB::] <newKey>:` for TODO-marked lines) and rewrites every on-disk marker line to reference its new key. Covers C002 postcondition.

UT: [Error] unresolvableSourceKeyRejected — entry whose `sourceKey` (or auto-extracted key) matches no ticket in Tickets.json → run exits non-zero, nothing written, stderr names the entry's file:line and the bad key. Covers C001 invariant.

UT: [Error] allOrNothingOnValidationFailure — 2 entries where the 2nd references a missing source file → Tickets.json stays byte-identical and the 1st marker line is untouched (no partial commit). Covers C002 invariant.
UT: [Error] missingManifestFieldRejected — entry missing `file` or `line` or `content` → rejected with a clear error; no writes. Covers C001 precondition.
UT: [Error] markerLineMissingRefused — target line that does not contain `[::STUB::]` → the file is never modified and the failure is reported without touching other files. Covers C003 invariant.

UT: [Boundary] sameFileMultipleMarkersDescending — 3 markers in one file at lines 5, 20, 41 → after the run, re-read the file and assert each was rewritten to its new key (descending-line-order processing keeps indices valid). Covers C003 postcondition.
UT: [Boundary] markerOnLastLineNoTrailingNewline — a marker on the final line of a file without a trailing newline → still rewritten; file ends with the new content. Covers C003 postcondition.
UT: [Boundary] maxPhaseAppendIncrementsIds — existing max real phase has tickets ids 1..N → new resolving tickets get ids N+1, N+2 in the same phase. Covers C002 postcondition.
UT: [Invariant] stubContentReferencesNewKey — for every created ticket, `stubs[].content` references the ticket's own new key (matches `P{phase}-{id}`). Covers C006 invariant.

UT: [Invariant] dryRunNoSideEffects — with `--no-write`, Tickets.json and all source files are byte-identical before/after; the dry-run validation outcome equals the pre-commit validation outcome. Covers C005 invariant.

UT: [Invariant] resolvedPathsAbsolute — manifest-relative paths resolve to absolute paths under the source root (cwd); a path that escapes the source root is rejected. Covers C004 postcondition+invariant.

UT: [Invariant] idempotentReRunNoDuplicates — run the tool on a valid manifest, then run it again with the same manifest; the second run refuses/skips every marker that already references an active ticket key and creates zero new tickets (C007).
UT: [Error] duplicateFileLineRejected — a manifest with two entries sharing the same file:line → validation error, exit non-zero, Tickets.json and source files byte-identical (C008).

UT: [Error] onDiskDivergenceRefused — the manifest says the marker line contains oldKey P4-2 but the on-disk line was edited to reference P9-9 → the entry is refused and the file is never modified (C009).

UT: [Boundary] rewriteMapWrittenBeforeCommit — in commit mode the rewrite map file is written before Tickets.json and before source rewrites; a simulated crash after map write is recoverable by an idempotent re-run that finishes the remaining rewrites without duplicates (C002+C007).
testIntegration: IT: [Integration point] batchCreateResolvingTicketsEndToEnd — run the tool’s CLI (`echo '<manifest-json>' | node batch-create-resolving-tickets.js [--no-write]`) against a fixture Tickets.json + fixture source tree. Assert: (a) Tickets.json gains N new todo tickets in the max real phase, each with `stubs[]` referencing its new key; (b) every fixture marker line on disk is rewritten to reference its new key; (c) running `validate-no-external-excuses.js --fail-on-excuse` against the fixture root exits 0. Covers C001–C006 jointly.

IT: [Verification] dryRunEndToEndNoChanges — `--no-write` on the same fixture → Tickets.json and all source files byte-identical before/after; the stdout validation summary matches the commit-mode pre-validation. Covers C005.

IT: [Prerequisites] conver modules present and self-tested — `.claude/scripts/tickets/create-resolving-ticket.js` (exports `createResolvingTicket`), `validate-no-external-excuses.js` (exports `extractTicketKey`/`findTicket`), `.claude/scripts/lib/create-ticket-from-source.js` exist in `~/shyme/zasso/tools/conver`; the tool requires them.

IT: [Related tickets] /find-omissions Step 1 preflight gate — `preflight-stub-cleanup.js` classifies markers; `validate-no-external-excuses.js --fail-on-excuse` is the loop condition the tool must converge. This ticket's tool replaces the manual create+rewrite step performed in the siprs preflight.
testExceptions: [Item] Unit tests cannot test execution against a real third-party project layout — Reason: it depends on the target project's structure, Tickets.json state, and ticket keys; the manifest-driven interface and fixture-based tests fully specify behavior across every manifest shape (explicit/auto sourceKey, missing seed, same-file multi-marker, no-trailing-newline). This is not an architectural defect: every input is expressible in the manifest and covered by fixtures.

[Item] The AI judgement that a marker is NOT_RESOLVED (semantic code reading) is not testable by this tool — Reason: it requires understanding of the source; the tool's contract starts at the manifest boundary (it consumes the manifest produced by that judgement) and is fully tested for all manifest shapes. This is not an architectural defect: the tool has no behavior outside the manifest boundary.

[Item] Producing real tickets in a live Tickets.json is not testable in unit tests — Reason: it would mutate a real ticket database; covered by the fixture integration test plus the existing siprs preflight run this tool generalizes. This is not an architectural defect: the tool's write path is identical for fixtures and live data and is fully verified on fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: [Happy path] A valid manifest (mix of explicit and auto-extracted sourceKey) → every resolving ticket created (status `todo`, no startedAt/completedAt, `stubs[]` embedded with its new key) AND every on-disk marker line rewritten to reference its new key; running `validate-no-external-excuses.js --fail-on-excuse` against the fixture root exits 0; the rewrite map is written.

[Error case] An invalid manifest (unresolvable sourceKey, missing file, non-marker target line, malformed entry) → exit non-zero, Tickets.json and all source files byte-identical (all-or-nothing), stderr lists each failure with file:line and an action directive.

[Edge case] `--no-write` → full validation with zero side effects (everything byte-identical); multiple markers in one file → rewritten in descending line order; a marker on the final line without a trailing newline → still rewritten; a path escaping the source root → rejected.

[Happy path] find-omissions.md Step 1 documents the new manifest-driven flow (manifest format, --no-write review, validate loop) so a fresh session can execute the preflight cleanup using the tool alone.
[Edge case] Batch safety verified: idempotent re-run (C007), duplicate file:line rejection (C008), on-disk divergence refusal (C009), and rewrite-map-first recovery (C002+C007) all pass their tests.

contracts.precondition: A manifest entry carries {file: string, line: positive int, content: string} and optionally {sourceKey: string, seed: {title?, scope?, background?}}. Testable input schema: a JSON array of such objects.
contracts.postcondition: sourceKey is auto-extracted from content via `extractTicketKey` when omitted; seed.title is auto-derived from the marker plan text after `--` (fallback: reason text) when missing, so `createResolvingTicket`'s non-empty-title precondition is always satisfied. Testable output: every entry yields a ticket with a non-empty title and a resolvable sourceKey.
contracts.invariant: An entry whose sourceKey (explicit or auto-extracted) does not exist in Tickets.json is rejected with an error and the whole run aborts before any write. Testable predicate: such an entry produces exit!=0 and zero file mutations.

contracts.precondition: All manifest entries are valid and every target marker line is resolvable on disk.
contracts.postcondition: Tickets.json is written exactly once (all new tickets appended to the max real phase with auto-incremented ids, status `todo`, no startedAt/completedAt) AND every target marker line is rewritten to reference its new key; no intermediate partial state is observable. Testable output: post-run Tickets.json has N new tickets; each source file's target line contains the new key. The rewrite map is written before Tickets.json so a crash mid-commit is recoverable by an idempotent re-run (C007).
contracts.invariant: Any validation failure leaves Tickets.json and all source files byte-identical (all-or-nothing). Testable predicate: capture pre-run bytes; on failure, post-run bytes are equal. Recovery after a crash window requires no manual repair: re-running with the same manifest converges without duplicating tickets (C007).

contracts.precondition: A target line index exists within the file.
contracts.postcondition: A line containing `[::STUB::]` is replaced with newContent that carries the new ticket key; multiple markers in one file are processed in descending line order so indices remain valid. Testable output: re-reading the file shows each target line replaced.
contracts.invariant: A line without `[::STUB::]` is never modified, even if listed in the manifest. Testable predicate: such a line remains byte-identical and the run reports the refusal.

contracts.precondition: File paths in the manifest are repo-relative (or already absolute).
contracts.postcondition: Paths resolve against the source root (cwd) to absolute paths before any I/O. Testable output: the rewrite map and any diagnostics contain absolute paths under the source root.
contracts.invariant: Resolved paths are absolute and within the source root; a path escaping the root is rejected. Testable predicate: `path.isAbsolute` and `path.relative(root, p)` does not start with `..`.

contracts.precondition: `--no-write` flag is set.
contracts.postcondition: Full validation runs (manifest parse, sourceKey resolution, marker-line presence) with zero writes to Tickets.json or source files. Testable output: exit 0/1 reflects validation only; stdout reports the would-be results.
contracts.invariant: The dry-run validation outcome equals the pre-commit validation outcome of a normal run. Testable predicate: same manifest → same pass/fail set.

contracts.precondition: A resolving ticket is created from a manifest entry.
contracts.postcondition: The ticket carries `stubs[]` = [{file, line, content}] reflecting the source marker. Testable output: each new ticket has `Array.isArray(stubs)` with length ≥ 1.
contracts.invariant: Every `stubs[].content` references the ticket's own new key `P{phase}-{id}` (the createResolvingTicket key rewrite). Testable predicate: `content` contains the new key and no other P-key.

contracts.precondition: A manifest entry references a marker that already points to an ACTIVE ticket (status todo/in_progress/planned/remanded).
contracts.postcondition: The marker is skipped or the entry is refused as already-resolved; no duplicate resolving ticket is created.
contracts.invariant: Re-running the tool with the same manifest never increases the ticket count (idempotent). Testable predicate: two consecutive runs produce the same Tickets.json ticket set.

contracts.precondition: The manifest contains two entries with the same file:line.
contracts.postcondition: The duplicate is rejected as a validation error; the whole run aborts before any write.
contracts.invariant: At most one manifest entry per file:line is accepted. Testable predicate: a duplicate file:line yields exit!=0 and zero mutations.

contracts.precondition: A target marker line exists on disk.
contracts.postcondition: The on-disk line is verified to contain the expected oldKey before any rewrite.
contracts.invariant: If the on-disk line does not contain the expected oldKey (manifest/disk divergence), the entry is refused and the file is never modified. Testable predicate: a divergent line yields exit!=0 and the file stays byte-identical.

tickets.notes:
- Implementation steps: (1) confirm conver test-runner convention (top-level `tests/*.test.cjs` use `node:test`+`node:assert`, run via `node --test tests/<name>.test.cjs`, NOT yet wired into Makefile — only `tests/rfc-graph/*` is), (2) write the test suite first (TDD red) with fixture Tickets.json + fixture source files under `tests/fixtures/`, (3) implement the script, (4) green, (5) add a Makefile target (e.g. `test-stub-resolution:`) running the new test, (6) refactor.
- Risks: path-format mismatch with phasify `rewriteSourceMarkerLines` — verify whether `stubs[].file` should be absolute or repo-relative by reading conver's `phasify-omissions.js` before finalizing the rewrite-map file path format.
- Caveats: `createResolvingTicket` requires a non-empty `seed.title`; the tool must auto-derive it from the marker plan text. The stubs key-rewrite regex `/[::STUB::]s+[^s:]+/` breaks on keyless `MUST RESOLVE` markers — the manifest must supply a resolvable `sourceKey` for those (as done for siprs asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs).
- Open items: keep `--no-write` as the review seam; consider a `--manifest-schema` mode that validates a manifest without touching anything.
- Future improvements: add a `--from-preflight` flag that parses `preflight-stub-cleanup.js` JSON output directly into a manifest, further automating Step 1.
Step 8 gate note: validate-no-external-excuses.js --fail-on-excuse exits 1 on the siprs tree because of 63 pre-existing stub markers that reference completed tickets (the find-omissions preflight state, deliberately rolled back per user instruction). These stubs are NOT owned by PX-1: its targetStubs is verified_empty (enumerate-ticket-targets auto-assigned one unrelated siprs stub at src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:165, which was removed as out-of-scope since PX-1 implementation files are new files in ~/shyme/zasso/tools/conver). The Step 8 gate intent — the ticket being made must not own a terminal-excuse/stale-key stub — is satisfied. Resolving the 63 siprs stubs is the /find-omissions preflight scope, explicitly out of scope for PX-1.

### Design principles
- B1 (safe execution): the tool never calls the create-resolving-ticket.js CLI per marker (N writes, partial-commit risk). It calls the exported `createResolvingTicket` function in memory, validates the whole manifest, then writes Tickets.json once + rewrites marker lines (two-phase commit).
- B2 (separable core): the manifest-driven batch-creation + atomic-commit core is separated from the stub-specific marker-key rewrite (the rewrite is an option). The manifest interface ({file,line,content,sourceKey?,seed?}) is deliberately generic so sibling ticket-creation flows can reuse the core.

### Same-family survey (evidence for future reuse)
- `create-crime-deferral-ticket.js` (start-ticket), `create-deferral-ticket.js` (resolve-ticket), and `add-tickets-for-phase.js`→`bulkAddTickets` (split-to-tickets) all share the deep-clone + non-PX-max-phase todo-append family with `create-resolving-ticket.js`. They differ only in seed content/use-case.
- Reuse plan (future ticket, NOT this ticket): apply the separable core to start-ticket / resolve-ticket / split-to-tickets, verifying the manifest interface can express crime-deferral / deferral / bulk-add seeds, and update each command file accordingly.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] For a valid manifest, every entry produces exactly one resolving ticket appended to the max real phase with a monotonically increasing id; every ticket has status `todo`, no `startedAt`/`completedAt`, and `stubs[]` referencing its own new key.
- [Error invariant] Any validation failure (unresolvable sourceKey, missing file, non-marker line, path escaping the source root, malformed manifest) aborts before any write — Tickets.json and every source file remain byte-identical.
- [Internal state invariant] The rewrite map is the single source of truth coupling new ticket keys to on-disk marker lines; it is produced only after all tickets validate and is consumed atomically with the writes, so no 'tickets created but markers stale' state is observable.
- [Boundary invariant] Manifest file paths are repo-relative and resolve against the source root (cwd) to absolute paths inside the root; `--no-write` never produces side effects; multiple markers in one file are rewritten in descending line order.
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] Every failure logged to stderr with prefix `[batch-create-resolving-tickets]` and the entry's file:line; per-entry error messages are self-contained action directives (English).
- [Metrics] On success, print a JSON summary to stdout: `{createdTickets: N, rewrittenMarkers: N, filesTouched: M, ticketsPath, rewriteMapPath}`.
- [Error tracking] Failures collected as structured objects `{entryIndex?, file?, line?, key?, error}` and emitted to stderr; exit code 1 on any validation failure, 0 on success, 2 on argument errors.
- [Health check] `--no-write` doubles as a health check: it runs full validation and reports pass/fail with the would-be summary, mutating nothing.

tickets.investigation:
- Material evidence gathered in Step 5: conver (at `~/shyme/zasso/tools/conver`) already ships the exact reusable modules the tool needs: `.claude/scripts/tickets/create-resolving-ticket.js` exports `createResolvingTicket({ticketsData, sourceKey, seed, stubs})` which deep-clones via `.claude/scripts/lib/create-ticket-from-source.js`, forces status `todo`, strips `startedAt`/`completedAt`, appends to the max real phase with an auto-incremented id, and rewrites `stubs[].content` keys to the new key via `/[::STUB::]s+[^s:]+/`. `.claude/scripts/tickets/validate-no-external-excuses.js` exports `extractTicketKey` (regex `STUB_TICKET_KEY_RE = /[::STUB::].*?([A-Z]+[A-Zd]*-d+)/`) and `findTicket` (P{phase}-{id} resolution). Top-level `tests/*.test.cjs` use `node:test`+`node:assert` (`describe`/`it`) and run via `node --test tests/<name>.test.cjs`; they are NOT yet wired into the Makefile (only `tests/rfc-graph/*.test.cjs` is, via `test-rfc-graph`). The Makefile `test-conver` target runs tsc-compiled `dist/*.test.js`; the new tool's test should follow the `.cjs` convention. The siprs preflight run validated the flow: `createResolvingTicket` ×63 → marker rewrites → `validate-no-external-excuses` 63/63 pass. The keyless `MUST RESOLVE` marker (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:165) needs an explicit sourceKey because the key-rewrite regex would mangle it.

### Design-rationale evidence
- Direct CLI per-marker invocation writes Tickets.json N times and leaves a partial-commit window if a later invocation fails; the exported `createResolvingTicket` is pure (returns merged data, caller writes once), which the tool exploits for atomic all-or-nothing commit.
- `createResolvingTicket` requires a non-empty `seed.title` and rewrites `stubs[].content` keys via `/[::STUB::]s+[^s:]+/` — the tool must auto-derive titles and supply resolvable sourceKeys for keyless MUST-RESOLVE markers.
- Safety mechanisms tested here: idempotent re-run (skip/refuse markers already referencing active tickets), duplicate file:line rejection, on-disk oldKey verification before rewrite, rewrite-map-first write for crash recovery.

tickets.title: Apply the separable generic ticket-creation core to sibling command flows
tickets.background:
### Goal
Make the PX-1 separable core the single shared ticket-creation path for all conver ticket-adding flows (start-ticket crime-deferral, resolve-ticket deferral, split-to-tickets bulk phase add) and verify the manifest/seed interface expresses resolving / deferral / crime-deferral / bulk-add shapes.

### Purpose
`create-crime-deferral-ticket.js`, `create-deferral-ticket.js`, and `add-tickets-for-phase.js`→`bulkAddTickets` each create tickets by deep-clone + non-PX-max-phase todo append — the same family as `create-resolving-ticket.js`. PX-1 established a safe batch pattern (validate-all → write-once). This ticket unifies the sibling flows behind that core so every creation flow inherits atomic-commit / idempotency / duplicate-rejection / on-disk-verification safety.

### Motivation
The sibling commands still write Tickets.json per invocation (partial-commit risk) and each reimplements ticket creation. Unifying removes that risk everywhere and makes the creation path uniform, so future preflight runs and the /find-omissions pipeline behave identically across projects.

### Constraints
Changes limited to `~/shyme/zasso/tools/conver`. PX-1 (the core) must be implemented first — it is a hard prerequisite. Reuse the PX-1 core rather than reimplementing. No new dependencies. Behavior parity is the acceptance bar: pre-unification output must equal post-unification output (verified by git-stash diff). TDD red-green-refactor mandatory.

### Implementation steps
1. Confirm PX-1 is implemented and green (the core exists and its tests pass). 2. Route the three flow scripts through it (green). 5. Update the three command .md files. 6. Refactor.

### Risks
- Behavior parity is hard to prove by hand — the acceptance test diffs pre-unification (git stash of the old script) vs post-unification output on the same fixture.

- `bulkAddTickets` already batches internally; the unification must not regress its nodeIds-coverage verification.

- PX-2 is blocked on PX-1: the core must exist before this ticket's integration tests can run.
- The seed schema must carry flow-specific fields (stubId / crimeId / stubs[] / tickets[]) without losing PX-1's safety contracts.

- Whether the unified core should fully replace `bulkAddTickets` or wrap it (wrapping preserves its existing tests).
- Whether `createTickets` should accept a mixed array of different seed shapes in one commit (batch across flows) or one flow per invocation.

tickets.background:
Phase P0 Crate Foundation & Scope Definition covers the crate purpose (N0001-related), non-goals and Tauri integration boundary (N0003), terminology glossary (N0004), compliance requirements including MSRV/OS targets (N0005), versioning policy (N0006), 15-item normative functional requirements scope (N0007), module directory structure and crate responsibility rationale (N0008), and M20 implementation priority map with design decision table (N0002). These 7 nodes form the foundational specification that constrains all downstream implementation phases.

### Goal
Produce a single authoritative spec document (`specs/P0-1.md`) that defines siprs crate identity, design constraints, and implementation roadmap. The spec must consolidate 7 RFC architectural nodes into a coherent, internally consistent specification that serves as the reference for all downstream implementation tickets (P0-2 through P0-6, and all P1+ phases). Every downstream ticket must be traceable back to a section in this foundation spec.

### Purpose
The siprs crate cannot be implemented piecemeal without a shared understanding of what the crate IS and IS NOT. Without an explicit foundation specification, each implementation ticket would operate with its own implicit assumptions about crate scope, module layout, naming conventions, and architectural boundaries — leading to integration failures, duplicated effort, and design drift. This spec establishes the common ground: a single source of truth for crate purpose, non-goals, terminology, compliance constraints, functional requirements, module structure, versioning, and implementation priority.

### Motivation
Current codebase has partial implementations scattered across `src/` sub-directories (api/, build/, config/, error/, model/, security/, state/, tests/) — these grew organically from boundify-graph output without an overarching spec. New contributors (including AI agents) lack a unified reference for what the crate should ultimately become. The RFC-ROOT.md contains comprehensive design but in prose form, not as a structured implementation spec. Creating P0-1 spec closes the gap between the RFC design intent and the scattered implementation artifacts, providing a structured foundation for the TDD workflow in all subsequent tickets.

### Constraints
- **Time**: This ticket produces a spec document only — no executable Rust code. Spec must be created before any implementation ticket enters the Green phase.
- **Scope boundary**: Spec covers only N0001–N0008 nodes. Downstream nodes (N0009 concurrency, N0010 command serialization, N0011 public API, N0013 ClientConfig, N0033 AudioMixer, N0037 FFI layer, N0039 build strategy, N0043 shutdown, N0045 lock rules, N0046 observability, N0047 security, N0050 audio device, N0052 test strategy, N0055 panic policy, N0057 acceptance criteria) are referenced only as forward pointers, not fully specified.
- **Consistency constraint**: Spec must not contradict any existing implementation in `src/` without a note documenting the deviation. Existing `src/config/versioning_policy.rs` must be referenced accurately.

Terminology: Client, Account, Call, Media Session, Source, Chunk Pair, Raw SIP Event definitions

testExceptions: Exception: Compliance with MSRV 1.95 / tokio runtime / PJSIP 2.17 cannot be verified by unit tests [cannot test]. Reason: MSRV is a Cargo.toml metadata field enforced by the Rust toolchain at build time; tokio is a runtime dependency resolved by Cargo at compile time; PJSIP version is a vendor directory constraint. All three are verified by CI build matrix across 3 target OS. Not a design defect — these are build-time constraints, not runtime behaviors, making CI the correct verification layer.

Exception: 15 functional requirements completeness is a specification property, not testable in code [not testable]. Reason: Correctness of a specification is a human-review property — automation can check format (headings exist, IDs are present) but cannot verify that the listed requirements accurately capture the RFC's normative intent. Not a design defect — spec completeness is a verification property addressable by cross-reference review against RFC-ROOT.md §5 text. Alternative verification: each of the 15 requirements mentioned verbatim in the spec; structural grep-based confirmation all 15 REQ-IDs appear in the spec Markdown.

Exception: Single-crate design decision is architectural — cannot be unit-tested [cannot test]. Reason: The decision to keep signalling, media, event bus in one crate is a design choice encoded in Cargo.toml and module structure (no workspace members). There is no runtime behavior that proves or disproves this decision. Not a design defect — this is a deliberate architectural choice documented in RFC §6.1 with future split path. Alternative verification: `cargo tree` confirms no siprs-* sibling crates; module structure shows audio/, ffi/, runtime/ as sub-directories not workspace members.

Exception: M20 priority ordering correctness (P0 before P3) is a planning artifact, not a testable property [not testable]. Reason: Priority is a development scheduling concern — the table can be verified for internal consistency (no lower priority before higher) but there is no runtime assertion that confirms the ordering is "correct." Not an architectural defect — priority is a planning-level concern verified by structural table audit.

Exception: Contract invariant stability (e.g., 'Definitions stable within document' C005 invariant) is a documentation quality attribute [not testable]. Reason: Invariant assertions in a specification document describe intended constraints, not machine-checkable properties at this stage. Not a design defect — documentation quality is verified by manual review of the spec for internal consistency across all 7 node sections.

**[Happy path] Spec is complete and internally consistent** — all 15 functional requirements from N0007 have corresponding sections. All 7 node descriptions reference their RFC source sections. The M20 priority table lists 15 items with correct priority tiers (P0–P3), each with a valid Q-reference. Module structure diagram matches RFC §6. Versioning policy distinguishes 0.x from 1.0+. **[Error case] Spec identifies contradictions with existing implementation** — if `src/config/versioning_policy.rs` or any existing code contradicts the RFC design, the spec documents the deviation in a note rather than silently choosing one. The spec does not claim the crate is fully implemented when it is not.

**[Edge case] Spec handles forward references to downstream tickets** — nodes that are not part of N0001–N0008 (e.g., N0009 concurrency, N0013 ClientConfig, N0039 build strategy) are referenced as forward pointers with clear indication that they are specified in separate P-phase tickets. The spec contains no orphan references to nodes outside its scope.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
### Translatability improvements planned for this ticket

**Scope**: This ticket produces only a spec document (`specs/P0-1.md`) — no Rust code is modified. However, the spec itself is a form of code (documentation as code) and must meet readability standards.

#### Spec document translatability
1. **Section headings as function names**: Each node section (N0001–N0008) has a heading that reads as a verb/noun phrase describing what it defines (e.g., "§1 Purpose — Responsibilities of this crate", "§2 Non-goals & Tauri Integration Boundary")
2. **Consistent section structure**: Every node section follows the same template: Node ID → Title → RFC Reference → Description → Cross-references → Contract mappings. This consistency makes the spec translatable as a table of contents.
3. **Cross-references as explicit links**: References to downstream nodes include parenthetical explanations (e.g., "depends_on N0009 Concurrency — specified in P0-2") rather than bare node IDs
4. **M20 priority table as readable prose**: Each row reads as a complete sentence: priority tier → what → why (Q-reference) → where (code impact)

#### Existing code (not touched but noted for future improvement)
5. **`src/config/versioning_policy.rs`**: Empty `Config {}` struct with `// TODO: [::STUB::]` — violates translatability because the struct name `Config` is a generic noun that doesn't convey its purpose (versioning policy). Future improvement: Rename to `VersioningConfig` or `VersionPolicy` when implemented.
6. **Boundify-generated files in `src/`**: All existing source files have Design Artifact headers but empty implementations. The `[::STUB::]` and `[::TICKET::]` markers satisfy the First-Class Rule but the files are not yet readable as executable prose. Resolution occurs in downstream P0 tickets.

tickets.background:
## Goal
Establish the single-core-reactor concurrency foundation for the siprs crate. The runtime/ module delivers a dedicated reactor thread that serializes all PJSUA control API calls through an unbounded MPSC channel, achieving Send+Sync safety without exposing PJSUA thread-safety constraints to library users.

## Purpose
PJSIP internally spawns native threads and fires callbacks on arbitrary threads. Calling pjsua_* functions from multiple threads concurrently causes data races, undefined behavior, and panics. This ticket implements the CoreReactor thread that owns the single source of truth (ClientState) and processes all commands sequentially.

## Motivation
Every higher-level feature (accounts, calls, audio, events) depends on thread-safe access to PJSIP. Without this foundation, the crate cannot provide any safe public API. The MPSC+oneshot pattern is the architectural invariant that unlocks all downstream tickets (P0-3 through P1+).

## Constraints
- Single-core-reactor: exactly one std::thread::JoinHandle<()> for all PJSUA control
- RuntimeCommand uses tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender for submission (never bounded channels - must not deadlock on backpressure)
- Each command variant carries a tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<_, SipError>> for async reply
- Four execution contexts explicitly modeled but only #1 (User async) and #2 (Core reactor) are instantiated in P0-2; #3 (PJSIP callbacks, P0-6) and #4 (Audio worker, P1+) are interface contracts only
- Lock rules: read().await for query snapshot APIs; write().await for reactor state mutation; blocking_read() prohibited
- ClientState source of truth is owned exclusively by reactor thread, not by RwLock - RwLock is only for snapshot sharing
- conf_port_id lives in PjsuaBackend, not in CallEntry

acceptanceCriteria: [Happy path] CoreReactor::spawn(boot_config) starts a dedicated OS thread. RuntimeHandle::submit(command) enqueues it via MPSC. Reactor thread processes it in FIFO order, calls the corresponding Backend trait method, and sends the result back via oneshot. RuntimeHandle::is_terminated() == false while reactor runs.
[Happy path] Shutdown command completes all prior commands, sends Ok(()) reply, reactor thread exits JoinHandle, is_terminated() == true.

[Error case] Reactor panics during dispatch: std::panic::catch_unwind captures the panic, sets is_terminated() = true, subsequent submit() returns Err(ReactorDown) immediately without blocking the caller.
[Error case] Shutdown submitted before Initialize: reactor returns Err(NotInitialized) but stays alive to accept further commands.
[Error case] Double Shutdown: after first Shutdown completes, second submit(Shutdown) returns Ok(()) immediately - reactor already stopped.
[Edge case] 10,000 rapid consecutive dummy commands: all processed without overflow, each reply received in order, no memory exhaustion.
[Edge case] Command submitted immediately after spawn() before reactor thread has entered its loop: command is buffered by MPSC and processed as soon as reactor starts receiving.

tickets.investigation:
## Investigation Results

### RFC Graph Analysis
- **N0009 (Section 7 Concurrency Model & Execution Contexts)**: Defines 4 execution contexts, single-reactor architecture, MPSC command serialization. Key design decisions: (1) PJSIP callbacks must NOT call pjsua_* directly - only enqueue work, (2) Audio worker tasks communicate via lock-free queue, (3) Single reactor sufficient for ~30 concurrent calls.
- **N0010 (Section 7.2 RuntimeCommand & Command Serialization)**: Full RuntimeCommand enum with 10 variants, each carrying oneshot::Sender for async reply. Enum design ensures all pjsua_* calls go through the channel, guaranteeing Send+Sync.
- **N0045 (Section 33 Runtime Internal State & Lock Rules)**: ClientState/AccountEntry/CallEntry struct definitions. Lock rules: read().await for queries (blocking_read() prohibited - will panic inside tokio runtime), write().await for reactor updates. conf_port_id managed by PjsuaBackend, not exposed in CallEntry.

### Existing Code Analysis
- `src/lib.rs` lines 44: `// [::STUB::] P0-2: runtime/ - Reactor, Command, Handle` - module is declared but commented out. Need to uncomment.
- `src/concurrency_contexts/command_serialization.rs` - contains `pub trait Service {}` stub bound to N0010. This is a DIFFERENT design approach (trait-based) from the enum-based RFC section 7.2. P0-2 implements the enum-based design. The Service trait should remain as a [::STUB::] cross-reference.
- `src/error/error_design_siperror.rs` - SipError is a stub `pub enum Error {}` (P0-4). P0-2 needs its own internal error type.
- `src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs` - N0017: RuntimeCommand error design stub (P0-4 M20 refinement).
- `src/error/m20_shutdown_routing.rs` - N0044: M20 Shutdown command routing stub (P1).
- `src/model/id_design_newtype.rs` - AccountId/CallId stubs (P0-3). P0-2 uses u64 placeholders.
- `Cargo.toml` - tokio with sync/rt/rt-multi-thread/time/macros features already present. No new crate deps needed.

### Key Architectural Decisions
1. **Enum dispatch rather than trait dispatch**: RFC section 7.2 specifies a concrete RuntimeCommand enum with named variants. This is intentional - it enables exhaustive match in the reactor loop and compile-time verification that every command is handled.
2. **Unbounded MPSC (not bounded)**: PJSIP operations can have unpredictable completion times; a bounded channel would risk deadlock under load. Memory is bounded by the rate of command submission from the single user async context.
3. **reactor thread is not equal to tokio runtime thread**: The reactor runs on a dedicated std::thread (non-tokio) to avoid blocking the async runtime with synchronous pjsua_* calls. The reactor can block; tokio tasks must not.
4. **ClientState ownership**: Single-writer (reactor) + multiple-reader (async queries) pattern via tokio::sync::RwLock. The RwLock guards the SNAPSHOT, not the source of truth - the source of truth is the reactor thread's local state variable.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
## Boy Scout Rule - Translatability Plan

### Inside P0-2 scope

Files being created (runtime/ module) follow translatability from inception:
- **Functions as verb phrases**: `CoreReactor::spawn()`, `RuntimeHandle::submit()`, `handle.is_terminated()`, `reactor.dispatch_command()`, `backend.initialize()` - each function name is a verb phrase that reads as a command in the processing narrative.
- **Structs as nouns**: `CoreReactor` (the thing that reacts), `RuntimeHandle` (thing you hold to submit), `ClientState` (the state of the client) - each type name is a domain concept.
- **One function one responsibility**: `recv_and_dispatch()` receives from MPSC then dispatches. `execute_command()` performs the Backend call. `send_reply()` sends the oneshot response. Not one big `run()` function.
- **Named constants**: Role constants (e.g., `const THREAD_NAME: &str = "siprs-reactor"`) extracted from string literals. Timeout values as `Duration` constants.
- **No error swallowing**: Every Result is propagated or explicitly handled. The `send_reply` helper logs on send error but never silently drops.

### Outside P0-2 scope (proactive improvements to touched files)

- **lib.rs** (touched to uncomment `pub mod runtime`): The existing `// [::STUB::] P0-N: module -- description` comments are well-structured. No change needed - readability is already good.
- **concurrency_contexts/command_serialization.rs**: Contains `pub trait Service {}` with a `// TODO: ...` comment but NO `[::STUB::]` marker. **Action**: Add `// [::STUB::] P0-2 DEPRECATED - superceded by runtime/command.rs RuntimeCommand enum` marker. Also rename `Service` to a more descriptive name if touched, but since it remains a stub, add the STUB marker and leave the trait name for P0-6 resolution.
- **Cargo.toml** (if touched): Verify tokio features list is clean and documented. No change needed presently.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Establish the siprs crate's public identity as a safe asynchronous SIP audio client library. Define SipClient as the top-level facade that integrates with P0-2's CoreReactor/RuntimeHandle/RuntimeCommand infrastructure.

### Purpose
Provide Rust application code with a safe, async-native facade over PJSUA SIP functionality, limited to audio-only voice communication. This crate exists to eliminate unsafe FFI boilerplate and deliver SIP calling capabilities through idiomatic Rust APIs — Result propagation, tokio async/await, typed events, and structured configuration.

### Motivation
P0-3 is the gateway ticket that establishes the crate's architectural identity before downstream tickets implement specific sub-systems: error types (P0-4), event system (P0-5), FFI layer (P0-6), audio pipeline (P1+). Without a defined SipClient + ClientConfig, no downstream implementation has a cohesive host. This ticket crystallizes the purpose defined in RFC 1 (§1) into concrete public API surface.

### Constraints
- Audio-only: no video API surface (RFC §1, §2). Enforced by compile-time assertions.
- All async public APIs must return Result<T, SipError> (RFC §1 constraint on N0001).
- PJSIP v2.x via FFI only — no raw socket-level SIP stack.
- Single crate with modular internal structure (RFC §6, C009).
- Shutdown must be cancellation-safe and idempotent (RFC §32, C044).
- SecretString for password storage (RFC §35-36, C048).
- Microphone input is optional via cpal-input feature flag (RFC §40, C051).
- MSRV 1.95, OS targets per RFC §4 (C006).

No video-related types exist in any src/ file. This is a compile-time property verified by the type system and module visibility. Any future addition of video types would fail the compile-time invariant tests defined in testUnit. This is NOT an architectural defect — the RFC deliberately scopes to audio-only, and the type system enforces this at compile time. Alternative verification: compile-time invariant checks in testUnit (UT: [Boundary] Audio-only API surface, UT: [Invariant] No video types in public module exports).

Exception: SipClient::new returning Result is a type-level invariant, cannot test as individual runtime assertion — Reason: The function signature SipClient::new(config: ClientConfig) -> Result<(Self, Receiver<SipEvent>), SipError> is enforced by the Rust compiler at compile time — every caller must handle both Ok and Err. The Err branch IS tested in testUnit for invalid config. Alternative verification: compile_fail tests in testUnit cover the error path at the type level. This is NOT an architectural defect — returning Result from fallible operations is idiomatic Rust design.

Exception: All public async fn signatures returning Result<T, SipError> cannot test individually at runtime — Reason: This architectural invariant is enforced by the Rust compiler and verified by compile-time tests in testUnit. Runtime testing of each method's specific error return path requires downstream tickets (P0-4 for SipError variants, P0-5 for event types, P0-6 for FFI integration). This ticket establishes the convention and verifies it at compile time. This is not a defect — this is a deliberate design choice for the facade layer.
acceptanceCriteria: [Happy path] SipClient::new is called with a valid ClientConfig — returns Ok(SipClient) with initialized CoreReactor. All five module declarations (client, config, account, call, transport) are active in lib.rs. SipClient::shutdown() terminates cleanly. The compile-time invariant tests pass (no video types, all APIs return Result, SipClient is Send+Sync).
[Error case] SipClient::new is called with empty sip_proxy_host — returns Err(SipError::InvalidConfig("sip_proxy_host must not be empty")). CoreReactor is NOT spawned. No orphaned resources.

[Edge case] SipClient::shutdown() is called twice — first call succeeds (returns Ok(())), second call is a no-op (also returns Ok(()), verifying C044: Shutdown is idempotent). Calling any method after shutdown returns Err(SipError::Shutdown).

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvements for P0-3:
1. lib.rs: Uncomment module declarations — convert [::STUB::] comments into active pub mod statements. Each module gets a one-line comment explaining its responsibility (noun phrase).
2. BootConfig → ClientConfig migration: Rename BootConfig::config: String to typed ClientConfig fields. This improves reader comprehension because "config" as a String tells nothing about its structure, while ClientConfig.sip_proxy_host etc. are self-documenting.
3. RuntimeCommand::Initialize { config: String } → { config: ClientConfig }: Replace opaque String with typed struct. This transforms a function that reads as "initialize with string" to "initialize with client configuration" — a transparent statement of intent.
4. ClientConfig validation: Extract validate() method with named error variants (InvalidConfig::EmptyHost, InvalidConfig::InvalidPort) instead of leaving validation implicit. This turns "check config" into "validate config structure" — a verb phrase that communicates what happens.
5. SipClient::new constructor: Implement the Builder pattern (already designed in client_config_spec.rs) for optional fields, keeping required fields in a non-optional constructor. This makes the calling code read as SipClient::builder().stun(...).ice(true).build() instead of SipClient::new(config_with_15_fields).
6. Apply the Boy Scout Rule to any runtime code touched during migration: ensure all functions read as verb phrases, all variables as domain nouns, no single-letter variable names, no hardcoded magic values.

tickets.title: Error Design — SipError, SipErrorKind, and M20 RuntimeCommand Error Mapping

contracts.precondition: Public API design in progress — SipClient facade methods (initialize, shutdown, etc.) define return types. Precondition test: compile-time assertion that each public async fn returns Result<_, SipError> (testUnit: "Contract C017 Precondition — API return types").
contracts.postcondition: Error design constrains API return types: all public async functions in SipClient must return Result<T, SipError>. Postcondition test: SipError struct has exactly 6 fields (kind, message, native_status, account_id, call_id, retryable) verified via construction test; SipErrorKind implements required traits (Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug) verified via compile-time assertion.
contracts.invariant: All APIs return Result<T, SipError> — invariant verified via 3 mechanisms: (1) compile-time Send+Sync assertion on SipError ensures it meets async API requirements, (2) struct field count assertion ensures no API-incompatible modifications, (3) exhaustive pattern match over SipErrorKind prevents accidental omission of error cases in API error handling.

contracts.precondition: Error design constrains API return types — M20 RuntimeCommand handlers (ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect, GetAccountInfo) must return errors through the existing SipError/SipErrorKind system. Precondition test: each M20 error converter function returns Result<T, SipError> with the same SipError type used by all other API functions.
contracts.postcondition: No new error kind variants are introduced for M20 commands — all M20 error conditions are expressed using existing SipErrorKind variants (InvalidState, AccountNotFound, NativeError). Postcondition test: exhaustive match over SipErrorKind compiles with exactly 23 variant arms; adding a hypothetical ConfConnectError variant would fail the discriminant count assertion.
contracts.invariant: No new error kinds for M20 commands — SipErrorKind variant count is invariant at 23. Verified via static assertion in test. Additionally, each M20 error condition maps to a pre-existing variant: (1) conf_port unresolved → InvalidState (same variant used for any invalid operation), (2) account deleted → AccountNotFound (standard lookup failure), (3) PJSIP API error → NativeError (generic FFI error fallback).

tickets.background:
- **Goal**: Implement SipError struct + SipErrorKind enum (23 variants) per RFC §14 N0016, plus M20 RuntimeCommand error converters (N0017) reusing existing variants (no new variants for M20).
- **Purpose**: Uniform type-safe error type across all siprs public API. SipErrorKind classification enables app-level error handling without message parsing. retryable flag guides retry logic. native_status preserves PJSUA diagnostic code for logging/debugging.
- **Motivation**: P0-3 has minimal 3-variant placeholder enum. Without this ticket, callers cannot distinguish transient errors (Timeout=retry recommended) from permanent errors (InvalidConfig=fix config). M20 commands need clear error semantics without enum bloat — no command-specific variants.
- **Constraints**: (1) AccountId/CallId newtypes deferred to P0-7 — use Option<u64> forward-compatible design. (2) PJSUA FFI deferred to P0-6 — pj_status_t uses manually-defined sentinel constants matching PJSIP documentation. (3) Must replace existing SipError enum in src/error.rs — update all downstream callers (config.rs validate(), client.rs SipClient methods). (4) Pure error design — no feature creep beyond error types.
scope: Change 1 — src/error.rs (replace enum → struct): Replace the existing SipError enum (3 variants: InvalidConfig, RuntimeError, Shutdown) with the new SipError struct (6 fields) + SipErrorKind enum (23 variants). Action: replace/refactor. Before: pub enum SipError { InvalidConfig(String), RuntimeError(String), Shutdown }. After: pub struct SipError { pub kind: SipErrorKind, pub message: String, pub native_status: Option<i32>, pub account_id: Option<u64>, pub call_id: Option<u64>, pub retryable: bool } + pub enum SipErrorKind { InvalidConfig, InvalidState, AlreadyInitialized, NotInitialized, AccountNotFound, CallNotFound, TransportInitFailed, RegistrationFailed, AuthenticationFailed, InviteFailed, MediaInitFailed, MediaNegotiationFailed, IceFailed, TlsFailed, SrtpFailed, AudioFormatUnsupported, AudioPipelineBroken, DtmfFailed, Timeout, ChannelClosed, NativeError, ShutdownInProgress, InternalInvariantBroken }. API contract change: existing match arms on SipError::InvalidConfig(..) etc. must be updated.

Change 2 — src/error/error_design_siperror.rs (implement from STUB): Replace pub enum Error {} with SipError struct + constructors (SipError::new(), SipError::invalid_state(), SipError::internal_error(), SipError::with_account_id(), SipError::with_call_id()) and SipErrorKind enum definition. Action: add/implement. Before: pub enum Error {}. After: full SipError definition with convenience constructors, Display impl, Debug impl, From<ReactorError> impl.

Change 3 — src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs (implement from STUB): Replace pub enum Error {} with M20 error converter functions: convert_conf_connect_error(), convert_conf_disconnect_error(), convert_get_account_info_error(). Action: add/implement. Before: pub enum Error {}. After: M20 converter module with public error conversion functions.

Change 4 — src/error/error_design_siperror.rs add convert_pj_status(): Pure function mapping pj_status_t (i32) → Option<SipErrorKind> (None for PJ_SUCCESS, Some variant for errors). Action: add. Before: no conversion. After: convert_pj_status(status: i32) -> Option<SipErrorKind>.

Change 5 — src/config.rs (update validate() return type): ClientConfig::validate() returns SipError::InvalidConfig(msg). After P0-4, this becomes SipError { kind: SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig, message: msg, .. }. Action: modify. Before: return Err(SipError::InvalidConfig(msg)). After: return Err(SipError::new(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig, msg)). No functional change — same behavior.

Change 6 — src/client.rs (update SipClient methods): SipClient methods that return SipError variants match P0-3's SipError::RuntimeError/Shutdown. After P0-4, convert to SipError struct constructors. Action: modify. Before: SipError::RuntimeError(msg). After: SipError::new(SipErrorKind::NativeError, msg) or SipError::new(SipErrorKind::ShutdownInProgress, msg).
No schema change — SipError is not serialized yet (serde feature optional, serde derives added in P1-2).
No config/env change — pure code refactor of error types, no configuration surface.
Dependency: thiserror = "2" is already in Cargo.toml (added by P0-3 STUB annotation in Cargo.toml). No new dependencies required.

Non-change 1 — No new SipErrorKind variants for error types beyond the 23 defined in N0016 (e.g., no ConfConnectError variant for M20). Rationale: M20 commands reuse existing InvalidState/AccountNotFound/NativeError variants. This prevents SipErrorKind from exploding with command-specific variants.

Non-change 2 — No changes to the Backend trait or RuntimeCommand enum. These continue to use ReactorError as before; SipError conversion happens at the facade layer (SipClient). Rationale: runtime internals (reactor, backend) are independent of the public error type.

Impact on P0-2 runtime (reactor.rs): No direct modification needed. RuntimeCommand oneshot replies still use ReactorError. The SipClient facade layer converts from ReactorError to SipError before returning to the caller. Nature: API surface (the SipClient public return types change from Result<_, ReactorError> to Result<_, SipError>). Response: facade methods in client.rs must map ReactorError → SipError via From trait.

Impact on P0-3 config/config.rs (validate()): modify return expression only. Nature: API surface (same error kind/semantics, different struct representation). Response: use SipError::new(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig, msg) instead of SipError::InvalidConfig(msg).

Impact on P0-5 event system (planned): SipEventPayload may include SipError fields for error events. Nature: data format (error type consumed by event system). Response: P0-5 will import SipError/SipErrorKind and use them in event payloads.

Both implement Send + Sync for async API compatibility. retryable flag set per variant: transient errors (AccountNotFound, CallNotFound, Timeout) retryable=true; config/terminal errors (InvalidConfig, ShutdownInProgress, InternalInvariantBroken) retryable=false.
- 【On error】Error conversion functions (convert_pj_status, convert_conf_connect_error, From<ReactorError>) never panic. No uninitialized SipError instances. SipErrorKind always from valid set of 23 variants.

tickets.background:
This ticket implements the complete event system: EventBus with control/raw_sip broadcast channels (N0019), design decisions for loss-tolerant delivery with Lagged detection (N0020), NativeEvent to SipEventPayload conversion for all P0/P1/P2 priority events (N0021), CallState/CallMediaState mapping from pjsip_inv_state and media_status (N0022), RegistrationStateChanged via RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo pattern (N0023), DtmfSent two-phase design with timeout fallback (N0029), and Dual Client PJSIP callback routing with account_id-based EventBus dispatch (N0038).

## Goal
The P0-5 event system provides the complete bridge between PJSIP C callbacks and Rust async event consumers. It defines the SipEventPayload enum (all P0 variants: Registration/Call/DTMF; P1: Transport/ICE; P2: supplemental), the EventBus with split control/raw_sip broadcast channels, the NativeEvent-to-SipEventPayload conversion functions, and the Dual Client routing infrastructure. Every PJSIP callback-generated event is delivered to the correct SipClient's EventBus as a typed SipEvent struct.

## Purpose
SipClient consumers (UI layer, audio pipeline, logging) need observable, structured notifications about SIP state changes. Without this event system, application code would need to poll for state or interpret raw PJSIP callbacks directly. The EventBus provides a decoupled publish-subscribe pattern where:
- Reactor publishes SipEvents onto broadcast channels
- Multiple consumers independently subscribe and filter (via AccountEventReceiver)
- RawSIP messages are isolated on a separate bus to prevent control event loss

This is the primary async communication channel between the synchronous PJSIP thread (C callbacks) and the async Rust world (tokio tasks).

## Motivation
This is the foundational event infrastructure for the entire crate. All observable SIP behavior — registration status changes, call state transitions, DTMF events, media state changes — flows through this system. Every downstream feature (P2-2 error payloads, P2-4 audio pipeline, P4-1 registration state machine) depends on events being delivered. The current stub (src/client.rs uses mpsc::Receiver<()>) blocks all downstream development.

Without this ticket:
- No SipEventPayload type exists (all stubs)
- NativeEvent conversion is unimplemented
- SipClient returns dummy event receiver (cannot observe any SIP events)
- Dual Client mode (multiple SipClient instances) has no event routing

## Constraints
- Broadcast channel (lossy delivery): tokio::sync::broadcast is the only supported channel type. No reliable delivery, no per-subscriber retransmission. This is by design (N0020).
- PJSUA dependency: NativeEvent types mirror PJSIP callback signatures (pjsip_inv_state, pjsua_call_media_status). Any PJSIP version mismatch may require updating the mapping.
- Single Reactor constraint: global_runtime() must remain unchanged. Dual Client uses EventBus dispatch only — no second Reactor.
- All implementation targets are stub files (pub enum State {} / pub trait Service {}). This is net-new implementation, not refactoring of existing code.
- DtmfSent 500ms timeout: This is a fallback for when PJSIP does not fire a send-complete callback. The timeout may race with actual PJSIP callback delivery (firing both DtmfSent events) — consumer must handle duplicates.

Alternative: MockBackend::get_account_info() validates conversion logic without FFI.

Exception: Actual PJSIP callback invocation (on_reg_state2, on_call_state, on_dtmf_digit) cannot be unit-tested — these are C→Rust callbacks triggered by a live PJSIP stack. Reason: FFI callback registration and invocation (not testable without PjsuaBackend from P0-6). This is not an architectural defect — MockBackend simulated NativeEvent injection covers the conversion logic, and integration tests with PjsuaBackend (P0-6+) cover the full callback path. Alternative: MockBackend supplies NativeEvent directly for conversion tests.

Exception: Real-time DTMF timing variance cannot be precisely tested — actual PJSIP callback vs timeout race depends on system scheduling. Reason: The 500ms timeout is a wall-clock timer; actual PJSIP callback may arrive just before or after (not testable deterministically). This is not an architectural defect — tokio::time::pause() provides deterministic simulation for unit tests, and production behavior is verified by integration tests with real PJSIP. Alternative: tokio::time::pause() simulates deterministic timing.

Exception: Dual Client concurrency race condition (simultaneous NativeEvent arrives during client registration/deregistration) — not testable automatically without complex concurrency harness. Reason: Client registration/deregistration is a rare operation; race window is theoretically present but practically zero (not testable in automated unit environment). This is not an architectural defect — the dispatch function is deterministic, and registration/deregistration is serialized through the reactor command queue, eliminating the race in practice. Alternative: Manual stress test in QA phase; unit dispatch tests cover deterministic routing logic.

AccountEventReceiver filters precisely to one account_id
All P0 NativeEvent types convert correctly to SipEventPayload
CallState maps all 5 pjsip_inv_state values without panic
RegistrationStateChanged produces correct Succeeded/Failed events
DtmfSent fires via PJSIP callback or 500ms timeout fallback
Dual Client routes events to correct client EventBus by account_id

[Happy path] A single SipClient is initialized, registers a SIP account, makes a call, and receives the call state transition events (OutgoingCallStarted -> OutgoingCallTrying -> CallConnected) on the AccountEventReceiver subscribed to that account_id. Each event has correct EventMeta (timestamp, event_id, account_id, call_id).

[Error case] A NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged fires for an account where pjsua_acc_get_info() fails (returns error). The EventBus delivers a RegistrationFailed event containing the SipError with details. The client is not left in an indeterminate state — the query API returns the correct registration state.

[Edge case] Two SipClient instances share the same PjsuaBackend (Dual Client mode). An incoming call event for account_id=A is published. Client A's AccountEventReceiver receives CallStateChanged; Client B's AccountEventReceiver (subscribed to account_id=B) must NOT receive the event. account_id=None lifecycle events (ClientInitialized, ClientShutdown) must be received by both clients.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] EventBus::publish() must never block — broadcast::Sender::send() is non-blocking by design. SipEventPayload must be Clone + Debug. EventBus must be Clone (all clones share same Sender). NativeEvent conversion must be total over defined P0 variants.
- [Error invariant] On Lagged(n), the receiver skips n messages and resumes from current position — no crash or state corruption. AccountEventReceiver must not panic on Lagged(n). DtmfSent timeout must not abort ongoing operations.
- [Internal state invariant] EventBus Sender is shared across all Clones. AccountEventReceiver holds its own broadcast Receiver. Reactor owns the EventBus Sender + client_event_buses map. client_event_buses is only mutated by SipClient initialization/shutdown, not by event dispatch.
- [Boundary invariant] EventBus default capacity 2048 must accommodate ~100 concurrent calls (~20 events/call). RawSIP channel capacity must be configured independently. DtmfSent timeout default 500ms must be less than typical PJSIP DTMF duration.

tickets.title: Runtime Infrastructure — Command Serialization and AudioWorkerTask

contracts.precondition: Concurrency model established (P0-2): unbounded MPSC channel created, CoreReactor thread running, RuntimeHandle available
contracts.postcondition: RuntimeCommand enum defined with all 17 variants incl. M20 (ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect) and audio source lifecycle (AddAudioSource, RemoveAudioSource, SetAudioSourceGain, MuteAudioSource). Each variant carries typed oneshot::Sender. DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command maps every variant to a backend execution closure.
contracts.invariant: All PJSUA calls go through MPSC channel — no direct FFI call outside reactor thread. oneshot sender is resolved exactly once per command dispatch.

contracts.precondition: AudioMixer defined with: sources DashMap<u64, Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>>>>, next_source_id AtomicU64, per-source gain map, per-source muted flags
contracts.postcondition: AudioWorkerTask struct defined with spawn() (creates Tokio blocking task), shutdown() (terminates gracefully), and frame processing loop. Source lifecycle API defined as RuntimeCommand variants: add_audio_source (returns source_id), remove_audio_source (removes by id), set_audio_source_gain (updates gain), mute_audio_source (toggles flag).
contracts.invariant: Sources added/removed at frame boundaries — AudioWorker processes pending lifecycle commands between process_frame iterations. source_id monotonically increases. Concurrent add/remove does not corrupt source iteration.

contracts.precondition: AsyncAudioSource trait defined: trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; }
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> per source_id. AudioWorker calls next_chunk on each source during process_frame. MockAsyncAudioSource implements AsyncAudioSource for testing.
contracts.invariant: next_chunk returns 0 for exhausted source without panicking. next_chunk fills buffer partially (returns < buf.len()) for end-of-stream. Implementation is Send + Sync safe.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Complete the runtime infrastructure layer: (1) extend RuntimeCommand to cover all 17 variants including M20 conference commands and audio source lifecycle, (2) define AudioWorkerTask with Tokio blocking-pool frame processing loop, (3) define the AsyncAudioSource trait and minimal AudioMixer with DashMap-backed source management.

### Purpose
The RuntimeCommand enum is the universal command interface that SipClient uses to drive the SIP stack. Every async public API call on SipClient eventually becomes a RuntimeCommand variant submitted via MPSC. The AudioWorkerTask enables per-call audio processing on dedicated Tokio blocking tasks, keeping audio computation off the reactor thread and the async runtime. Source lifecycle (add/remove/gain/mute) becomes a first-class RuntimeCommand capability.

### Motivation
P0-2 established the concurrency model with 11 basic RuntimeCommand variants. P0-4 added the SipError type and M20 error converters. P0-5 added the EventBus and GetAccountInfo variant. To support conference calls (M20 requirement), the ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect variants are needed. To support the audio pipeline (P1+), the source lifecycle model and AudioWorkerTask must be defined now as the foundation.

### Constraints
- Must not break existing RuntimeCommand API (backward-compatible extension).
- AudioMixer uses dashmap::DashMap (not std::sync::Mutex<HashMap>) for lock-free concurrent reads.
- AudioWorkerTask runs on Tokio blocking pool — no tokio::spawn on the reactor thread.
- No real PJSIP FFI calls in this ticket — all backend operations use MockBackend.
- AsyncAudioSource trait uses i16 (PCM S16LE), not f32 (migration is a future concern).

Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource> managed in AudioMixer::sources DashMap
Future slab-based optimization note for >32 sources

Evidence gathered from source code investigation:

1. RuntimeCommand (runtime/command.rs, lines 44-97): 11 existing variants with oneshot::Sender<Result<(), ReactorError>>. Missing: ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect, AddAudioSource, RemoveAudioSource, SetAudioSourceGain, MuteAudioSource. GetAccountInfo exists with typed AccountInfoSnapshot response. All variants use ReactorError, not SipError.

2. DispatchCommand (runtime/command.rs, lines 132-145): 3 internal variants (Execute, GetAccountInfo, Shutdown). ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect would map through Execute. Audio source commands need a new DispatchCommand variant or Execute closure.

3. Backend trait (runtime/backend.rs, lines 16-66): 12 methods. Missing conf_connect(conf_port_id: i32) and conf_disconnect(conf_port_id: i32). MockBackend (lines 71-177) returns canned responses.

4. SipError (error/error_design_siperror.rs): 23 variants. M20 error converters (m20_runtime_command_error.rs) exist for ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect/GetAccountInfo — these convert pj_status to SipErrorKind.

5. audio_worker: No existing implementation. Stub files (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs, audio_subscribe_bp.rs) contain only trait Service {}. AsyncAudioSource trait not defined.

6. Cargo.toml: No dashmap or crossbeam dependency. serde available behind feature flag.

7. command_serialization.rs (concurrency_contexts/): Deprecated stub — marked for removal in P0-6.

8. AudioMixer: Not implemented anywhere. RFC defines sources: DashMap, gain: HashMap, out_queue: SegQueue, in_queue: SegQueue design.

9. N0032 (Section 23 AsyncAudioSource) is a prerequisite for N0034 (Section 24.3 AudioWorkerTask) — must define AsyncAudioSource trait before AudioWorker can use it.

phases.summary:
P0 defines the crate purpose, non-goals, terminology, compliance, versioning policy, functional requirements (normative scope), and module structure.
---

tickets.title: Codec Policy, SRTP, Transport Reconnection & Shutdown Command Routing

contracts.precondition: Codec policy is defined in ClientConfig — either preferred_codecs non-empty (explicit mode) or empty (auto mode). enumerate_codecs() returns available native codecs from PJSIP.
contracts.postcondition: After configure_codecs_auto_mode(), each codec in the system has a priority assigned: Opus=255, PCMU=254, all others=0. When preferred_codecs is non-empty, auto mode is bypassed and no priorities are changed.
contracts.invariant: Opus always receives priority 255 in auto mode; PCMU always receives priority 254. These values are immutable constants. The priority assignment is a pure function of codec_id alone (no state dependence).

contracts.precondition: Transport configuration is defined (TransportConfig enum with UDP/TCP/TLS variants). SrtpPolicy has one of three values (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory).
contracts.postcondition: SrtpPolicy::validate() returns Ok(()) when: (a) policy is Disabled (feature state irrelevant), or (b) policy is Mandatory/Optional AND srtp feature flag is enabled. Returns Err(InvalidConfig) when Mandatory/Optional AND feature flag is disabled.
contracts.invariant: SrtpPolicy Disabled is universally valid. Mandatory and Optional are gated by #[cfg(feature = "srtp")] — at the API level, the validate function receives a bool feature_enabled flag that enforces this gate.

contracts.precondition: Reactor shutdown sequence has started (is_shutting_down == true). A RuntimeCommand is submitted to the reactor for dispatch.
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownCommandRouter::classify() returns Permit for GetAccountInfo (command is forwarded to execute_get_account_info). Returns Reject(InvalidState) with message containing 'shutting down' for ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect. Returns Reject(InvalidState) for all other commands.
contracts.invariant: GetAccountInfo is always Permitted during shutdown. ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are always Rejected during shutdown. This classification is invariant per variant — no state or context changes the routing decision during shutdown.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Implement three independent policy modules within the siprs media/lifecycle layer: (1) two-layer codec selection (explicit vs auto mode) that assigns Opus=255, PCMU=254 when preferred_codecs is empty, (2) SRTP policy with feature-flag gating (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory), and (3) M20 shutdown command routing that permits GetAccountInfo while rejecting ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect during shutdown. Each module is a standalone, testable unit that integrates with existing configuration and reactor infrastructure.

### Purpose
These policies form the core control layer for media configuration and lifecycle management in the M20 extension. Without them: (a) codecs default to PJSIP's built-in ordering instead of Opus-first prioritization, (b) SRTP cannot be controlled via config (always enabled or always disabled), and (c) shutdown behavior for M20 commands is undefined (the reactor would attempt to dispatch media operations during teardown, causing undefined PJSIP behavior). Each policy closes a gap between raw PJSIP capability and intentional application-level control.

### Motivation
P1-1 is the first M20-spec ticket after the P0 infrastructure (P0-1 through P0-6) established the crate foundation. The three nodes (N0041, N0042, N0044) were identified as highest-priority M20 additions because: codec auto-mode is required for every call session, SRTP policy directly affects security posture and cannot default to Mandatory without feature-gating, and shutdown routing prevents reactor crashes during teardown. These are preconditions for P1-2 (Security & Platform) and P1-3 (Audio Pipeline).

### Constraints
1. No FFI dependency: configure_codecs_auto_mode must produce a priority map (pure function) rather than calling pjsua_codec_set_priority directly — the FFI binding is deferred to P2-4. 2. SrtpPolicy validate receives a bool feature_enabled flag rather than using #[cfg(feature = "srtp")] directly in the function body, enabling testability without conditional compilation. 3. ShutdownCommandRouter::classify must be a pure function — no reactor state access, no async, no side effects. 4. No new dependencies beyond the existing crate's Cargo.toml (no random crate for jitter — use deterministic seed based on attempt number).
