tickets.invariants: 【C053】Each example exercises a defined layer of the test strategy — examples are the Layer 5 API documentation surface and their flows are re-run as integration tests. 【C056】Example main functions return Result and never panic on error paths; errors propagate to the top level with a user-facing message. 【C066】The example flows mirror the public API structure so tests/ example-driven integration tests stay aligned with the API. 【CLI determinism】Every example accepts the same style of positional/flag args and produces the same usage message when args are invalid, so behavior is scriptable.
tickets.investigation: All five examples currently compile (behind the `spec-examples` feature per Cargo.toml lines 94-112) but perform no real work. examples/account_register.rs:11-26 — builds ClientConfig, calls SipClient::new, constructs an unused `_account_config`, and immediately client.shutdown(); no register() call, no CLI args. examples/client_init.rs:11-19 — same pattern, no transports/STUN config. examples/make_call.rs:11-27 — builds an unused `_request: OutgoingCallRequest` and shuts down; no dial, no event loop. examples/audio_tap.rs:11-20 — uses MockAsyncAudioSource directly instead of subscribe_audio; no call. examples/tts_source.rs:13-21 — only a compile-time `_assert_tts_source::<MockAsyncAudioSource>()`; no real source injection. Cargo.toml:13 `autoexamples = false` and the [[example]] required-features gates (lines 94-112) keep them out of the default build. RFC §41 (41.1-41.5) specifies the exact flows each example must implement. A real implementation must add CLI arg parsing, drive the named SipClient operation, replace the mock with the real flow, and cover the flows with Layer 5 integration tests (C066).
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Each example main reads as a runnable walkthrough: parse_args() → build config → SipClient::new → perform operation → shutdown. Split the body into verb-phrase helper functions (parse_args, connect_client, run_call_flow).
- Remove the unused placeholder locals (_account_config, _request) — the real flow uses them.
- The unused `_assert_tts_source` compile-time function in tts_source.rs is replaced by a real TtsStreamSource struct with a named type, making the example translatable.
- CLI arg parsing is extracted into a small shared helper (e.g. examples/common/cli.rs) so all five examples share one arg convention instead of five divergent parsers.
tickets.instrumentation:
- Each example logs its lifecycle at info level with tracing (client initialized, account registering, call ringing/connected, tap frame count) so users can follow the flow.
- On failure, examples print the error to stderr and exit non-zero; tracing::error! records call_id/uri context.
- make_call prints the observed SipEventPayload variants (ringing/connected/rejected) so the event flow is visible to the user.

tickets.title: Add cpal as an optional dependency behind the cpal-input feature and implement device-backed capture returning Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError> with an integration test

contracts.precondition: cpal is an optional dependency reachable only through the `cpal-input` feature (default build graph contains no cpal). The RFC §40 signature exists behind #[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")]: `pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>`. The input `format` is a validated AudioFormat (AudioFormat::new succeeded; sample_rate ∈ {Hz8000, Hz16000, Hz24000, Hz48000}, bit_depth ∈ {I16, F32}, channel_layout ∈ {Mono, StereoInOut}, frame_ms ∈ {10, 20, 40, 60}).
contracts.postcondition: When a default input device exists and its native sample format is convertible to the i16 pipeline contract, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) whose next_chunk fills the caller's &mut [i16] buffer with captured PCM and returns the written sample count. Device-open, format-mismatch, build-stream, and play failures surface as Err(SipError) (SipErrorKind::NativeError for device/stream errors; SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats) — never a panic.
contracts.invariant: The returned source is AsyncAudioSource + Send and can be stored as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> in AudioMixer (ErasedAudioSource auto-derived via blanket impl). Sample conversion clamps into the valid i16 range (no wraparound). With `cpal-input` disabled, the function, the CpalMicrophoneSource type, and the cpal crate are compiled out of the build.

contracts.precondition: Audio subscribe uses sources — AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>; AsyncAudioSource trait is defined as #[async_trait::async_trait] pub trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; }.
contracts.postcondition: ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derived for all T: AsyncAudioSource + Send; SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> provided for synchronous sources; any new concrete source (e.g. CpalMicrophoneSource) implementing AsyncAudioSource + Send automatically gains ErasedAudioSource.
contracts.invariant: ErasedAudioSource auto-derived for every AsyncAudioSource implementor — blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T must compile. SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send. CpalMicrophoneSource must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send so it is usable as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Replace the P8-4 placeholder body of `open_default_microphone_source` (src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:167-176) with real cpal device capture by adding cpal as an optional dependency behind the `cpal-input` feature, so the RFC §40 API returns `Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` backed by the platform default microphone, plus a feature-gated integration test.

### Purpose
The `cpal-input` feature has been declared empty (Cargo.toml:27) since P1-3, and the microphone source is the only RFC-required audio source that is not device-backed. Downstream consumers (AudioMixer via P5-2, the audio_tap example via P8-6, AI TTS source insertion) rely on opening the default microphone as an AsyncAudioSource; without this ticket the function is a stub that always returns a typed error.

### Motivation
P8-4 delivered the AsyncAudioSource adapter machinery (ErasedAudioSource/SyncAudioSource/SyncSourceAdapter) under a no-new-dependencies constraint, deferring the cpal dependency and leaving the `[::STUB::] P8-7` marker. This ticket removes that deferral: the adapter types are stable, the feature gate exists, and the remaining work is wiring cpal in and resolving the marker.

### Constraints
- cpal must be an optional dependency reachable only via `cpal-input`; default builds must not pull the cpal crate (feature-additive invariant). Cargo.toml:40 already declares `check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("cpal-input"))']`.
- MSRV is 1.95; pin a cpal version whose API is stable and documented. cpal 0.15/0.16/0.18 differ — v0.18 requires an explicit `stream.play()` after build and pins the sample rate/config explicitly.
- The public `open_default_microphone_source` signature must not change (C051 precondition); the returned source must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send.
- No panics on device failure — all errors map to SipError (NativeError for device/stream, AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats).
- CI without audio hardware must not run the device integration test by default (#[ignore]).
scope:
**Scope of changes:**
- [File/module path] Cargo.toml — [dependencies] + [features] sections
- [Action] MODIFY (add optional dependency + rewire feature)
- [What specifically changes] Add `cpal = { version = "0.18", optional = true }` to [dependencies]; change `cpal-input = []` to `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`; update the `[::STUB::] P1-3 (N0050)` comment that says 'Full implementation requires the cpal crate (P8-4)'.
- [Before → After] Before: `cpal-input = []` (empty feature, no cpal). After: `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]` (feature pulls cpal; default build unchanged).
- [File/module path] src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — open_default_microphone_source + new CpalMicrophoneSource
- [Action] MODIFY + ADD (replace placeholder body; add source type behind #[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")])
- [What specifically changes] Replace `let _ = format; Err(SipError::new(SipErrorKind::NativeError, "cpal microphone source not yet integrated (P8-4)"))` with `CpalMicrophoneSource::new(format).map(|source| Box::new(source) as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>)`. Add `CpalMicrophoneSource { stream: cpal::Stream, samples: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<i16>>> }` with `new(format) -> Result<Self, SipError>` (default_host → default_input_device → default_input_config → per-format build_input_stream → play), `#[cfg(test)] from_queue(SampleQueue)`, and `#[async_trait::async_trait] impl AsyncAudioSource for CpalMicrophoneSource`. Add pure helpers: `SampleQueue` (push_i16/drain_to), `convert_f32_sample_to_i16`, `convert_u16_sample_to_i16`, and error-mapping helpers (map_default_config_error/map_build_stream_error/map_play_error).
- [API contract change] None breaking — the public signature `pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` is unchanged (C051 precondition); behavior changes from always-Err to real capture.
- [Data schema change] None — no serialized data format changes.
- [Config/env change] None — no env vars required; the integration test may honor SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1 to force device tests on capable hosts.
- [Dependency added] `cpal` (optional, behind `cpal-input`) — the only new crate.

**Out of scope:**
- [Excluded item] AudioMixer auto-wiring of the microphone and real PJSIP media conf-port bridging (P3-2 N0050)
- [Why excluded] Mixer integration already accepts any AsyncAudioSource (P5-2); conf-port wiring is a separate PJSIP-media ticket; this ticket resolves only the device-source adapter and its feature gate.
- [Excluded item] Sample-rate resampling inside the adapter
- [Why excluded] Converting the device's native rate to an arbitrary requested rate belongs to model::audio_resampler; this adapter uses the device's default config when the requested format is not natively supported.

**Affected areas:**
- [Affected component] src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs, Cargo.toml, tests/ (new verify_spec_p8_7.rs), Cargo.lock
- [Nature of impact] Additive optional dependency; default builds pull no cpal crate; the `cpal-input` feature becomes real (was empty).
- [Corresponding change needed] Y — CI jobs that enable `cpal-input` need audio device access or must rely on the #[ignore] device test; `make test` (default) runs the feature-off build.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] C051-Pre: RFC §40 signature — `#[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")] pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` must exist with the exact arity/return type. Already implemented as `open_default_microphone_source_has_correct_signature` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:429): the generic future-bound `assert_microphone_future<F: Future<Output = Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>>>` fails to compile if the output type drifts; the future is dropped unpolled so no device access occurs.

UT: [Normal] C051-Post: SampleQueue::drain_to fills an i16 buffer with queued PCM in FIFO order and returns the exact written count — construct SampleQueue::new(), push [100i16, 200i16, 300i16], drain into a [0i16; 4] buffer, assert written == 3 and buf[0..3] == [100, 200, 300].

UT: [Normal] C051-Post: CpalMicrophoneSource::next_chunk delegates to the shared SampleQueue — use the #[cfg(test)] constructor CpalMicrophoneSource::from_queue(SampleQueue) (bypasses the real cpal::Stream), push 4 synthetic samples, call AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk(&mut src, &mut buf), assert written == 4 and buf == the pushed samples.

UT: [Normal] C051-Post: ErasedAudioSource auto-derivation for the concrete source — a `Box<dyn ErasedAudioSource>` is constructible from CpalMicrophoneSource::from_queue(...) (blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T compiles) and next_chunk delegates correctly.

UT: [Error] C051-Post: SampleQueue::drain_to on an empty queue returns 0 without panicking — end-of-stream per the AsyncAudioSource contract (next_chunk returning 0 signals exhaustion); drain a fresh empty queue into a [0i16; 4] buffer and assert 0.

UT: [Error] C051-Post: sample conversion clamp — convert_f32_sample_to_i16(1.0) == i16::MAX, convert_f32_sample_to_i16(-1.0) == i16::MIN, convert_f32_sample_to_i16(0.0) == 0, and out-of-range values (2.0 / -2.0) clamp to i16::MAX / i16::MIN, never wrap.

UT: [Error] C051-Post: unsupported sample-format mapping — the per-format stream builder returns Err(SipError::new(SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported, ...)) for a sample format outside the convertible set (I16/F32/U16) rather than panicking; the pure error-mapping helper is unit-tested directly.

UT: [Boundary] C051-Post: convert_u16_sample_to_i16 boundary — u16::MAX -> i16::MAX, 0 -> i16::MIN, 0x8000 (midpoint) -> 0, and 1 -> -32767 (linear DC-offset-preserving mapping, exact at the extremes).

UT: [Boundary] C051-Post: zero-length buffer — CpalMicrophoneSource::next_chunk with a `&mut [i16; 0]` returns 0 without panicking (AsyncAudioSource contract: fewer samples signals partial availability; a zero buffer is valid).

UT: [Invariant] C051-Inv: Send bound — CpalMicrophoneSource (and Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>) is Send; assert_send::<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>>() and assert_send::<CpalMicrophoneSource>() compile, so the source can live inside AudioMixer's DashMap as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal condition】With `cpal-input` enabled and a default input device present, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) and next_chunk fills the i16 buffer with device PCM. The cpal crate compiles only under the feature (Cargo.toml: cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]).

- 【Internal state invariant】CpalMicrophoneSource holds a cpal::Stream plus an Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<i16>>> sample queue; the queue grows only from the cpal callback thread and shrinks only via next_chunk; next_chunk returns 0 when the queue is empty (end-of-stream).
- 【Boundary invariant】Sample conversion is bijective at the extremes and clamped in between: u16::MAX↔i16::MAX, 0↔i16::MIN, 0x8000↔0; f32 in [-1.0, 1.0] maps linearly with clamping. A zero-length buffer returns 0 without panicking; a 65536-sample buffer (AudioMixer boundary) drains without overflow.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】AudioTapMode is defined with exactly the Realtime and Lossless variants; Default == AudioTapMode::Realtime (RFC §22.1).
【Happy path】AudioTapHandle wraps a tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<AudioChunkPair> and `recv()` returns Option<AudioChunkPair>, yielding None when the sender closes.

【Happy path】The subscribe_audio entry point exists with the RFC §22 signature: subscribe_audio(call_id: CallId, format: AudioFormat, capacity: usize, mode: AudioTapMode) -> Result<AudioTapHandle, SipError>.

【Happy path】In Realtime mode, when the channel is full the oldest pair is dropped and the newest pair is preferred (oldest-drop), reporting an AudioTapOverflow condition — the audio pipeline is not blocked.
【Happy path】In Lossless mode, when the channel is full the producer side applies backpressure (blocks instead of dropping) so no pair is lost.
【Error case】subscribe_audio for an unknown call_id returns Err(SipError::not_found(...)) and does not create a handle.
【Edge case】capacity == 0 is rejected with Err(SipError) since a zero-capacity channel cannot carry a pair.
【Invariant】AudioTapMode is Clone + Copy + Debug + PartialEq + Eq; AudioTapHandle is Send and not Clone (a single consumer per tap).

tickets.invariants: 【C032】The Audio Subscribe API is available with a backpressure policy: Realtime is the default and never blocks the audio pipeline (oldest-drop + AudioTapOverflow report); Lossless is best-effort integrity that backpressures the producer and may induce jitter if the consumer is slow (RFC §22.1). 【C033】The tap consumes AudioChunkPair frames produced by AsyncAudioSource-driven media; the handle's receiver is single-consumer. 【Error handling】subscribe_audio never panics — unknown call_id and capacity == 0 return Err(SipError).
tickets.investigation: src/api/audio_subscribe_bp.rs — the file is a design-artifact shell: line 20 declares `pub trait Service {}` (unused placeholder) and line 23 carries the `[::STUB::]` marker. No AudioTapMode, AudioTapHandle, or subscribe_audio entry point exists anywhere in src/. The RFC §22 spec (lines 1368-1517) defines: AudioTapMode { Realtime (default), Lossless }, AudioTapHandle { rx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<AudioChunkPair> } with `recv() -> Option<AudioChunkPair>`, and `SipClient::subscribe_audio(call_id, format, capacity, mode) -> Result<AudioTapHandle, SipError>`. §22.1 specifies the backpressure policy: Realtime = oldest-drop + MediaError(AudioTapOverflow) with no pipeline impact; Lossless = producer-side backpressure in AudioWorkerTask with a best-effort integrity caveat. AudioChunkPair already exists in src/model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs (re-exported at lib.rs:106-111). A real implementation must define the enum + handle in this file and provide the subscribe_audio entry point (which may delegate to the SipClient/reactor once the backend exists).

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】RawSipMessage has the RFC §16 fields: direction, transport, start_line, headers: Vec<(String, String)>, body: Option<Vec<u8>>, text, content_length: usize, remote_addr/local_addr: Option<SocketAddr>.

【Happy path】RawSipMessage::parse(bytes) parses a raw SIP message into the typed fields: request/response line → start_line + direction, header block → headers, CRLF-CRLF body → body (Some when present), content_length derived from the Content-Length header.

【Happy path】Parsed-field accessors exist: start_line(), header(name) -> Option<&str> (case-insensitive), headers(), body() -> Option<&[u8]>, text() -> &str, content_length(), direction(), transport(), remote_addr()/local_addr().
【Happy path】redact_authorization() still replaces password values in Authorization (and Proxy-Authorization) headers when enabled, returning a new message (immutable pattern).
【Error case】Parsing a non-SIP / malformed byte sequence returns Err(SipError) instead of panicking.
【Edge case】A message with no body yields body: None and content_length: 0; an empty header block yields headers: vec![].
【Edge case】A message whose Content-Length header is absent but has a body yields body: Some(...) with content_length derived from the actual body bytes (best-effort).
【Invariant】RawSipMessage implements Clone + Debug; the `data` field is no longer public — bytes are only reachable through the parsed fields.

This work item resolves the markers by implementing real account info retrieval: convert_get_account_info_error returns a real AccountInfo on success, the backend's get_account_info derives data from the account state, and SipAccountHandle::registration_state() queries the reactor instead of unconditionally returning RegistrationState::Idle.

tickets.background: Source ticket P3-2 (PJSIP FFI Layer, Runtime State & AudioMixer Architecture) defined the CallEntry state machine (C027) and ClientState with a calls map keyed by CallId (C046). SipAccountHandle::make_call was left returning a hardcoded Ok(1) because the MakeCall reply did not yet carry the assigned CallId. This work item resolves the marker by threading the real CallId assigned by the backend reactor through the MakeCall reply and returning it from make_call().
scope: src/api/public_api_design.rs (make_call — await the MakeCall reply and return the real CallId instead of Ok(1))
src/runtime/command.rs (RuntimeCommand::MakeCall reply type Result<(), ReactorError> → Result<u64, ReactorError>; dispatch carries the id back)

Out of scope: pjsua_call_make_call FFI call (P8-20 / P4+); CallId NonZeroU64 newtype migration (P4-1).
Impact: make_call() now returns the CallId that call_state(), Hangup, and Hold must use, removing the fabricated id 1.

UT: [C027] make_call with a mock reactor replying Err(...) returns Err(SipError) with SipErrorKind::InviteFailed.

UT: [C046] The returned CallId equals the CallEntry.id present in the reactor ClientState.
UT: [Error] A dropped reply channel makes make_call return an Err mapped from the oneshot recv error.
testIntegration: IT: [Reactor round-trip] Submit MakeCall, capture the returned CallId, then call_state() contains a CallEntry with that id.
IT: [Disconnect] Hangup using the returned CallId succeeds against the reactor.
testExceptions: The real pjsua_call_make_call id assignment cannot be tested without live PJSIP linkage; MockBackend supplies deterministic incrementing ids.
CallId remains u64 in the public API — the NonZeroU64 newtype (C013 / P4-1) migration is out of scope.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】make_call() awaits the MakeCall reply and returns the CallId assigned by the backend reactor — the hardcoded Ok(1) at src/api/public_api_design.rs:142 is removed.
【Happy path】The returned CallId matches the CallEntry.id recorded in ClientState.calls (C046), so subsequent Hangup/Hold operate on a valid id.
【Error case】When the reactor replies Err(ReactorError), make_call() maps it to a SipError (e.g. SipErrorKind::InviteFailed) and does not fabricate a CallId.
【Error case】When the reply channel is dropped before sending, make_call() surfaces an error (oneshot recv failure) instead of returning a hardcoded value.
【Edge case】Backend-assigned CallIds are unique across consecutive MakeCall commands — no two calls share the same returned id.
The MakeCall reply is sent exactly once, preserving the RuntimeCommand reply discipline.

tickets.investigation: src/api/public_api_design.rs:123-144 — make_call validates CallMediaConstraints, submits RuntimeCommand::MakeCall with a oneshot channel, but discards `_rx` and returns Ok(1). src/runtime/command.rs:60-68 and 296-302 — RuntimeCommand::MakeCall reply is oneshot::Sender<Result<(), ReactorError>> and the DispatchCommand::Execute closure calls backend.make_call(account_id as i32, &request)? then returns Ok(()), discarding the returned tuple. src/runtime/backend.rs:46-52 — SipBackend::make_call already returns Result<(i32, CallEntry), ReactorError>, and the MockBackend impl at backend.rs:181-193 returns Ok((1, entry)) with a hardcoded native_call_id=1. contracts.postcondition: Public API designed around RuntimeCommand pattern
contracts.invariant: API is Send+Sync

tickets.background: Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) defined AccountConfig and its validation rules (C015/C052). SipAccountHandle::update_config was left as a no-op because no incremental update path existed. This work item resolves the marker by introducing an AccountConfigPatch type and a RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount variant so account configuration can be changed at runtime and dispatched through the reactor.
scope: src/api/public_api_design.rs (update_config — accept AccountConfigPatch, submit RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount, await the reply)
src/runtime/command.rs (add RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount variant and dispatch to SipBackend::update_account)
src/runtime/backend.rs (SipBackend::update_account trait method; MockBackend impl)
src/runtime/state.rs (ClientState AccountEntry config update on success)
src/config/account_config_spec.rs (AccountConfigPatch type definition)
Out of scope: full AccountConfig schema migration; pjsua_acc_modify FFI call (P8-20 / P4+).
Impact: update_config is no longer a silent no-op; patches are validated and applied via the reactor.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] AccountConfigPatch construction, field access, and Default (no-op) derive.
UT: [C015] update_config with an invalid patch returns Err(SipError) before dispatch.
UT: [Normal] update_config submits UpdateAccount and returns Ok(()) on a successful mock reactor reply.
UT: [Error] update_config maps a reactor Err to a SipError (e.g. ConfigError).
UT: [Boundary] Applying a no-op patch leaves the ClientState account entry unchanged.
testIntegration: IT: [Reactor round-trip] update_config(patch) followed by accounts()/QueryState reflects the patched config in ClientState.
IT: [Dispatch] RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount is serialized FIFO with other commands through the reactor channel.
testExceptions: The actual PJSUA account modification (pjsua_acc_modify) cannot be tested without live PJSIP linkage; the patch type, validation, and reactor dispatch are fully unit-testable.
The exact set of runtime-mutable fields is a product decision — the patch must only expose fields the backend can actually change.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】update_config(patch) submits RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount and returns Ok(()) when the reactor applies the patch.
【Happy path】An AccountConfigPatch type exists exposing a runtime-mutable subset of AccountConfig (e.g. register_on_start, transport policy, codec policy), Send+Sync and Default (no-op patch).
【Error case】A patch that fails AccountConfig validation (C015/C052) returns Err(SipError) before dispatch — fail-fast.
【Error case】A reactor Err from UpdateAccount maps to a SipError (e.g. ConfigError) instead of silently succeeding.
【Edge case】An empty/no-op patch is accepted and returns Ok(()) without modifying reactor state.
The applied patch is reflected in the reactor ClientState account entry (subsequent accounts()/QueryState reflects it).
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P5-2 (depends on: AudioMixer uses audio format types), P2-3 (depends on: event system uses AudioChunk), P7 (depends on: audio subscribe uses AudioChunkPair)
tickets.notes: Stub: src/api/public_api_design.rs:148. Adding a RuntimeCommand variant is a public command-enum change — update every match in src/runtime/command.rs (name(), to_dispatch, Debug) and any exhaustive matches elsewhere. Related: P3-1 (AccountConfig/validation), P4-2 (codec policy subset), P7 (config-change events).
tickets.invariants: C012 — API is Send+Sync. C015 — Validation rules enforced. C052 — All validation rules enumerated. New: update_config never silently drops a patch — a non-Ok reply is surfaced as an error.
tickets.instrumentation: log::trace! on update_config dispatch with the changed field set. log::warn! on patch validation failure.
tickets.investigation: src/api/public_api_design.rs:146-152 — update_config(&self, _patch: AccountConfig) -> Result<(), SipError> is a no-op that discards the patch and returns Ok(()). src/runtime/command.rs — RuntimeCommand has AddAccount/RemoveAccount/SetRegistration but no UpdateAccount variant; a new variant must be added and matched in name(), to_dispatch, and Debug (command.rs ~154-190). src/runtime/backend.rs — the SipBackend trait has add_account/remove_account but no update_account method. src/config/account_config_spec.rs:151 — AccountConfig is the full config; a runtime-mutable subset must be defined separately as AccountConfigPatch. Real implementation: define AccountConfigPatch, add RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount { account_id, patch, reply }, add SipBackend::update_account, update the ClientState AccountEntry on success, and make update_config dispatch + await the reply.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Replace the discard-pattern `_patch` parameter with a real typed patch. Reuse AccountConfig::validate rules (C015/C052) for the mutable subset so patch validation cannot diverge. Keep the RuntimeCommand match arms exhaustive when adding the new variant.

tickets.title: Implement startup account restoration by loading accounts via db.load_accounts() and calling sip_client.add_account() for each

contracts.precondition: ClientConfig defined
contracts.postcondition: AccountConfig specified with validation
contracts.invariant: Validation rules enforced

contracts.precondition: Standalone server mode (N0061) is configured and running; Axum router is built with shared AppState
contracts.postcondition: HTTP/WS protocol defines 18 REST API endpoints, 2 WebSocket endpoints (control+audio, audio-only), JSON text frame format (type/seq/payload), and binary audio frame format (AudioFrameHeader + PCM data). Axum router registers all routes.
contracts.invariant: Event-audio correlation via sequence numbers: SipEvent.meta.seq and AudioChunkPair.first_seq/last_seq share the same monotonically increasing global counter domain. A consumer can correlate seq=N event with first_seq=N audio chunk.

contracts.precondition: Standalone server mode (N0061) is configured; SQLite database path is specified in config
contracts.postcondition: SQLite schema with 4 tables (accounts, transport_configs, client_settings, tls_configs) is created at startup. SeaORM migration files are generated. Makefile targets for migration management (gen-migration, migrate-up, migrate-fresh, gen-entities) are available.
contracts.invariant: rusqlite bundled feature ensures SQLite builds without system library dependency. DatabasePool uses single connection (SQLite file-locked for writes) with busy timeout to avoid database is locked errors.

tickets.background: Source ticket P4-3 (Shutdown, Media Bridge, HTTP/WS Protocol & SQLite Schema) defined the SQLite accounts table and the standalone server mode (C065/C063). run_server() opens the DatabasePool but never restores persisted accounts, so saved accounts are not re-registered on startup. This work item resolves the marker by adding DatabasePool::load_accounts() and replaying each saved account through sip_client.add_account() at server startup.
scope: src/api/standalone_server_config.rs (run_server — load accounts from the pool and add each to sip_client before serving)
src/model/sqlite_schema.rs (DatabasePool::load_accounts() — query the accounts table into AccountEntity values)
src/client.rs (SipClient::add_account public method wrapping RuntimeCommand::AddAccount, if not already present)
src/runtime/command.rs (AddAccount dispatch — verify the reply path and account id)
Out of scope: the account persist/save path; full AccountEntity ↔ AccountConfig bijection beyond the read direction.
Impact: restarting the server re-registers all accounts saved in a previous run; feature-gated behind sqlite-storage.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] DatabasePool::load_accounts() on a temp DB returns the inserted AccountEntity rows.
UT: [Boundary] load_accounts() on an empty accounts table returns an empty Vec.
UT: [Error] load_accounts() propagates a DB error (e.g. missing table) as Err.
UT: [Normal] AccountEntity → AccountConfig mapping for the fields consumed by add_account.
UT: [Normal] The restoration loop calls add_account exactly once per loaded account (mock sip_client).
testIntegration: IT: [Server startup] Insert accounts into a temp DB, run the run_server restoration step, and verify sip_client.accounts() contains the restored accounts.
IT: [Fresh DB] run_server with an empty DB starts successfully with zero restored accounts.
testExceptions: Full registration against a live SIP registrar requires a network registrar and is not a unit-test concern. The restoration step (load + add_account) is testable with a temp SQLite DB and MockBackend.
The exact AccountEntity ↔ AccountConfig bijection depends on the persist path (out of scope); load_accounts only needs the read direction.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】run_server (sqlite-storage enabled) calls db.load_accounts() and calls sip_client.add_account() for each saved account before binding the listener.
【Happy path】DatabasePool::load_accounts() returns the rows of the accounts table as AccountEntity values; an empty table yields an empty Vec.
【Error case】A DB error from load_accounts() surfaces as a startup SipError rather than silently starting with no accounts.
【Edge case】A fresh/empty accounts table starts the server with zero accounts and no error.

【Edge case】Each AccountEntity maps to an AccountConfig (username, domain, transport, register_on_start, display_name) so the restored account is equivalent to the persisted one; an account that fails add_account is logged and skipped rather than aborting startup.
No account restoration occurs when the sqlite-storage feature is disabled.

tickets.background: Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) specified the codec policy but left runtime enumeration deferred. The marker at src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69 was left as a stub because the FFI-defined pjsua_codec_info types are not generated until bindgen runs under the pjsua-native feature. This work item resolves it by replacing the placeholder codec list and Codec type with runtime codec enumeration via the PJSIP codec API.
scope: - src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69,187 — replace the available_codecs: Vec<Codec> placeholder and the Codec struct with FFI-backed enumeration
- src/ffi/bindings.rs — consume the bindgen-generated pjsua_codec_info type once pjsua-native is enabled
- src/ffi/mod.rs — expose the codec-enumeration FFI surface (pjsua_enum_codecs path)
- Out of scope: PairAligner/resampler pipeline (C036/C037); codec policy/negotiation internals (C041/C042) beyond what enumeration feeds.
- Impact: ClientCapabilities.available_codecs, ClientCapabilities.opus_available, and every caller reading codec capability.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] maps a pjsua_codec_info fixture (id="opus", clock_rate=48000) to Codec { id, name, clock_rate }
UT: [Normal] opus_available is true when the enumerated list contains "opus" and false otherwise
UT: [Boundary] an empty enumeration yields an empty available_codecs and opus_available=false
UT: [Error] an enumeration FFI error returns an empty list with a logged diagnostic and no panic
testIntegration: IT: With pjsua-native enabled, ClientCapabilities::new() reflects the real codec set; with it disabled, available_codecs is empty.
testExceptions: Real codec enumeration requires a linked PJSIP library (pjsua_enum_codecs), so unit tests use a fixed pjsua_codec_info fixture — the live call is environment-dependent. Only the three Codec fields (id, name, clock_rate) are modelled and asserted; other pjsua_codec_info fields are out of scope.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】ClientCapabilities.available_codecs is populated from a real pjsua codec enumeration when pjsua-native is enabled, mapping each pjsua_codec_info entry to Codec { id, name, clock_rate }.
【Happy path】ClientCapabilities.opus_available reflects whether the enumerated codecs contain "opus".
【Error case】When enumeration fails (no PJSIP link, FFI error), available_codecs degrades to an empty list rather than panicking, and the failure is logged.
【Edge case】A one-to-one mapping test converts a fixed pjsua_codec_info fixture (id, name, clock_rate) to Codec.
【Edge case】Without pjsua-native, the fallback path still yields an empty available_codecs and the crate compiles without PJSIP.

tickets.notes: Stub sites: src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69,187. Depends on P8-5 (bindgen generates pjsua_codec_info) and P8-16 (pjsua-native feature flag). Implementation: (1) add Codec::from_pjsua_codec_info; (2) add the FFI codec-enumeration function under pjsua-native; (3) call it when populating ClientCapabilities; (4) keep the empty-list fallback for the non-feature path. Related: P8-18 (PJSIP constants).
tickets.invariants: Codec auto mode must assign Opus=255 and PCMU=254 invariantly (C042). Codec policy only accepts PCMU and Opus (C041) — enumeration may report more codecs, but policy filtering still restricts to PCMU/Opus. Every enumerated Codec has a non-empty id and clock_rate > 0. available_codecs is derived from enumeration, never hand-maintained — no hardcoded codec list remains.
tickets.instrumentation: Add tracing::info! on enumeration success with the codec count, and tracing::warn! on enumeration failure. Consider a 'codecs.enumerated' counter metric.
tickets.investigation: src/config/observability_metrics.rs declares ClientCapabilities.available_codecs: Vec<Codec> at line 69, ClientCapabilities::new() initializes it to Vec::new(), and the Codec struct at lines 187-196 is { id: String, name: String, clock_rate: u32 } — a pure placeholder with no FFI backing (the marker covers :69 and :187). ffi/bindings.rs currently provides only stub type aliases (pjsua_acc_id = i32, pjsua_call_id = i32, pjsua_conf_port_id = i32, pjsua_transport_id = i32) and a minimal pjsua_call_info mirror — there is no pjsua_codec_info yet (that arrives with the P8-5 bindgen work). A real implementation must add a codec-enumeration FFI surface (pjsua_enum_codecs / pjsua_codec_info), map each entry into Codec, populate available_codecs and opus_available, and keep the non-pjsua-native path compiling with an empty list.

Implementation: (1) expose the bindgen constants from ffi::bindings under pjsua-native; (2) replace the local consts with ffi::bindings references; (3) keep stub aliases for the non-feature path; (4) keep the mapping tests green. Related: P8-17 (codec enumeration), P8-20 (FFI call sites).
tickets.invariants: No PJSIP/PJSUA numeric constant is hand-coded in src/error or src/state — every value comes from ffi::bindings (bindgen under pjsua-native, stub aliases otherwise). Codec auto mode must assign Opus=255 and PCMU=254 invariantly (C042). Codec policy only accepts PCMU and Opus (C041).
tickets.instrumentation: No new runtime metrics required. Add a compile-time assertion that the mapping functions still compile when the constant source switches to bindgen.
tickets.investigation: Three files hand-code PJSUA constants. error_design_siperror.rs:32 defines const PJ_SUCCESS: i32 = 0, PJ_ENOMEM: i32 = -2, PJ_EINVALIDOP: i32 = 150002, PJ_EBUSY, consumed by convert_pj_status (lines 300-306). m20_runtime_command_error.rs:32 defines PJ_SUCCESS = 0 and PJ_EINVALIDOP = 150002, consumed by convert_conf_disconnect_error and native_error_with_status (lines 40-50). m20_callstate_mapping.rs:59-70 defines pjsip_inv_state { NULL=0, CALLING=1, CONNECTING=2, CONFIRMED=3, DISCONNECTED=4 } and pjsua_call_media_status { NONE=0, ACTIVE=1, LOCAL_HOLD=2, REMOTE_HOLD=3, ERROR=4 }, used by convert_call_state and convert_call_media_state. ffi/bindings.rs currently carries stub aliases (PJ_SUCCESS=0, PJ_EUNKNOWN=-1, PJSUA_CALL_NULL..PJSUA_CALL_DISCONNECTED=0..6, PJSUA_REG_STATE_*) and will be replaced by bindgen output under pjsua-native. The real implementation must route the three files through ffi::bindings constants and delete the local duplicate const blocks.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Delete the duplicated const blocks and route every reference through ffi::bindings so there is a single source of truth. Remove the 'hand-coded duplicates of pjsua.h' comments. Consolidate the PJ_SUCCESS/PJ_EINVALIDOP imports shared by error_design_siperror.rs and m20_runtime_command_error.rs onto one source.

tickets.background: Source ticket P5-1 (Raw SIP Message, Call API & Audio Subscribe) specified the event model and call API. The markers at src/error/error_design_siperror.rs:204 and src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs:115 were left as stubs because the error fields still use raw i32/u64 where AccountId/CallId newtypes already exist in the event model but callers are not yet migrated. This work item resolves them by migrating the error fields (and AccountInfo) to the AccountId/CallId newtypes once the newtypes are stable across callers.
scope: - src/error/error_design_siperror.rs:204 — SipError.account_id: Option<u64> → Option<AccountId>, call_id: Option<u64> → Option<CallId>
- src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs:115 — AccountInfo.account_id: u64 → AccountId
- src/model/id_design_newtype.rs — the AccountId/CallId newtypes (NonZeroU64, from_u64)
- All SipError construction sites: SipError::new, native_error_with_status, convert_get_account_info_error, ReactorError::from, plus every in-crate caller that sets or matches account_id/call_id
- Out of scope: the reactor account state machine (P8-12) that delivers real AccountInfo values.
- Impact: every caller constructing or matching SipError / AccountInfo.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] SipError::new produces account_id: None and call_id: None with the newtype field types
UT: [Normal] native_error_with_status preserves native_status and leaves account_id/call_id as None
UT: [Boundary] converting a native acc_id of 0 (sentinel) via AccountId::from_u64 yields None and the error omits the id
UT: [Boundary] a valid non-zero native id converts to Some(AccountId) and round-trips to the same u64
UT: [Error] the account-not-found error path returns AccountNotFound with account_id None — no u64 leaks into the error
testIntegration: IT: A MakeCall failure flows through the reactor to a SipError whose call_id is a CallId newtype, and the caller can match on it without raw u64.
testExceptions: Full caller migration spans the whole call/account API surface; unit tests cover the error type and its converters, while integration tests cover reactor-to-API propagation. Real AccountInfo values still depend on P8-12 (reactor account state machine) — this ticket changes the types, not the retrieval.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】SipError carries account_id: Option<AccountId> and call_id: Option<CallId> (newtypes), and AccountInfo.account_id is AccountId — no u64 ID fields remain in these types.
【Happy path】SipError::new / native_error_with_status compile with the newtype fields and default account_id/call_id to None.
【Error case】A native id of 0 (PJSUA invalid sentinel) converts to None via AccountId::from_u64 / CallId::from_u64 — never a panic and never a stored 0.
【Edge case】All in-crate callers that set account_id/call_id are migrated to construct the newtypes from the native u32/u64 via from_u64, dropping the 0 sentinel.
【Edge case】The stub markers are removed only after the type migration compiles and the full test suite passes.

Implementation: (1) change SipError.account_id/call_id to Option<AccountId>/Option<CallId>; (2) change AccountInfo.account_id to AccountId; (3) update all constructors and callers; (4) keep the 0-sentinel → None rule. tickets.invariants: Every SipError account_id/call_id is a NonZeroU64-backed AccountId/CallId or None — never a bare 0. The PJSUA 0 sentinel always maps to None at the FFI boundary; it is never stored as a valid identifier. Answer semantics and call-state invariants from the call API remain unchanged by the type migration (C028). SipError keeps exactly its 6 public fields with Send + Sync preserved.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Replace the u64 fields with the newtypes crate-wide so the error type keeps its 6-field invariant with stronger typing. Remove the P8-19 stub comment once migrated. Update doc comments that describe account_id/call_id as u64 to describe the newtypes.
tickets.instrumentation: Add a tracing::warn! (or debug_assert!) when a 0 native id is dropped to None during conversion, aiding sentinel diagnostics.
tickets.investigation: SipError (error_design_siperror.rs:180-206) has six public fields including native_status: Option<i32>, account_id: Option<u64>, call_id: Option<u64>; the marker at :204 flags the u64 fields as pending AccountId/CallId migration. AccountId and CallId already exist as NonZeroU64-backed newtypes re-exported via event_model_payload_bus.rs:29-32 (pub use crate::model::AccountId / CallId) and are already used by the event model (RegistrationInfo.account_id, ConnectedCallInfo.call_id) and by m20_callstate_mapping::convert_call_state via CallId::from_u64. AccountInfo (m20_runtime_command_error.rs:107-116) still uses account_id: u64. Construction sites include SipError::new, native_error_with_status (m20_runtime_command_error.rs:40-50), convert_get_account_info_error (which also carries a P8-12 stub returning placeholder AccountInfo), and ReactorError::from. Migration must update all of these and their callers, mapping native u32/u64 ids through AccountId::from_u64 / CallId::from_u64 and dropping the 0 sentinel to None.

tickets.background: Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) specified the audio pipeline, but the underlying PJSIP FFI calls were left canned or unimplemented. The markers at src/ffi/bindings.rs:123, src/runtime/backend.rs:287, and src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs:110 were left as stubs because the pjsua-native feature and library linkage are not ready. This work item resolves them by replacing the canned/unimplemented FFI call sites with real bindgen-generated calls and obtaining actual media_status.
scope: - src/ffi/bindings.rs:123 — replace the canned pjsua_call_get_info stub with the real bindgen call; extend pjsua_call_info to the full bindgen struct (conf_slot + media_status)
- src/runtime/backend.rs:287 — implement PjsuaBackend methods against real PJSUA FFI instead of Err(BackendError("unimplemented"))
- src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs:110 — call the real pjsua_call_get_info to obtain actual media_status instead of hardcoding 1
- Out of scope: build detection/feature flags (P8-16); bindgen generation (P8-5); callback registration (P8-21).
- Impact: CallMediaStateChanged event accuracy; PjsuaBackend call/registration/media operations.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] convert_call_media_state maps media_status values (0=NONE, 1=ACTIVE, 2/3=LOCAL/REMOTE_HOLD, 4=ERROR) to CallMediaState
UT: [Normal] a real pjsua_call_get_info result (fixture) sets both conf_slot and media_status on the info struct
UT: [Error] pjsua_call_get_info returning non-PJ_SUCCESS produces a BackendError carrying the status
UT: [Edge] an unknown/absent media_status maps to a safe default (CallMediaState::Error) rather than panicking
testIntegration: IT: An incoming call's media event flows callback → NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged → real pjsua_call_get_info → CallMediaState, without the hardcoded media_status=1.
IT: PjsuaBackend::hangup / make_call propagate real PJSUA return codes into ReactorError.
testExceptions: Real FFI calls require PJSIP library linkage (pjsua-native + linked lib); unit tests use a fixture/mock for pjsua_call_get_info because the real symbol is unavailable in the sandbox. End-to-end media_status accuracy depends on a live PJSIP call — the event-conversion path is unit-tested with fixture media_status values.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Under pjsua-native, pjsua_call_get_info invokes the real FFI symbol and fills conf_slot and media_status from the actual pjsua_call_info struct.
【Happy path】NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged converts the real media_status from pjsua_call_get_info into CallMediaState (Active/Held/Error) — no hardcoded 1.
【Happy path】PjsuaBackend methods (make_call, answer_call, hangup, conf_connect, etc.) call real PJSUA functions and return their actual status.
【Error case】A non-success PJSUA status from a real FFI call maps to Err(ReactorError::BackendError) with the diagnostic preserved — never a canned success.
【Edge case】Without pjsua-native, the stub aliases remain so the crate compiles; the real-call path is feature-gated.
【Edge case】The canned-value tests in bindings.rs are replaced by tests asserting the real-call wiring (or are feature-gated).

tickets.notes: Stub sites: src/ffi/bindings.rs:123, src/runtime/backend.rs:287, src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs:110. Depends on P8-5 (bindgen output incl. full pjsua_call_info) and P8-16 (pjsua-native feature + linkage). Implementation: (1) replace the pjsua_call_get_info stub with the real call under pjsua-native; (2) extend pjsua_call_info with media_status; (3) wire m20_native_event_conv to read the real media_status; (4) implement the PjsuaBackend methods; (5) keep the non-feature stub path. Related: P8-18 (constants), P8-21 (callbacks).
tickets.invariants: The media_status reported for a call always comes from pjsua_call_get_info — never a hardcoded constant. Every PjsuaBackend method returns Err on a non-zero PJSUA status; a canned Ok(()) for an unexecuted FFI call is prohibited. Audio delivery keeps IN/OUT paired by timestamp (C031); codec policy remains PCMU and Opus only (C041); auto mode assigns Opus=255 and PCMU=254 (C042).
tickets.instrumentation: Add tracing::warn! on non-success PJSUA status at the FFI boundary. Expose a counter for CallMediaStateChanged events with their mapped media status.
tickets.investigation: ffi/bindings.rs:110-134 defines a minimal pjsua_call_info mirror containing only conf_slot and a stub pjsua_call_get_info that writes conf_slot = call_id and returns PJ_SUCCESS — canned values; its tests assert the canned behavior (conf_slot must match call_id). m20_native_event_conv.rs:104-113 handles NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged by calling convert_call_media_state(cid, 1) — media_status hardcoded to 1 (ACTIVE) because the real pjsua_call_get_info is not wired. runtime/backend.rs:287+ defines PjsuaBackend (derives Default) whose SipBackend methods (set_registration, make_call, answer_call, hangup, send_dtmf, configure_codecs, transfer_call, shutdown, conf_connect, conf_disconnect) all return Err(ReactorError::BackendError("... not yet implemented (P4-2)")). A real implementation must gate these on pjsua-native, invoke the bindgen FFI symbols, propagate status codes, and obtain actual media_status for CallMediaStateChanged.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the canned pjsua_call_get_info body and the test asserting conf_slot == call_id. Extract a resolve_media_status helper used by the CallMediaStateChanged path. Replace the per-method Err("... not yet implemented (P4-2)") boilerplate in PjsuaBackend with real calls, deleting the stub strings.

tickets.background: Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) specified the audio/media pipeline; the PJSIP → Rust event bridge in src/ffi was left as no-ops. The markers at src/ffi/callback.rs:16 and src/ffi/mod.rs:27 were left as stubs because PJSIP is not yet linked. This work item resolves them by registering all PJSIP callbacks via pjsua_config.cb and enqueuing NativeEvents through the reactor channel.
scope: - src/ffi/callback.rs:16,30,51,74,91,97 — implement on_incoming_call, on_reg_state, on_call_state, on_call_media_state, on_reg_started, on_call_redirected, on_dtmf_digit, on_call_transfer_status as NativeEvent producers
- src/ffi/mod.rs:27 — wire the callback module and expose a register_callbacks entry point that fills pjsua_config.cb

- src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs — consume the newly produced NativeEvent variants, including the currently-deferred P1/P2 variants (CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected)
- The reactor event channel — the lock-free queue / MPSC that NativeEvents are enqueued onto
- Out of scope: real FFI call sites (P8-20); build detection/linkage (P8-16).
- Impact: every event-driven path (incoming call, registration, call state, media, DTMF, transfer).
testUnit: UT: [Normal] on_incoming_call copies acc_id/call_id into a CallStateChanged NativeEvent without retaining rdata pointers
UT: [Normal] on_reg_state maps (acc_id, is_registering, code) into RegistrationStateChanged carrying the native status code
UT: [Normal] on_call_media_state produces NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged
UT: [Boundary] a queue-full enqueue returns a drop signal and increments a loss counter (no block)
UT: [Error] null rdata / reason pointers are handled without dereferencing null, and the event is still enqueued with an empty reason
testIntegration: IT: register_callbacks fills pjsua_config.cb with all callback pointers, and the reactor round-trips a NativeEvent → SipEventPayload for an incoming call.
IT: dtmf_digit and call_redirected events propagate to SipEventPayload without the current deferred-None behavior.
testExceptions: Live PJSIP callback invocation requires a linked PJSIP and a running account/call; unit tests invoke the extern "C" functions directly with synthetic args. The exact pjsua_config.cb field names are bindgen-dependent — the registration helper is asserted for the set of callback pointers, not the C layout.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Each PJSIP callback is registered into pjsua_config.cb and, when invoked, enqueues a NativeEvent (on_incoming_call → CallStateChanged, on_reg_state → RegistrationStateChanged, on_call_media_state → CallMediaStateChanged, on_dtmf_digit → DtmfDigit, on_reg_started → RegistrationStarted, on_call_redirected → CallRedirected, on_call_transfer_status → CallTransferStatus).

【Happy path】The enqueue uses only the permitted operations — copy params into a pre-allocated NativeEvent and push on a lock-free queue / MPSC — with no locks, allocation, .await, or PJSUA re-entry (design constraint in callback.rs:6-14).
【Error case】When the queue is full, the enqueue is loss-tolerant (event dropped, counter incremented) — it never blocks the PJSIP real-time thread.

【Edge case】The P1/P2 NativeEvent variants that currently return None in convert_native_event_to_payload (CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected) are now produced by their callbacks and either converted or explicitly deferred with a documented reason.
【Edge case】The stub markers are removed only after the callbacks enqueue real events and the reactor round-trip tests pass.

tickets.notes: Stub sites: src/ffi/callback.rs:16,30,51,74,91,97; src/ffi/mod.rs:27. Depends on P8-16 (pjsua-native / linkage) and the reactor channel. Implementation: (1) add register_callbacks(pjsua_config, channel); (2) implement each callback to enqueue a NativeEvent; (3) use a pre-allocated lock-free queue / MPSC per the design constraints; (4) update convert_native_event_to_payload for the newly produced variants; (5) keep the no-op stub path behind !pjsua-native. Related: P8-20 (FFI call sites), P8-13 (real CallId).
tickets.invariants: Callbacks never allocate, lock, await, or call back into PJSUA (design constraint from callback.rs:6-14). NativeEvent enqueue is loss-tolerant: a full queue drops the event and increments a counter, never blocking. Audio delivery keeps IN/OUT paired by timestamp (C031); codec policy remains PCMU and Opus only (C041); auto mode assigns Opus=255 and PCMU=254 (C042).
tickets.instrumentation: Add a monotonic counter for enqueued NativeEvents and a separate counter for dropped events on queue-full. tracing::debug! on callback entry with call_id/acc_id only (no payload copy).
tickets.investigation: ffi/callback.rs declares #[no_mangle] unsafe extern "C" callbacks — on_incoming_call (:16), on_reg_state (:30), on_call_state (:51), on_call_media_state (:74), plus on_reg_started / on_call_redirected / on_dtmf_digit / on_call_transfer_status (covers :91,97 per the marker) — each currently discards its arguments (let _ = (...)): pure no-ops. The design-constraint comment (callback.rs:6-14) mandates copying event params into a pre-allocated NativeEvent and enqueueing on a lock-free queue or MPSC channel. ffi/mod.rs:27 documents the callback module; there is no register_callbacks entry point yet. m20_native_event_conv.rs declares the NativeEvent variants (RegistrationStateChanged, RegistrationStarted, CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfDigit, plus P1/P2 TransportStateChanged, IceTransportError, CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected) but convert_native_event_to_payload returns None for the P1/P2 variants. The real implementation must (1) register the callbacks in pjsua_config.cb, (2) enqueue NativeEvents via a lock-free / MPSC channel, (3) let the reactor drain and convert, and (4) decide P1/P2 conversion or document deferral.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the let _ = (...) no-op bodies and replace them with a shared enqueue_native_event helper used by every callback (single source of truth for the lock-free enqueue). Delete the stale doc comments claiming the callbacks are no-ops. Ensure the channel is pre-allocated at registration time to honor the no-allocation rule.

tickets.background: Source ticket P3-1 specified the public API surface for account and transport configuration (AccountConfig validation, TransportConfig/ICE). The src/lib.rs:51 stub deferred the account/call/transport lifecycle methods because the configuration types (AccountConfig, TransportConfig, OutgoingCallRequest) were not yet stable enough to wire through RuntimeCommand dispatch. This work item resolves the deferred lifecycle by implementing the account and transport configuration lifecycle methods - creating (add), modifying (update_config), and deleting (remove) accounts, plus transport configuration methods.
scope: - src/lib.rs - replace the P8-22 stub at line 51; keep account/call/transport module declarations
- src/client.rs - SipClient::add_account / remove_account facade methods
- src/api/public_api_design.rs - SipAccountHandle lifecycle: real update_config (replaces the P8-14 no-op), remove, and transport methods
- src/runtime/command.rs - RuntimeCommand variants for account modify/delete and transport configuration
- src/runtime/reactor.rs - dispatch the new account/transport lifecycle commands
- src/config/account_config_spec.rs - AccountConfig validation reused for the modify path
- src/config/transport_ice_spec.rs - TransportConfig types wired into the transport lifecycle
- src/transport.rs - re-export/verify transport config types

- Out of scope: SipCall lifecycle (make/answer/hangup/hold/transfer/send_dtmf) is covered by P8-9; Audio Subscribe by P8-8; registration-state retrieval by P8-12; startup account restoration by P8-15.
- Impact: public API surface for account/transport lifecycle; RuntimeCommand gains new variants; SipClient/SipAccountHandle stay Clone + Send + Sync.
testUnit: UT: [C012] SipClient::add_account submits RuntimeCommand::AddAccount (asserted via MockBackend call records).
UT: [C012] SipClient::remove_account submits RuntimeCommand::RemoveAccount with the correct account_id.
UT: [C015] add_account rejects AccountConfig with empty username with Err(InvalidConfig) before dispatch.
UT: [C052] add_account rejects AccountCodecPolicy with both enable_pcmu=false and enable_opus=false.
UT: [C052] update_config with an invalid patch returns Err(InvalidConfig) and leaves the stored account unchanged.
UT: [C016] TransportConfig UDP/TCP variants construct and round-trip; the TLS variant compiles only with the tls feature.
UT: [C017] All lifecycle methods return Result<T, SipError> (compile-time signature assertions).
UT: [Normal] add_account with all-Optional-fields-None AccountConfig succeeds (display_name=None, auth_username=None, registrar_uri=None, outbound_proxy=[], contact_params=[]).
UT: [Boundary] remove_account of the same account twice: the second call returns Err (not found), no panic.
UT: [Error] update_config/remove_account on a non-existent account_id returns Err.
testIntegration: IT: [Lifecycle] add_account -> accounts() shows the account -> update_config changes stored config -> remove_account removes it, verified via the reactor's authoritative ClientState (read().await).
IT: [Validation-before-dispatch] MockBackend records zero add_account calls when an invalid AccountConfig is submitted.
IT: [Concurrency] Add and remove accounts from multiple tokio tasks; FIFO order preserved through the MPSC channel (C011).
testExceptions: Actual PJSUA registration/transport binding requires a running PJSIP stack (pjsua-native feature), which is not available in unit tests; MockBackend/PjsuaBackend stubs are used instead.
TLS compile-time gating is verified via cargo check with/without the tls feature, not by runtime unit tests.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】SipClient::add_account(AccountConfig) validates the config, submits RuntimeCommand::AddAccount, and returns a SipAccountHandle with a non-zero account_id on success.
【Happy path】SipAccountHandle::update_config(patch) submits an account-modify command and applies validated changes without dropping or recreating the account.
【Happy path】SipClient::remove_account(account_id) submits RuntimeCommand::RemoveAccount; the account no longer appears in accounts().
【Happy path】Transport configuration (UDP/TCP/ICE via TransportConfig) is accepted and reflected in the reactor's transport runtime state.
【Error case】add_account with an invalid AccountConfig returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig) before any RuntimeCommand is submitted - no state mutation on validation failure.
【Error case】update_config/remove_account on a non-existent account_id returns Err (InvalidConfig or NotInitialized), never panics.
【Edge case】AccountConfig with register_on_start=false and allow_outbound_without_register=true validates successfully and can be added.
【Edge case】All lifecycle methods are async fn returning Result<T, SipError>; SipClient/SipAccountHandle remain Clone + Send + Sync.

- Implementation steps: (1) add SipClient::add_account/remove_account facades; (2) implement real update_config and transport methods; (3) add RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount and transport variants; (4) wire reactor dispatch; (5) Red tests, then Green.
- Dependencies: RuntimeCommand already has AddAccount/RemoveAccount/SetRegistration (command.rs:49-56) backed by SipBackend trait methods (backend.rs:31-38); reuse AccountConfig validation from account_config_spec.rs.
- Related tickets: P8-9 (SipCall lifecycle), P8-13 (real CallId), P8-14 (update_config), P8-12 (account info), P8-15 (startup account restoration).

tickets.background: Source ticket P4-2 specified the foundational audio primitives: AudioFormat/AudioChunkPair (model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs), PairAligner (model/audio_aligner.rs), ResamplePipeline (model/audio_resampler.rs), and NegotiatedCodec/CodecSelectionPolicy (config/codec_policy_fallback.rs). The audio/ module was commented out in src/lib.rs:64-66 because those format types were not yet stable. This work item uncomments the audio/ module and implements higher-level audio orchestration that composes the model/ primitives into a usable pipeline.
scope: - src/lib.rs - uncomment `pub mod audio;` (line 66) and remove the P8-23 stub at line 64
- src/audio/ (new) - higher-level audio orchestration module: mod.rs plus orchestration submodules
- src/model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs - reuse AudioFormat, AudioChunk, AudioChunkPair, SampleRate, BitDepth, ChannelLayout (read-only)
- src/model/audio_aligner.rs - reuse PairAligner/TimedFrame
- src/model/audio_resampler.rs - reuse ResamplePipeline, interleave_in_out
- src/config/codec_policy_fallback.rs - reuse NegotiatedCodec, CodecSelectionPolicy
- Out of scope: FFI audio capture/playback (P8-26 / P3-2 FFI), AudioMixer/process_frame internals (P3-2), cpal device I/O (P8-7).
- Impact: new audio/ module compiled and linked; lib.rs module graph gains the audio submodule.
testUnit: UT: [C031] AudioFormat all 64 valid combinations construct; invalid frame_ms returns Err.
UT: [C036] PairAligner within-tolerance pairing returns (in,out); over-tolerance drops the earlier frame and zero-pads.
UT: [C037] ResamplePipeline 48kHz->16kHz resample yields correct output dimensions; stereo L=IN, R=OUT.
UT: [C041] CodecSelectionPolicy::PreferOpusFallbackPcmu resolves Opus first, falls back to PCMU.
UT: [C042] Auto-mode codec id assignment: Opus=255, PCMU=254, others=0.
UT: [Normal] Orchestration module re-exports exist (compile-time).
UT: [Edge] Empty AudioChunk::I16 flows through the pipeline.
UT: [Error] Invalid AudioFormat is rejected by the orchestration entry point with AudioFormatError.
testIntegration: IT: [Pipeline] Feed a stereo 48kHz frame through the audio/ orchestration API end-to-end (align -> resample -> policy) and verify the OUT buffer length and channel mapping.
IT: [Module-graph] cargo check succeeds with `pub mod audio;` uncommented and all re-exports resolving.
testExceptions: Actual rubato resampling fidelity/performance requires the rubato native crate, which is verified by dependency build, not unit assertions.
FFI capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame) is out of scope; the orchestration layer is tested with in-memory AudioChunk buffers.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】src/audio/ compiles with `pub mod audio;` uncommented; the module re-exports the orchestration API and composes AudioFormat, AudioChunkPair, PairAligner, ResamplePipeline, and CodecSelectionPolicy.

【Happy path】A full IN/OUT pipeline run (align -> resample -> codec policy) on a valid 48kHz stereo frame produces output matching the source invariants (stereo L=IN, R=OUT; IN/OUT paired by timestamp).
【Happy path】The orchestration layer propagates zero-padding from PairAligner when a pair exceeds tolerance, without panicking.
【Error case】Orchestration with an invalid AudioFormat (e.g., frame_ms outside {10,20,40,60}) returns a typed error (AudioFormatError); no partial/inconsistent AudioFormat is constructed.
【Error case】Codec policy fallback with no mutually supported codec returns an error (e.g., MediaNegotiationFailed), never panics.
【Edge case】AudioChunk::I16 with an empty Vec<i16> flows through the orchestration pipeline (valid edge state, len=0).

tickets.title: Implement memory ownership and default policies per node N0056 (Sections 47 & 48)

contracts.precondition: Tokio async runtime must be initialized (tokio::runtime::Handle::current() succeeds). AudioWorkerTask must be spawned on Tokio blocking pool via tokio::task::spawn_blocking.
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer struct created with lock-free queue boundary: crossbeam::ArrayQueue<Vec<i16>> out_queue separates AudioWorkerTask (async context) from RustMediaPort (PJSIP RT callback context). AudioWorkerTask runs process_frame loop in blocking pool.
contracts.invariant: No blocking operations (lock acquisition, dynamic memory allocation, syscall, .await) are permitted inside any function called from PJSIP RT callback thread (get_frame/put_frame). Only lock-free queue pop/push, memcpy, and zero-fill are allowed.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit validates: AudioMixer::new() creates struct with empty crossbeam::ArrayQueue. AudioWorkerTask::spawn succeeds when called from tokio::test context.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit validates: AudioWorkerTask::process_frame pushes mixed frame to out_queue. Mixer entry push operation does not panic.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit validates: crossbeam::ArrayQueue push from std::thread does not deadlock or panic. memcpy within callback context verified via mock port struct.

contracts.precondition: Rust FFI required to call C PJSUA library functions. Concurrency model defines reactor thread for serialized command execution.
contracts.postcondition: PJSIP FFI layer created with: (1) ffi::bindings module generated by bindgen build.rs with allowlist pattern, (2) PjOwnedStr safe wrapper for pj_str_t with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing, (3) extern C callback functions enqueue NativeEvent, (4) runtime/ modules use only safe SipBackend trait.
contracts.invariant: All unsafe code isolated to ffi/ module. No unsafe keyword in runtime/, client.rs, or config/. Compile-time lint enforces unsafe isolation.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit: build.rs must exist with allowlist patterns. ffi::bindings module references pjsua_* types at compile time.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit: PjOwnedStr::new creates pj_str_t with ptr pointing to owned Vec<u8>. extern C callback compiles without panic.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit via compile-time: runtime/ directory grep for 'unsafe' returns 0 matches (excluding test code).

contracts.precondition: PJSUA C library uses pj_pool_t for memory allocation. Callback parameters valid only within callback scope.
contracts.postcondition: pj_str_t always has Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>). Native callback pointers not held beyond callback scope. pj_pool_t memory never embedded in Rust structs.
contracts.invariant: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory. Original PJSUA ptr only used as source for immediate copy, never stored.
contracts.testPrecondition: Deferred to P4-2/P5-2. P3-2 verifies only that PjOwnedStr ensures Rust-ownership.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit: PjOwnedStr::new copies input bytes to owned Vec<u8>. Dropping PjOwnedStr does not invalidate external pointers.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit via compile-time: ffi/pj_str.rs contains no unsafe beyond initial pj_str_t construction.

tickets.background: Source ticket P3-2 specified the PJSIP FFI layer and runtime state, including node N0056 (§47 Memory Ownership & §48 Default Policies) which governs who owns pj_str_t / pj_pool_t memory across the FFI boundary. The memory_ownership_defaults.rs file was created as a stub (`pub struct Model {}` plus the P8-24 marker at line 23) because the ownership model was deferred. This work item implements the memory ownership model and default policies per node N0056.
scope: - src/model/memory_ownership_defaults.rs - replace the stub with the memory ownership model types and default policies
- src/model/mod.rs - re-export the new types
- src/ffi/pj_str.rs - reuse PjOwnedStr (Rust-owned pj_str_t backing) as the concrete ownership primitive
- src/ffi/mod.rs - verify the ownership model integrates with the FFI boundary
- Out of scope: new bindgen bindings, the callback bridge implementation, and any unsafe-code changes in runtime/ (all unsafe remains isolated to ffi/).
- Impact: memory-ownership types available to the FFI layer and runtime state; formalizes who owns callback-parameter memory.
testUnit: UT: [C057] Ownership model classifies PjOwnedStr as Rust-owned; a pj_str_t copied from an FFI callback source is immediately copied to Vec<u8>.
UT: [C057] Default policy marks callback-parameter memory as valid only within callback scope.

testExceptions: Real pj_pool_t lifetime semantics require a live PJSUA stack (pjsua-native feature); the ownership model is specified as type-level/documentation invariants and verified with PjOwnedStr unit tests, not against a live pool.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】memory_ownership_defaults.rs defines the ownership model (e.g., an Ownership distinction between Rust-owned and PJSUA-pool-owned, with default policies) and it compiles and re-exports through model/mod.rs.
【Happy path】The default policy matches C057: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory; the original PJSUA ptr is only used as an immediate copy source, never stored.
【Happy path】PjOwnedStr remains the concrete implementation of the Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>) and satisfies the ownership model's Rust-owned policy.
【Error case】The model forbids embedding pj_pool_t-owned memory in Rust structs (type-level/documentation invariant) - no owned pj_pool_t memory in Rust structs.
【Edge case】Empty strings (slen=0) and large inputs (>4096 bytes) remain valid under the ownership model.

contracts.precondition: Tokio async runtime must be initialized (tokio::runtime::Handle::current() succeeds). AudioWorkerTask must be spawned on Tokio blocking pool via tokio::task::spawn_blocking.
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer struct created with lock-free queue boundary: crossbeam::ArrayQueue<Vec<i16>> out_queue separates AudioWorkerTask (async context) from RustMediaPort (PJSIP RT callback context). AudioWorkerTask runs process_frame loop in blocking pool.
contracts.invariant: No blocking operations (lock acquisition, dynamic memory allocation, syscall, .await) are permitted inside any function called from PJSIP RT callback thread (get_frame/put_frame). Only lock-free queue pop/push, memcpy, and zero-fill are allowed.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit validates: AudioMixer::new() creates struct with empty crossbeam::ArrayQueue. AudioWorkerTask::spawn succeeds when called from tokio::test context.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit validates: AudioWorkerTask::process_frame pushes mixed frame to out_queue. Mixer entry push operation does not panic.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit validates: crossbeam::ArrayQueue push from std::thread does not deadlock or panic. memcpy within callback context verified via mock port struct.

contracts.precondition: AudioMixer must exist and be accessible via Arc<AudioMixer>. AudioWorkerTask must be spawned and running.
contracts.postcondition: AudioWorkerTask::process_frame iterates all sources in AudioMixer, calls AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk for each, applies gain/mute, mixes via i32 accumulation to saturating i16 clamp, pushes result to out_queue. Sources added/removed via AudioMixer are reflected at next frame boundary.
contracts.invariant: Sources are added and removed at frame boundaries. Source iteration uses snapshot of source_ids to avoid DashMap invalidation during iteration.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit validates: AudioMixer::add_source increments next_source_id and returns sequential IDs. Arc<AudioMixer> is Send + Sync.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit validates: AudioWorkerInner::process_frame with 2 MockAsyncAudioSources sums samples to mixed output buffer. Muted source skipped. Gain-adjusted source produces scaled output.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit validates: AudioMixer::add_source during AudioWorkerTask iteration does not cause panic. 32 sources added sequentially all get correct IDs.

tickets.background: Source ticket P3-2 specified the AudioWorkerTask and its per-call state (mixer, call_id, frame_duration). These fields are stored (src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:266-279) but marked #[allow(dead_code)] and never exposed. This work item adds inspection/query accessors so the runtime and diagnostics can read AudioWorker state, and wires call_id into logging/metrics correlation for when call lifecycle is active.
scope: - src/runtime/audio_worker.rs - add inspection accessors (mixer(), call_id(), frame_duration()) to AudioWorkerTask and AudioWorkerInner; remove the #[allow(dead_code)] attributes
- src/runtime/mod.rs - verify re-export/compile
- Out of scope: AudioMixer behavior changes, process_frame logic, FFI capture/playback (P8-26), and call-lifecycle activation (P8-9/P8-13).
- Impact: read-only observation of per-call audio worker state from the runtime layer; enables future metrics correlation by call_id.
testUnit: UT: [C034] AudioWorkerTask::spawn(mixer, 42, 20ms) -> call_id() == 42, frame_duration() == 20ms, mixer() == same Arc.
UT: [C035] Accessors return the exact Arc<AudioMixer> identity (Arc::ptr_eq) passed to spawn.
UT: [Normal] frame_duration() round-trips Duration::from_millis(20).
UT: [Boundary] frame_duration of Duration::ZERO is reported as-is (no clamping).
UT: [Error/compile] Accessors take &self (immutable) - verified by calling them through &AudioWorkerTask.
UT: [C038] runtime/audio_worker.rs contains no unsafe keyword (grep test).
testIntegration: IT: [Observation] Spawn a worker, read call_id()/frame_duration() while running, then shutdown(); state remains readable after shutdown.
IT: [Metrics] A log line emitted during the worker lifecycle includes the call_id field (verified with a tracing subscriber in test).
testExceptions: Wiring call_id into live metrics requires an active call lifecycle plus a metrics pipeline; until then, correlation is verified via log-lines and accessor tests.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】AudioWorkerTask exposes mixer() -> &Arc<AudioMixer>, call_id() -> u64, and frame_duration() -> Duration accessors returning the values passed to spawn().
【Happy path】AudioWorkerInner likewise exposes the same state (mixer, call_id, frame_duration) for the in-loop context.
【Happy path】After spawn(), call_id() returns the exact call_id argument (e.g., 42) and frame_duration() returns the exact Duration.
【Error case】Accessors are read-only - no mutation of mixer/call_id/frame_duration through inspection (accessors take &self and return immutable values/references).
【Edge case】A worker with frame_duration = 20ms reports the same Duration through frame_duration().
【Edge case】call_id is surfaced in worker log lines/metrics labels when present, with graceful absence when call lifecycle is not active.
