tickets.boyScoutPlan:
### Boy Scout Rule — Translatability Plan

- Replace `AccountId::from_u64(1).expect("NonZeroU64::new(1) should never fail")` with typed `account_id: Option<AccountId>` propagation — removes the hardcoded value and the `.expect()`. The CONFIRMED arm becomes `account_id: account_id?` (total: `None` → `None`, never a panic).
- Rename the `_call_id` parameter in `convert_call_state_with_previous` to `call_id` now that it is forwarded (not discarded) — a parameter that is passed through must carry its real name so the narrative "convert the call state, forwarding the call's account" reads top-to-bottom.
- In `convert_native_event_to_payload`, name the account context parameter `call_account_id` (the account that owns the call) instead of a generic `account_id`, keeping the conversion's responsibility explicit: the caller resolves the call's account; the function converts.
- Update the `extract_event_ids` doc comment — it currently claims account_id resolution "once call tracking lands (P4-1)"; after P9-6 the reactor resolves it from `calls` immediately, so the comment must be rewritten to the truth (comments must not lie).
- Remove the now-unneeded `AccountId::from_u64(1)` construction and its justification comment — a hardcoded value defended by a justification comment is a No-Justification-Rule violation.
- Keep each function single-responsibility: `convert_call_state` maps `pjsip_inv_state` → payload; the account resolution stays in the caller (`convert_native_event_to_payload`/reactor), never inside the mapping function.

tickets.background:
Goal: Eliminate the three [::STUB::] P10-1 placeholders so account info retrieval (convert_get_account_info_error, MockBackend::get_account_info, the GetAccountInfo dispatch) and SipAccountHandle::registration_state() return real data derived from the reactor's authoritative ClientState (ClientState.accounts / AccountEntry.registration).

Purpose: Callers of the public API observe the actual registration status and account information of their SIP accounts instead of a hardcoded RegistrationState::Idle and canned mock values. This closes the P3-1 placeholder gap that deferred account-info retrieval until the reactor account state machine (N0025) existed.

Motivation: The reactor already maintains authoritative ClientState.accounts (populated by the AddAccount handler, reactor.rs:195-199); RegistrationState (7 variants) and its transition table are fully implemented (registr_state_machine.rs); three P10-1 STUBs remain and the ticket is [::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::] — a previous implementation round was rejected. Completing this ticket removes the last P3-1-era placeholders from the account-info surface.

Constraints: C017 (all public APIs return Result<T, SipError>); C013 (IDs are NonZeroU64 AccountId); C026 (registration independent of call ability). AccountEntry.registration is the authoritative source; the registration state machine transitions themselves (N0025 core) are out of scope. The real pjsua_acc_get_info FFI call (P8-20) is out of scope — the MockBackend path is the deterministic test substrate. Query paths must read a snapshot of ClientState and never block the reactor loop (query_state() is the sanctioned mechanism).

tickets.investigation:
Material evidence from source investigation:
1. Three [::STUB::] P10-1 markers remain in source: (a) src/api/public_api_design.rs:117 — SipAccountHandle::registration_state() returns Ok(RegistrationState::Idle) unconditionally; its doc comment (lines 111-114) admits it is a placeholder pending the reactor account state machine. (b) src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs:161-165 — convert_get_account_info_error(account_exists: bool, pj_status: i32) validates account_exists (→ Err(AccountNotFound, retryable=false)) and pj_status (→ Err(native_error_with_status)), then falls through to Err(SipError::new(NativeError, "account state not yet available (P3-1)")) — the Ok(AccountInfo) path is unreachable. (c) src/runtime/backend.rs:244-255 — MockBackend::get_account_info returns a canned AccountInfoSnapshot { registration_status: 200, registration_expires: Some(3600), online_status: true, uri: format!("sip:user{native_acc_id}@mock.example.com") } when get_account_info_result is None; it is not connected to any account state.
2. The authoritative reactor state exists: ClientState.accounts: BTreeMap<AccountId, AccountEntry> (src/runtime/state.rs:42-52) is populated by the AddAccount handler (src/runtime/reactor.rs:195-199). AccountEntry (state.rs:58-67) carries id: u64, native_id: i32, config: String, registration: String (placeholder types). RuntimeHandle::query_state() (handle.rs:141-156) submits DispatchCommand::QueryState and returns a ClientState clone — the sanctioned non-blocking query mechanism (reactor.rs:225-228).
3. RegistrationState (7 variants) with a full transition table and Display impl producing canonical strings is implemented in src/state/registr_state_machine.rs:76-163. No storage-string parser exists yet.
4. The GetAccountInfo flow: RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo { native_acc_id: u32, reply: oneshot<Result<AccountInfoSnapshot, ReactorError>> } (command.rs:88-93) → DispatchCommand::GetAccountInfo (command.rs:342-348) → reactor handler calls backend.get_account_info(native_acc_id) inside catch_unwind and replies (reactor.rs:151-185). RuntimeHandle::submit_get_account_info (handle.rs:115-134) is the typed caller.
5. SipBackend::get_account_info(&self, native_acc_id: u32) -> Result<AccountInfoSnapshot, ReactorError> (backend.rs:89). AccountInfoSnapshot (m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs:31-43): acc_id: AccountId, registration_status: u32, registration_expires: Option<u32>, online_status: bool, uri: String. It feeds registration_status_to_payload (m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs:50-67) used by process_native_event (reactor.rs:310-330).
6. SipClient::accounts() (client.rs:197-210) already maps AccountEntry → public AccountSnapshot via account_snapshot_from_entry (client.rs:307-316), which computes registered: entry.registration == "Registered" — the only existing consumption of AccountEntry.registration.
7. Duplicate account-info types flagged by Boy Scout: AccountInfo (m20_runtime_command_error.rs:116-128) vs AccountInfoSnapshot (m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs:31-43). The public AccountInfo has no production caller today; convert_get_account_info_error is only invoked from its own test module.
8. MockBackend::add_account (backend.rs:152-164) hardcodes id: 1, native_id: 1 and registration: "Registered"; it returns the entry to the reactor, which stores it keyed by AccountId::from_u64(entry.id). A registry keyed by native_acc_id does not exist today, so get_account_info cannot derive from account state.
9. make test == cargo test (Makefile); unit tests live in #[cfg(test)] mod tests blocks, integration tests in tests/verify_spec_*.rs (e.g. tests/verify_spec_p8_3.rs asserts the C026 make_call/RegistrationState independence by reading the source signature).
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvements, inside and outside this ticket's scope:
- Inside: registration_state() reads as prose — 'query reactor state, resolve account entry, map registration string, default to Disabled' — with one responsibility per step; replace the misleading doc comment (public_api_design.rs:111-114) with one that states the real behavior.
- Inside: extract account_entry_to_snapshot (a verb-phrase function 'derive snapshot from stored entry') in backend.rs instead of an inline struct literal, and name the mock's registry field accounts (a domain noun) instead of an anonymous map.
- Inside: convert_get_account_info_error reads as 'if no account return AccountNotFound; if the FFI status failed return NativeError; otherwise return AccountInfo' — one responsibility per branch, no fall-through placeholder Err.
- Inside: RegistrationState::from_storage_str is a single named verb with a fully matched domain vocabulary; no catch-all except the documented Disabled fallback for unknown storage strings.
- Outside (Boy Scout): the duplicate AccountInfo (m20_runtime_command_error.rs:116) and AccountInfoSnapshot (m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs:31) types are flagged but NOT consolidated in this ticket (the ripple touches command.rs/handle.rs/reactor.rs and process_native_event) — recorded as an open item with a consolidation plan for a future ticket.
- No error swallowing: query_state failures are mapped to SipError; MockBackend::get_account_info for an unknown native_acc_id returns Err rather than a canned Ok.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Replace the no-op fn main() {} in src/build/build_strategy_os_deps.rs with real PJSIP build detection (RFC §28), declare the pjsua-native feature in Cargo.toml, wire tls/srtp feature flags from detection, and provide a build/CI entry point (run_ci_matrix) that consumes the existing cicd_docker_prebuilt.rs CI matrix — so both with-PJSIP and without-PJSIP builds are exercised and diagnosed.

### Purpose
The crate must build in two modes per RFC §4/§28: with a system PJSIP install (the pjsua-native feature path — bindgen output from P8-5 replaces stub aliases, build.rs emits link directives) and without one (stub-alias fallback keeps cargo build/test green on PJSIP-free CI). Today src/build/build_strategy_os_deps.rs is an empty fn main() {} with a [::STUB::] P10-2 marker, Cargo.toml has no pjsua-native feature, and the CI matrix in cicd_docker_prebuilt.rs is dead code. This ticket makes build-time detection real so the feature surface (tls/srtp flags, ClientCapabilities.tls_available/srtp_available, TransportConfig::Tls) is grounded in what the build actually found.

### Motivation
This ticket is [::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::] — a previous implementation round was rejected. Source ticket P3-1 (Public API Surface & Account/Transport Configuration) specified the public API and config surface but left the Build Strategy & OS Dependencies node (N0039) unmapped; the marker at src/build/build_strategy_os_deps.rs:27 was left as a stub because the crate compiles without a system PJSIP install. Downstream tickets (P8-5/P11-5 bindgen, P8-20 FFI call sites, P8-21 callback registration) all depend on pjsua-native existing and on detection being real. CI workflows already declare the 3 OS × 4 feature matrix; the in-code consumer is missing.

### Constraints
- Must not implement bindgen generation (P8-5/P11-5), runtime FFI call sites (P8-20), or callback registration (P8-21) — those are separate tickets that consume this ticket's detection result.
- The pjsua-native feature name must match what src/ffi/bindings.rs, src/ffi/mod.rs, and build.rs expect (all three document pjsua-native as the canonical name).
- The crate must still compile and its test suite must still pass with all build features disabled (no PJSIP installed) — the no-PJSIP build is a first-class supported mode.
- Feature flags derived from detection must be deterministic for a given environment and must keep cfg!(feature = "tls")/cfg!(feature = "srtp") semantics that observability_metrics.rs:122,126 already rely on.
scope:
**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
  - src/build/build_strategy_os_deps.rs — MODIFY: replace the empty fn main() {} (line 32) with the PJSIP build-detection entry point per RFC §28; add named functions detect_pjsip(), resolve_feature_flags(), run_ci_matrix() so the module reads as prose
  - src/build/mod.rs — MODIFY: add `pub mod build_strategy_os_deps;` so the new module and its entry point are exported (today only cicd_docker_prebuilt is declared)
  - src/build/cicd_docker_prebuilt.rs — MODIFY: consume the existing CI matrix (CiOsTarget::all(), FeatureCombination::all()) from run_ci_matrix(); extract the 12 (OS, features) iteration into a tested helper
  - build.rs — MODIFY: coordinate PJSIP header/library detection with the pjsua-native feature flag (today it is a P11-5 bindgen stub fn main() {}); emit cargo:rustc-link-search/rustc-link-lib only when detection reports a prebuilt/source build present
  - Cargo.toml — MODIFY: declare `pjsua-native = []` under [features]; add `pjsua-native` to lints.rust check-cfg values (next to cpal-input) so cfg(feature = "pjsua-native") is a recognized cfg
  - Cargo.toml — MODIFY: wire tls/srtp feature resolution from detection; keep default = ["serde", "tls"] unchanged so no-PJSIP builds still compile
  - src/config/observability_metrics.rs — CONTEXT: ClientCapabilities.tls_available/srtp_available already read cfg!(feature = "tls")/cfg!(feature = "srtp") (lines 122,126); the detection-wired flags must keep these semantics (feature on ⇔ flag true)
  - .github/workflows — CONTEXT: ci.yml/integration.yml/prebuilt-refresh.yml already define the 3 OS × 4 feature matrix and Docker/prebuilt jobs; the run_ci_matrix() entry point mirrors this matrix in-code so CI yaml and code stay consistent

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - bindgen binding generation (P8-5/P11-5) — Excluded because bindgen needs PJSIP headers present and is a separate ticket; this ticket only wires the pjsua-native feature flag and detection that P8-5 will consume
  - runtime FFI call sites (P8-20) and callback registration (P8-21) — Excluded because they require the generated bindings to exist first; they consume the detection result but are not build-time detection

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - cargo build / CI matrix for the crate — Nature: build-time behavior; a present-PJSIP detection enables the pjsua-native path and link directives, absent detection keeps the stub-alias fallback; CI matrix jobs exercise both. No API surface change.
  - feature-gated config types (TransportConfig::Tls, ClientCapabilities.tls_available/srtp_available) — Nature: compile-time availability; the tls/srtp features wired from detection gate these types (C016/C043 semantics preserved).

tickets.title: Implement account and transport configuration lifecycle methods (make, answer, hangup) per the P3-1 specification

contracts.precondition: Command serialization established — RuntimeCommand variants (AddAccount/RemoveAccount/UpdateAccount/CreateTransport) are constructible with a tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender reply channel and enqueue on the reactor's UnboundedSender MPSC channel (RuntimeHandle::submit / submit_add_account, handle.rs).
contracts.postcondition: Public API designed around RuntimeCommand pattern — SipClient::add_account/remove_account/add_transport and SipAccountHandle::update_config/remove submit the corresponding RuntimeCommand variants; verified via MockBackend call records and the reactor's ClientState.
contracts.invariant: API is Send+Sync — assert_send/assert_sync::<SipClient> and SipAccountHandle compile-time assertions (public_api_design.rs:302).

contracts.precondition: ClientConfig defined — ClientConfig::builder() constructs a valid config (client_config_spec.rs) that passes validate(); AccountConfig has 16 fields including codecs/dtmf/media.
contracts.postcondition: AccountConfig specified with validation — AccountConfig::validate() returns Ok for a valid config and Err(InvalidConfig) for empty username/domain/password, both codecs disabled, empty DTMF send/receive, zero registration_expires, invalid opus bitrate/complexity/ptime (account_config_spec.rs:198-263).
contracts.invariant: Validation rules enforced — every violated rule yields a distinct InvalidConfig message; validation is reused in add_account and the update_config merge path.

contracts.precondition: ClientConfig includes transport/ICE — ClientConfig.transports accepts Vec<TransportConfig>; IceConfig/StunServerConfig/TurnServerConfig/TurnTransport are available (transport_ice_spec.rs).
contracts.postcondition: TransportConfig and ICE config specified — Udp/Tcp construct with bind_addr; IceConfig supports full ICE (enabled/aggressive_nomination/renomination/max_host_candidates); SipClient::add_transport dispatches CreateTransport and the reactor records TransportRuntimeState in client_state.transports.
contracts.invariant: Full ICE support, trickle ICE optional — IceConfig default has trickle_ice=false; a full-ICE config with aggressive_nomination is supported (transport_ice_spec.rs tests).

contracts.precondition: Public API design in progress — all lifecycle method signatures are defined (SipClient::add_account/remove_account/account/add_transport, SipAccountHandle::update_config/remove).
contracts.postcondition: Error design constrains API return types — every lifecycle method returns Result<T, SipError>; ReactorError is mapped to SipError (NativeError for reactor-down/backend errors, AccountNotFound for missing accounts, InvalidConfig for validation failures).
contracts.invariant: All APIs return Result<T, SipError> — compile-time fn-pointer signature assertions for every lifecycle method.

contracts.precondition: Account API needs state — an account must exist (add_account succeeded) before registration_state()/update_config() operate; SipAccountHandle carries the client + account id.
contracts.postcondition: Registration state machine defined — registration_state() maps AccountEntry.registration via RegistrationState::from_storage_str (P10-1); MockBackend stores "Registered" on add_account; register()/unregister() submit SetRegistration.
contracts.invariant: Registration independent of call ability — update_config does not change registration state; register/unregister operate regardless of config changes.

contracts.precondition: AccountConfig defines codec policy — AccountCodecPolicy { enable_pcmu, enable_opus, opus: OpusConfig } is a field of AccountConfig (account_config_spec.rs:85).
contracts.postcondition: Codec enforcement and fallback rules specified — AccountConfig::validate rejects enable_pcmu=false && enable_opus=false; opus ranges enforced (bitrate 500-512000, complexity 0-10, ptime 10/20/40/60).
contracts.invariant: PCMU and Opus only — at least one of enable_pcmu/enable_opus must be true for any account config accepted by add_account/update_config.

contracts.precondition: Transport config defined — TransportConfig enum with Udp/Tcp and #[cfg(feature="tls")] Tls(TlsTransportConfig) (transport_ice_spec.rs).
contracts.postcondition: SRTP spec and reconnection policy specified — AccountMediaConfig.srtp accepts SrtpPolicy::{Disabled,Optional,Mandatory}; the transport lifecycle records TransportRuntimeState for created transports.
contracts.invariant: SRTP feature-gated — the Tls variant and TlsConfig only compile under #[cfg(feature="tls")]; at runtime without the feature the variant is absent at the type level.

contracts.precondition: ClientConfig defined — ClientConfig::validate() exists (client_config_spec.rs) and enforces event_bus_capacity>=16, raw_sip bounds, max_calls>0, transports non-empty.
contracts.postcondition: Validation phase with fail-fast rules — the first violation is returned as Err(InvalidConfig) with a rule-specific message; no RuntimeCommand is submitted on validation failure (no partial state mutation).
contracts.invariant: All validation rules enumerated — every AccountConfig validation rule (empty username/domain/password, no codec, empty DTMF send/receive, zero registration_expires, opus ranges) has a dedicated test entry.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Make the account and transport configuration lifecycle fully functional on the public API and through the runtime: SipClient::add_account/remove_account/account/add_transport facades that validate then dispatch, a real SipAccountHandle::update_config (replacing the no-op), and reactor dispatch that keeps the authoritative ClientState in lockstep with backend operations.

### Purpose
P3-1 specified the configuration types (AccountConfig, TransportConfig, ClientConfig) but deferred the lifecycle methods behind the src/lib.rs:54 stub. Without these methods the crate cannot add, modify, or remove accounts at runtime — the core of any SIP client. This ticket turns the deferred stub into real, tested behavior.

### Motivation
Source ticket P3-1 explicitly deferred account/call/transport lifecycle methods because AccountConfig/TransportConfig/OutgoingCallRequest were not yet stable. Those types are now stable (P3-1, P4-1, P10-1 landed). The prior no-op update_config (P11-7, previously P8-14) and the reactor AddAccount reply that discards the assigned account_id make the facade unable to return a real handle. This ticket removes the deferred stub and the no-op.

### Constraints
- All lifecycle methods are async fn returning Result<T, SipError> (C017); SipClient/SipAccountHandle stay Clone + Send + Sync (C012).
- Validation must occur before dispatch (fail-fast, C052): invalid config/patch returns Err(InvalidConfig) with zero state mutation.
- SipCall lifecycle (make/answer/hangup/hold/transfer/send_dtmf) is OUT of scope (P8-9); real CallId wiring is P8-13; startup account restoration is P8-15; real PJSUA FFI is P3-2/P4-2.
scope: - src/lib.rs:54 — Replace the `[::STUB::] P10-3` marker ("account/call/transport lifecycle methods are deferred") with a real doc comment; KEEP `pub mod account; pub mod call; pub mod transport;` declarations. The module declarations stay; only the stub-gating comment is removed. Also update the line-52 doc comment "Account and Transport type stubs" which becomes a lie once lifecycle methods are real.

- src/client.rs — Add `SipClient::add_account(&self, config: AccountConfig) -> Result<SipAccountHandle, SipError>`: validate config first (fail-fast, Err(InvalidConfig) with zero dispatch), then submit via `RuntimeHandle::submit_add_account`, return `SipAccountHandle::new(self.clone(), account_id)` with the backend-assigned id.

- src/client.rs — Add `SipClient::remove_account(&self, account_id: u64) -> Result<(), SipError>`: submit RuntimeCommand::RemoveAccount. The reactor must ALSO remove the entry from client_state.accounts — today the Execute closure only calls backend.remove_account and leaves ClientState stale.
- src/client.rs — Add `SipClient::account(&self, account_id: u64) -> Result<SipAccountHandle, SipError>`: query_state; Err(AccountNotFound) if the id is missing, else return a handle.

- src/client.rs — Add `SipClient::add_transport(&self, config: TransportConfig) -> Result<(), SipError>`: submit RuntimeCommand::CreateTransport; the reactor records a TransportRuntimeState in client_state.transports.

- src/api/public_api_design.rs — Implement real `SipAccountHandle::update_config(&self, patch: AccountConfigPatch) -> Result<(), SipError>`: query_state -> find AccountEntry -> `patch.apply(&entry.config)` (merge + AccountConfig::validate) -> submit RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount with the merged config. Replaces the `[::STUB::] P11-7` no-op.
- src/api/public_api_design.rs — Add `SipAccountHandle::remove(&self) -> Result<(), SipError>`: convenience that delegates to `self.client.remove_account(self.id)`.

- src/runtime/command.rs — Change `RuntimeCommand::AddAccount.reply` from `Result<(), ReactorError>` to `Result<u64, ReactorError>` so the reactor returns the assigned logical account_id; update the manual Debug/Display impls and `DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command`.

- src/runtime/command.rs — Add `RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount { account_id: u64, config: AccountConfig, reply }` and `RuntimeCommand::CreateTransport { config: TransportConfig, reply }`; update Debug/Display impls and DispatchCommand conversion.

- src/runtime/handle.rs — Add `RuntimeHandle::submit_add_account(&self, config: AccountConfig) -> Result<u64, ReactorError>` (pattern: submit_get_account_info / submit_add_audio_source); in `submit()`, route DispatchCommand::AddAccount to `unreachable!("use submit_add_account")` and add the UpdateAccount/CreateTransport match arms.

testIntegration: IT: [Lifecycle] End-to-end account lifecycle via the reactor: SipClient::new -> add_account(valid) -> accounts() contains the account with matching uri -> update_config(valid patch) changes entry.config in query_state (authoritative ClientState) -> SipAccountHandle::remove() / remove_account(id) -> accounts() no longer contains the account. Each step is verified by reading client.handle().query_state().await.accounts, not the event stream (C021 O-004).

IT: [Validation-before-dispatch] MockBackend records zero add_account calls when an invalid AccountConfig is submitted: add_account(empty-username config) returns Err(InvalidConfig) and backend.accounts stays empty (no side effect, no partial state mutation).

IT: [Concurrency] Add and remove accounts from multiple tokio tasks concurrently; FIFO order through the unbounded MPSC channel (C011) guarantees unique incrementing ids and no lost accounts: spawn 5 tasks each adding one account, join, assert accounts() has 5 distinct ids; then spawn 5 removal tasks, join, assert accounts() is empty.

IT: [Transport] add_transport(CreateTransport) -> reactor's authoritative ClientState transports reflects TransportRuntimeState (transport_id, transport_type, port): add_transport(TransportConfig::udp(5070)) -> query_state().transports has one entry with port 5070.
testExceptions: Item: Real PJSUA registration/transport FFI binding. Reason: the real PJSUA registration/transport behavior is NOT TESTABLE in unit tests because it requires a running PJSIP stack linked via the pjsua-native feature, which is not available in this environment; we cannot test it without the FFI dependency. This is NOT a design defect — the SipBackend abstraction (backend.rs:20, C038) intentionally isolates FFI behind MockBackend/PjsuaBackend, which provide a deterministic in-process stand-in for every lifecycle command; the real FFI binding is a P3-2/P4-2 dependency by design, not an untested behavior gap.

Item: TLS compile-time feature gating. Reason: the absence of the TransportConfig::Tls variant when the tls feature is disabled is NOT TESTABLE at runtime because the variant is removed at the type level (RFC §12) — we cannot test a type that does not compile into the test binary. This is NOT an architectural defect — the feature gate is an explicit, deterministic compile-time contract. Alternative verification: `cargo check --no-default-features` (variant absent) vs `cargo check --features tls` (variant present), plus a cfg-gated #[test] that only compiles under the feature.

Item: Actual socket binding of TransportConfig.bind_addr. Reason: the real socket bind is NOT TESTABLE because PjsuaBackend::create_transport is unimplemented until P3-2/P4-2 wires pjsua_transport_create, and a real bind requires a live network stack; we cannot test it without those dependencies. This is NOT a design defect — the reactor's TransportRuntimeState recording and CreateTransport dispatch are deterministic and fully unit-tested with MockBackend (which returns Ok(()) for create_transport); only the FFI layer is deferred, by design (C038).
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】SipClient::add_account(AccountConfig) validates the config, submits RuntimeCommand::AddAccount (via submit_add_account), and returns a SipAccountHandle with a non-zero account_id on success; the account is immediately visible in accounts() and query_state.

【Happy path】SipAccountHandle::update_config(patch) merges the patch with the stored AccountConfig, validates the merged result, and submits RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount; the changed config is reflected in the reactor's authoritative ClientState without dropping or recreating the account (same account_id).
【Happy path】SipClient::remove_account(account_id) submits RuntimeCommand::RemoveAccount and the reactor removes the account from client_state.accounts; the account no longer appears in accounts().

【Happy path】Transport configuration (TransportConfig UDP/TCP via SipClient::add_transport) is accepted and reflected in the reactor's client_state.transports as TransportRuntimeState (transport_id/type/port).

【Error case】add_account with an invalid AccountConfig returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig) before any RuntimeCommand is submitted — no state mutation on validation failure (MockBackend records zero calls).
【Error case】update_config/remove_account on a non-existent account_id returns Err (AccountNotFound), never panics.
【Edge case】AccountConfig with register_on_start=false and allow_outbound_without_register=true validates successfully and can be added.
【Edge case】All lifecycle methods are async fn returning Result<T, SipError>; SipClient/SipAccountHandle remain Clone + Send + Sync.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】All account/transport lifecycle API functions return Result<T, SipError> (C017); add_account/update_config succeed only after AccountConfig::validate() passes (C015); a successful add_account yields a SipAccountHandle with a non-zero account_id and the account is visible in the reactor's authoritative ClientState (C021).
- 【Invariant on error】Validation failures return Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig) BEFORE any RuntimeCommand submission — no partial state mutation (C052 fail-fast); a downed reactor maps to Err(NativeError); missing accounts map to Err(AccountNotFound), never panic.
- 【Internal state invariant】The reactor's ClientState is the single source of truth (O-004): AccountEntry.config holds the full AccountConfig, entry.id is the logical account id, and remove_account must remove the entry from client_state.accounts (not just the backend registry). Registration state is independent of config updates (C026).
- 【Boundary invariant】AccountConfig with register_on_start=false + allow_outbound_without_register=true is valid (RFC §11.1); TransportConfig TLS variant is feature-gated and never present at runtime without the tls feature (C016/C043); codec policy accepts only PCMU and Opus (C041).

tickets.title: Migrate to a Debug-friendly sender wrapper and derive Debug for RuntimeCommand

contracts.precondition: RuntimeCommand variants are constructible with a Debug-friendly Reply channel wrapping tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender
contracts.postcondition: derived Debug output for every variant is non-panicking and identifies the variant while Display output remains unchanged
contracts.invariant: every RuntimeCommand variant is Debug via derive and DispatchCommand retains its manual Debug impl

contracts.precondition: Reply wraps a tokio oneshot sender
contracts.postcondition: Reply is Debug for any payload without requiring payload Debug; send delivers the value and into_inner recovers the sender
contracts.invariant: Debug output is stable and never panics regardless of payload type

contracts.precondition: DebugBox wraps a non-Debug boxed payload such as Box dyn AsyncAudioSource
contracts.postcondition: DebugBox is Debug without requiring the inner type to be Debug and into_inner returns the original box
contracts.invariant: audio sources reach the mixer unchanged after DebugBox round-trip

tickets.background:
- 【Goal】Replace the hand-written Debug impl on RuntimeCommand (command.rs:161-191) with #[derive(Debug)] by introducing a Debug-friendly wrapper around tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender and a Debug wrapper for the boxed AsyncAudioSource payload
- 【Purpose】The manual Debug impl only prints RuntimeCommand::{Variant} and hides all payloads; it has drifted into an exact duplicate of the Display match (command.rs:194-221) and must be edited by hand every time a variant is added — a maintenance trap
- 【Motivation】tokio 1.x oneshot::Sender does not implement Debug (the STUB at command.rs:161 states this) and RuntimeCommand::AddAudioSource carries Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> which is not Debug (command.rs:43). A Reply<T> wrapper plus a DebugBox<T> wrapper makes every field Debug so the enum can derive Debug, the manual impl is deleted, and tracing can log field-rich command payloads
- 【Constraints】Zero behavior change: derived Debug output must be non-panicking for every variant and identify the variant; the Display impl is unchanged; existing tests (Display variant names command.rs:510-532/576-655/851-865, DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command conversion, reactor reply delivery, send_reply) must keep passing; AsyncAudioSource must NOT gain a Debug supertrait (CpalMicrophoneSource.stream is cpal::Stream, not Debug in cpal 0.18.1, so a supertrait breaks --features cpal-input and is a breaking change for downstream implementors)
scope: - src/runtime/command.rs — ADD Reply<T> newtype wrapping tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<T> with pub(crate) new()/send()/into_inner() and a manual Debug impl printing a stable placeholder
- src/runtime/command.rs — ADD DebugBox<T> newtype wrapping Box<T> with pub(crate) new()/into_inner() and a manual Debug impl printing an opaque placeholder; T need not be Debug

- src/runtime/command.rs — CHANGE every RuntimeCommand reply field from tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<.., ReactorError>> to Reply<Result<.., ReactorError>> (all 20 variants); CHANGE AddAudioSource.source from Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> to DebugBox<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>; ADD #[derive(Debug)] to RuntimeCommand and DELETE the manual Debug impl at lines 161-191

- src/runtime/command.rs — CHANGE DispatchCommand reply fields to Reply<..> and AddAudioSource.source to DebugBox<..> so from_runtime_command moves the wrappers directly; KEEP the manual DispatchCommand Debug (BackendFn = Box<dyn FnOnce> at line 225 can never derive Debug); UPDATE from_runtime_command (line 318) and send_reply (line 492) to the Reply type

- src/runtime/handle.rs — CHANGE submit() (line 53) to inject Reply::new(tx) into each DispatchCommand variant; CHANGE submit_add_audio_source (line 204) to wrap the source in DebugBox::new; submit_add_account (line 177) / submit_get_account_info (line 129) / audio helpers construct Reply::new
- src/runtime/reactor.rs — CHANGE AddAudioSource dispatch (line 118) to audio_mixer.add_source(source.into_inner()); CHANGE every reply.send(...) to the Reply::send method on the reactor thread

- src/client.rs + src/api/public_api_design.rs + src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs — CHANGE RuntimeCommand construction sites (client.rs:120 Initialize, :258 RemoveAccount, :308 CreateTransport, :391 Shutdown; public_api_design.rs:58/78/98 SetRegistration, :145 MakeCall, :189 UpdateAccount) to wrap the reply sender in Reply::new

- tests/ — UPDATE command.rs / handle.rs / reactor.rs / client.rs / public_api_design.rs test modules and tests/verify_spec_p10_1.rs / verify_spec_p9_1.rs / examples/common/client.rs that construct RuntimeCommand variants to use Reply::new and DebugBox::new

- src/runtime/mod.rs — RE-EXPORT Reply (and DebugBox) alongside RuntimeCommand; RuntimeCommand is pub (runtime/mod.rs:39) and its variant fields reference Reply, so the wrapper must be at least as visible as the enum
- NOT changing: AsyncAudioSource trait (no Debug supertrait); RuntimeCommand Display impl; DispatchCommand manual Debug; command dispatch semantics, FIFO ordering, or oneshot reply semantics

- Impact on components: src/runtime/command.rs (Reply/DebugBox/derive Debug), src/runtime/handle.rs (submit + typed helpers), src/runtime/reactor.rs (dispatch arms), src/client.rs, src/api/public_api_design.rs, src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs, command/handle/reactor/client test modules, examples/common/client.rs

- Impact nature: API surface of pub RuntimeCommand (reply field type changes from tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender to Reply) — a compile-time break for any external constructor, contained to the crate's runtime types; Debug output becomes field-rich; no runtime behavior, performance, or data-format change

- Impact response: YES — all in-crate construction sites and tests must be updated in this ticket; downstream crates (if any construct RuntimeCommand) need a compile-fix; DispatchCommand/ReactorError are unaffected in behavior

- Implementation steps: (1) Red — write the failing testUnit/testIntegration suite asserting derived-Debug behavior (non-panicking, variant-identifying {:?}, stable Reply/DebugBox placeholders); (2) add Reply<T> and DebugBox<T> to command.rs with Debug impls and new()/send()/into_inner(); (3) change RuntimeCommand and DispatchCommand field types, add #[derive(Debug)] to RuntimeCommand, delete the manual Debug (lines 161-191), rewrite the command.rs:43 doc comment; (4) update handle.rs submit() + typed helpers, reactor.rs dispatch arms, send_reply; (5) update client.rs / public_api_design.rs / m20_native_event_conv.rs construction sites; (6) update all tests and examples; (7) Green — make test; (8) Refactor — Boy Scout
- Risks: (a) changing the reply field type breaks every construction site and test that builds a RuntimeCommand/DispatchCommand — 33 oneshot::Sender sites in command.rs/handle.rs/reactor.rs/tests must migrate atomically; (b) DispatchCommand::Execute closure (BackendFn) is not Debug, so DispatchCommand must keep manual Debug — the derive applies only to RuntimeCommand; (c) derived Debug exposes payload fields in logs — intended richer output, but log content changes
- Caveats: submit() discards the caller-supplied reply channel and injects its own (handle.rs:59), so the caller reply stays vestigial — P10-4 preserves this behavior and only wraps the type; it does not redesign the channel flow; the stale targetStubs TS-001 (P0-2 resolved) and the null stubs entry on the ticket are cleaned up in Step 8; DispatchCommand::AddAudioSource also gains DebugBox (needed for from_runtime_command to move the wrapper)
- Open items: whether DispatchCommand could eventually derive Debug if BackendFn were replaced by a Debug-friendly handle — out of scope, tracked as a future improvement; the RFC (N0010) declares RuntimeCommand reply as Result<_, SipError> while the implementation uses ReactorError — pre-existing discrepancy, not changed here
- Future improvements: redesign RuntimeCommand to drop the vestigial caller reply field so submit() owns reply-channel creation entirely (removes the dead-channel pattern noted in P10-3 Boy Scout); add Debug to AsyncAudioSource implementors only if cpal::Stream ever gains Debug

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】RuntimeCommand derives Debug; every variant's {:?} output is non-panicking and identifies the variant; Reply<T> and DebugBox<T> Debug outputs are stable placeholders independent of the payload type
- 【Invariant on error】Debug/Display formatting never panics for any payload combination (full ClientConfig/AccountConfig, trait-object audio source); Reply::send still returns Err(value) when the oneshot receiver is dropped
- 【Internal state invariant】Reply and DebugBox are value-transparent: into_inner/send preserve the underlying oneshot channel and boxed source exactly; DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command transfers the wrappers without dropping the reply channel

tickets.investigation: Material evidence — (1) RuntimeCommand (command.rs:44-159) has 20 variants each with reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<T, ReactorError>>; manual Debug at 161-191 prints only RuntimeCommand::{Variant} and exactly duplicates the Display match at 194-221; doc comment at 43 states Debug is manual because Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource> is not Debug. (2) DispatchCommand (236-313) carries BackendFn = Box<dyn FnOnce(&mut dyn SipBackend) -> Result<(), ReactorError> + Send> (line 225) plus Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource> in AddAudioSource — it can never derive Debug and keeps manual Debug (449-489). (3) from_runtime_command (318-446) moves fields; send_reply (492-500) takes a raw oneshot::Sender. (4) handle.rs submit() (53-93) converts RuntimeCommand to DispatchCommand then injects a FRESH (tx, rx) (line 59), discarding the caller reply; submit_add_account (177-185), submit_add_audio_source (204-212), submit_get_account_info (129-140) follow the same pattern. (5) reactor.rs AddAudioSource dispatch (118-127) calls audio_mixer.add_source(source) and reply.send(Ok(source_id)); reply.send is used throughout the dispatch arms. (6) tokio 1.x oneshot::Sender has no Debug impl (STUB at command.rs:161 states this; confirmed against the tokio crate in the cargo registry). (7) AsyncAudioSource (audio_worker.rs:25-31) is trait AsyncAudioSource: Send; implementors MockAsyncAudioSource (derive-able: data/position), CpalMicrophoneSource { stream: Option<cpal::Stream> } (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:312; cpal::Stream = Stream(StreamInner) in cpal 0.18.1, NOT Debug), TtsStreamSource (test code, verify_spec_p9_1.rs) — a Debug supertrait would break --features cpal-input. (8) All config payloads are Debug: ClientConfig (client_config_spec.rs:136), AccountConfig (account_config_spec.rs:52), TransportConfig (transport_ice_spec.rs:70), OutgoingCallRequest (call_types.rs:48). (9) No test asserts on {:?} of RuntimeCommand; Display is tested at command.rs:510-532/576-655/851-865. (10) Construction sites: client.rs:120/258/308/391, public_api_design.rs:58/78/98/145/189, m20_native_event_conv.rs (GetAccountInfo flow handled by the reactor). (11) cpal-input is a non-default feature (Cargo.toml default = serde, tls). (12) Design: Reply<T> wraps the sender and DebugBox<T> wraps the boxed source so #[derive(Debug)] compiles for RuntimeCommand without touching the AsyncAudioSource trait
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Translatability plan: (1) replace the duplicated manual Debug match (command.rs:161-191) — which drifted into an exact copy of the Display match — with #[derive(Debug)]; the Display impl remains the single manual match; (2) name the wrappers as domain nouns — Reply<T> (a debuggable reply channel) and DebugBox<T> (an opaque debuggable box) — so RuntimeCommand reads 'variant { payload, reply }'; (3) rewrite the stale doc comment at command.rs:43 ('Debug is manual...') to state Debug is derived via Reply/DebugBox and why (oneshot::Sender and trait objects are not Debug); (4) remove the vestigial dead-channel construction in touched files where trivially possible (client.rs:391 Shutdown passes _dummy_tx) by using RuntimeHandle::submit's internal channel creation; (5) clean the stale targetStubs TS-001 (P0-2) and null stubs entry on the ticket so provenance points only at the real command.rs:161 stub; (6) keep DispatchCommand's manual Debug but deduplicate its per-variant debug_struct arms with a small finish_non_exhaustive helper if the touch is natural
planTestCode: UT: [Contract C011] Precondition — RuntimeCommand variants are constructible with a Debug-friendly Reply channel
```rust

let cmd = RuntimeCommand::Shutdown { reply: Reply::new(tx) };
fn assert_debug<T: std::fmt::Debug>() {}
assert_debug::<RuntimeCommand>(); // compile-time: derive replaced the manual impl
Postcondition — derived Debug output identifies the variant and never panics
```rust
let (tx, _rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<Result<(), ReactorError>>();
let cmd = RuntimeCommand::Shutdown { reply: Reply::new(tx) };
let dbg = format!("{:?}", cmd);
assert!(dbg.contains("Shutdown"), "derived Debug must identify the variant");
assert_eq!(format!("{}", cmd), "RuntimeCommand::Shutdown", "Display unchanged");
// Red-proof: the manual impl prints only the variant name — this assertion fails on it
let (tx2, _rx2) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<Result<(), ReactorError>>();
let up = RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount { account_id: 1, config: AccountConfig::default(), reply: Reply::new(tx2) };
assert!(format!("{:?}", up).contains("config"), "derived Debug must expose payload fields");
Invariant — every variant is Debug; DispatchCommand keeps manual Debug
```rust
assert_debug::<RuntimeCommand>();
assert_debug::<Reply<Result<(), ReactorError>>>();
assert_debug::<DebugBox<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>>();
assert_debug::<DispatchCommand>(); // manual impl still holds
UT: [Contract C053] Precondition — Reply wraps a tokio oneshot sender
```rust
let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<u64>();
let reply = Reply::new(tx);
Postcondition — Reply is Debug for any payload; send delivers; into_inner recovers
```rust

let reply = Reply::new(tx);
let dbg = format!("{:?}", reply);
assert!(!dbg.is_empty(), "Reply Debug must be stable");
reply.send(42).ok();
assert_eq!(rx.await, Ok(42));
let (tx2, _rx2) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<u64>();
let inner: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<u64> = Reply::new(tx2).into_inner();
assert_eq!(inner.send(7).map_err(|v| v), Ok(()));
Invariant — Debug output is stable and never panics
```rust
let (tx, _rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<Result<(), ReactorError>>();

let (tx2, _rx2) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<Result<u64, ReactorError>>();
let b = format!("{:?}", Reply::new(tx2));
assert_eq!(a, b, "Reply Debug is payload-independent");

tickets.background:
### Goal
Remove the redundant standalone `TransportType` enum from `src/transport.rs` (lines 12-20) now that every caller uses `TransportConfig` directly, leaving `TransportConfig` as the single transport type in the crate.

### Purpose
`TransportType { Udp, Tcp, Tls }` is a public enum that duplicates the variant names of the canonical `TransportConfig` enum (`Udp(UdpTransportConfig)`, `Tcp(TcpTransportConfig)`, `Tls(TlsTransportConfig)`). Two enums with identical variant concepts split the transport-API surface and force consumers to choose between them; the standalone enum also lacks the payloads (`SocketAddr`, `TlsConfig`) that the canonical type carries, so it is strictly less useful. Removing it makes `TransportConfig` the one and only transport type.

### Motivation
P3-1 introduced `TransportConfig` as the canonical type (transport_ice_spec.rs:28) and left `TransportType` behind as a `[::STUB::] P10-5` marker with the note that it must be removed once all callers migrate to `TransportConfig` directly. The workspace audit in this ticket confirms zero in-repo callers of `TransportType` (grep matches only the definition and its STUB comment in `src/transport.rs`). All account/transport config lifecycle work (P10-3) and public API re-exports (P8-22) build on `TransportConfig`. The migration precondition is satisfied, so the redundant type can be deleted.

### Constraints
- Must not touch the canonical `TransportConfig` enum or its re-export set (C016).
- Must not alter the crate-root re-export block (lib.rs:120-145) — `TransportType` is already absent there.
- `pub mod transport;` (lib.rs:60) must remain valid; the module body keeps only the re-export.
- Feature-gated TLS (`#[cfg(feature = "tls")]`) paths must be untouched.
- TDD: write the failing source-tree-scan test first (RED), delete the enum (GREEN), keep the suite green (Refactor).

  - [Before → After] Before: transport.rs has a re-export (lines 7-10) plus a redundant public enum; After: transport.rs contains only the re-export and the module doc comment.
  - [API contract change] `siprs::transport::TransportType` is removed from the public API. The crate-root `pub use` block (lib.rs:120-145) already excludes `TransportType`, so the crate-root API is unchanged; only the `transport` module path shrinks. Consumers must use `TransportConfig` (C016).
  - [Data schema change] None — no serialized data format depends on `TransportType`.
  - [Config/env change] None — no config field or env var references `TransportType`.
  - [Dependency added/removed] None.

**Out of scope:**
  - [Excluded item] Changes to the canonical `TransportConfig` enum or `TlsConfig`/`IceConfig`/STUN/TURN config definitions (transport_ice_spec.rs).

  - [Nature of impact] API shrink — a public type is deleted. No behavior change for the re-export set; no runtime effect.

tickets.investigation:
Source-code evidence gathered during make-stage investigation (P10-5):

1. **src/transport.rs:7-10** — The module already re-exports `IceConfig, StunServerConfig, TransportConfig, TurnServerConfig, TurnTransport, UdpTransportConfig` from `crate::config::transport_ice_spec`, i.e. the canonical config types are re-exported at the `transport` module root.

2. **src/transport.rs:12-20** — A redundant standalone `pub enum TransportType { Udp, Tcp, Tls }` (derive Debug, Clone) carries the `[::STUB::] P10-5` marker at line 14. This is the exact removal target. It duplicates the variant names of the canonical `TransportConfig`.

3. **src/config/transport_ice_spec.rs:28-33** — The canonical enum is `pub enum TransportConfig { Udp(UdpTransportConfig), Tcp(TcpTransportConfig), #[cfg(feature = "tls")] Tls(TlsTransportConfig) }`. It is the single source of truth for transport selection (RFC N0015 §12, C016). `TcpTransportConfig`/`UdpTransportConfig` structs and (feature-gated) `TlsTransportConfig`/`TlsConfig` are defined in the same file.

4. **src/lib.rs:55-60** — `pub mod transport;` is declared (line 60) and remains valid after removal since the re-export module body (transport.rs:7-10) is untouched.

5. **src/lib.rs:120-145** — The crate-root `pub use` block re-exports `config::transport_ice_spec::{IceConfig, TcpTransportConfig, TransportConfig, TurnServerConfig, TurnTransport, UdpTransportConfig}` (lines 136-139) and feature-gated `TlsConfig` (line 140-141). **`TransportType` is NOT in the crate-root re-export list** — it was only reachable via `siprs::transport::TransportType`. Removing it therefore shrinks only the `transport` module path, not the crate root API.

6. **Workspace-wide grep** (`grep -rn "TransportType" --include="*.rs" .`) returns exactly two matches, both inside `src/transport.rs`: the STUB comment (line 14) and the enum definition (line 16). **Zero callers exist anywhere in the workspace** (lib, tests/, siprs-server, examples).

7. **RFC graph** N0015 (§12 TransportConfig & §13 ICE/STUN/TURN) confirms TransportConfig is the canonical transport type; N0011 (§8 Public API Design) crate-root re-exports do not include TransportType; N0051 (§42 Validation) requires ClientConfig to carry transport/ICE and validate fail-fast.

8. **Feature gates** — Tls variant is `#[cfg(feature = "tls")]` in both the canonical enum and the re-export; the removal does not touch feature-gated code.

Conclusion: removal is a pure 8-line deletion in `src/transport.rs` (doc comment lines 12-13, STUB marker line 14, derive line 15, enum lines 16-20). No other file needs to change.

tickets.background:
### Goal
The P10-6 event system provides the complete bridge between PJSIP C callbacks and Rust async event consumers. It defines the SipEventPayload enum (all P0 variants: Registration/Call/DTMF; P1: Transport/ICE; P2: supplemental), the EventBus with split control/raw_sip broadcast channels, the NativeEvent-to-SipEventPayload conversion functions, and the Dual Client routing infrastructure (single Reactor + account_id-based EventBus dispatch). Every PJSIP callback-generated event is delivered to the correct SipClient's EventBus as a typed SipEvent struct. This is the re-implementation round closing the five ABC-inspection gaps (O-001..O-005) so every contract (C020-C024, C030, C039) is verifiable against production code.
### Purpose
SipClient consumers (UI layer, audio pipeline, logging) need observable, structured notifications about SIP state changes. Without this event system, application code would poll for state or interpret raw PJSIP callbacks directly. The EventBus provides a decoupled publish-subscribe pattern: the Reactor publishes SipEvents onto broadcast channels; multiple consumers independently subscribe and filter (via AccountEventReceiver); RawSIP messages are isolated on a separate bus to prevent control event loss. This is the primary async communication channel between the synchronous PJSIP thread (C callbacks) and the async Rust world (tokio tasks).
### Motivation
The prior implementation produced green tests that did not exercise the production publication/dispatch flows: RegistrationStateChanged never published an event (O-001), DtmfSent never fired as a timeout (O-002), dual-client routing existed only inside test bodies (O-003), the query API did not exist (O-004), and Lagged(n) was asserted loosely (O-005). The ABC Inspection Pipeline confirmed contracts' pre/post/invariants were not translated into tests of production behavior. Downstream tickets (P2-2 error payloads, P2-4 audio pipeline, P4-1 registration state machine, P0-6 FFI bridge) depend on these events actually being delivered. Leaving the gaps means contract violations are undetectable.
### Constraints
- Single Reactor constraint: global_runtime() unchanged — dual-client dispatch is EventBus-only (C039). dispatch_event/process_native_event are pub(crate) and wired into the reactor loop only when the FFI callback bridge (P0-6/P3-2) delivers NativeEvents ([::STUB::] P12-7).
- Broadcast channel (lossy delivery): tokio::sync::broadcast is the only supported channel type. No reliable delivery, no per-subscriber retransmission (N0020).
- PJSUA dependency: NativeEvent types mirror PJSIP callback signatures (pjsip_inv_state, pjsua_call_media_status). CallMediaStateChanged currently hardcodes media_status=1 ([::STUB::] P11-10).
- DtmfSent 500ms timeout may race with the real PJSIP callback — consumers must tolerate duplicate DtmfSent events (N0029). spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout is invoked by the SendDtmf handler only when P5-2 completes wiring ([::STUB::] P11-6).
- tokio::time::pause() requires the `test-util` tokio feature — enabled in Cargo.toml (test-time only, no runtime dependency change).
- No new crates; the production flow must be testable with MockBackend (no live PJSIP). Real pjsua_acc_get_info() is deferred to P4-2.

testExceptions: Exception: Real pjsua_acc_get_info() FFI call for NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged is not testable in a pure Rust unit environment — it requires a live pjsua library with registered accounts. Reason: pjsua_acc_get_info() is a C FFI function needing a running pjsua instance; not testable without the live PJSIP stack. This is not an architectural defect — MockBackend::get_account_info() (src/runtime/backend.rs:276-287) provides the identical data shape (AccountInfoSnapshot) for deterministic unit tests, and the real FFI call is covered by P0-6+ integration tests. Alternative: MockBackend with configurable get_account_info_result validates the full conversion + publication logic without FFI.

Exception: Actual PJSIP callback invocation (on_reg_state2, on_call_state, on_dtmf_digit) is not testable in a pure Rust unit environment — these are C→Rust callbacks triggered by a live PJSIP stack. Reason: FFI callback registration and invocation requires a live PjsuaBackend (P0-6); not testable without the real PJSIP stack. This is not an architectural defect — NativeEvent injection (constructing NativeEvent values directly) deterministically covers the conversion/dispatch logic, and P0-6+ integration tests cover the real callback path. Alternative: construct NativeEvent values directly for process_native_event/convert_native_event_to_payload tests.

Exception: Real-time DTMF callback-vs-timeout race timing variance is not testable deterministically — the actual PJSIP callback may arrive just before or after the 500ms wall-clock timeout. Reason: the timeout is a wall-clock timer; system scheduling makes the race non-deterministic and thus not testable in a deterministic unit environment. This is not an architectural defect — tokio::time::pause()/advance() provides a deterministic simulation (test-util feature), and production behavior is verified by P0-6+ integration tests. Alternative: tokio::time::pause() drives the deadline deterministically in unit tests.

Exception: Dual Client concurrency race (a NativeEvent arriving during client registration/deregistration) is not testable automatically without a complex concurrency harness. Reason: client registration/deregistration is a rare operation serialized through the reactor command queue, making the race window theoretically present but practically zero and not testable in an automated unit environment. This is not an architectural defect — dispatch_event is a pure function over (client_event_buses, default_event_bus, event) with no shared mutable state; deterministic routing tests cover all three branches (matching/default/broadcast). Alternative: deterministic dispatch tests; QA-phase stress test for the registration/deregistration race.

Exception: A live SIP registrar's registration timeout/error response is not testable in a deterministic unit environment. Reason: a real registration timeout depends on the network peer's non-response, which cannot be simulated without a live network peer and is therefore not testable deterministically. This is not an architectural defect — MockBackend::get_account_info() can be configured to return Err(ReactorError::BackendError) or any status code, deterministically exercising the production failure publication path. Alternative: MockBackend returns Err and the test asserts SipEventPayload::Error is published exactly once.
acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path]** Production RegistrationStateChanged flow: NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged{acc_id=1} → Reactor::process_native_event → backend.get_account_info() (MockBackend 200) → registration_status_to_payload → dispatch_event publishes RegistrationSucceeded on client A's EventBus; the AccountEventReceiver for acc_id 1 receives it. DtmfSent flow: SendDtmf accepted (reply Ok) then spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)} after the configured 500ms (tokio::time::advance) — both the synchronous return and the async event are observed (O-001, O-002). Single SipClient call-state transition events (OutgoingCallStarted → OutgoingCallTrying → CallConnected) arrive with correct EventMeta (timestamp, event_id, account_id, call_id).

**[Error case]** RegistrationStateChanged with backend.get_account_info() returning Err(ReactorError::BackendError): the production flow publishes exactly one failure SipEvent (SipEventPayload::Error or RegistrationFailed) — no silent drop, no panic, no duplicate; then SipClient::accounts()/call_state() still returns authoritative state consistent with the mock (O-001 + O-004, C021 + C024). Dual-client dispatch with an unmatched account_id falls back to default_event_bus — no panic, no misrouting (O-003).

**[Edge case]** Dual Client production dispatch: two SipClient instances with account_ids A and B registered in client_event_buses; dispatch_event(event for A) → client A's bus receives it and client B's bus does not (TryRecvError::Empty) — proving the C039 isolation invariant against production code, not a test-local HashMap. account_id=None lifecycle events reach both buses plus default_event_bus. Exact Lagged(2) is asserted for capacity-2 overflow (O-003 + O-005). DtmfSent timeout does not fire before the deadline (499ms → no event; 500ms → event).

C2: DtmfSent timeout may double-fire with a real callback — tests must not assert 'exactly one DtmfSent ever' at the integration level (C030 allows duplicates). tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] EventBus::publish() must never block — broadcast::Sender::send() is non-blocking by design (eventbus_publish_non_blocking). SipEventPayload must be Clone + Debug. EventBus must be Clone (all clones share the same Sender — eventbus_clones_share_same_sender). NativeEvent conversion must be total over defined P0 variants; convert_call_state total over pjsip_inv_state 0-4 with explicit match arms.
- [Error invariant] On Lagged(n), the receiver skips n messages and resumes from the current position — no crash or state corruption; AccountEventReceiver must not panic on Lagged(n) (account_receiver_lagged_propagated). RegistrationStateChanged with backend.get_account_info() returning Err must still publish a failure event (SipEventPayload::Error) — no silent drop, no reactor state corruption (process_native_event_registration_err_publishes_failure, C024). DtmfSent timeout fallback must not abort any ongoing call operation — it only publishes DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)} (C030).
- [Internal state invariant] EventBus Sender is shared across all Clones. AccountEventReceiver holds its own broadcast Receiver. The Reactor owns the EventBus Sender + client_event_buses map; client_event_buses is only mutated by SipClient initialization/shutdown, not by event dispatch. DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms is read once at SendDtmf dispatch time; later config changes do not affect already-queued timers (C030). SipClient::accounts()/call_state() read the authoritative ClientState, not the event stream (C021, O-004).
- [Boundary invariant] EventBus default capacity 2048 must accommodate ~100 concurrent calls (~20 events/call); RawSIP channel capacity must be configured independently. DtmfSent timeout default 500ms must be less than typical PJSIP DTMF duration; sent_timeout_ms is configurable via DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms (C030). Lagged(n) count equals the number of skipped messages (broadcast channel semantics) — asserted exactly, not matched with a wildcard (eventbus_lagged_detection asserts Lagged(2), C020/O-005).
tickets.instrumentation:

NativeEvent conversion logs info for unmapped events. DtmfSent timeout logs info with call_id and digit. Reactor::dispatch_event() logs at trace level with the destination (client_account_id or default_event_bus) and whether the event was fanned out for None account_id; RegistrationStateChanged publication logs info with acc_id and the resulting payload variant (RegistrationSucceeded/RegistrationFailed). spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout logs debug when arming with timeout_ms and info when the Timeout fires.
- [Metrics] Event bus publish count (counter, label: bus_type=control|raw_sip). Event bus lagged count (counter). NativeEvent conversion count (counter, label: event_type). DtmfSent total count vs timeout count (counter, labels: path=callback|timeout). dispatch_event routing count (counter, label: destination=matching|default|broadcast). RegistrationStateChanged outcome count (counter, label: result=succeeded|failed|backend_error). All metrics gated behind the `metrics` feature flag.
- [Error tracking] NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged with GetAccountInfo failure logs error with acc_id and ReactorError before publishing the failure event; a dropped oneshot reply on the GetAccountInfo path logs warn (the reactor must still publish a failure event — never silently drop). CallState conversion on unrecognized inv_state logs warn. AccountEventReceiver Lagged(n) logged at warn level with n count.
- [Health check] EventBus capacity check: verify control channel remaining capacity > threshold (configurable percentage). Lagged rate monitoring: if Lagged(n) occurs >10 times in 1 minute, alert. AccountEventReceiver connectivity: heartbeat event published every 30s; subscriber missing 3 consecutive heartbeats logs error. Registration flow health: if RegistrationFailed or a GetAccountInfo error is published for an account more than N times in a window, log error (registration unhealthy). DtmfSent timeout ratio monitoring: if timeout count / total DtmfSent exceeds a threshold, alert (PJSIP callback path may be broken).

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Boy Scout Rule — Translatability improvements (P10-6 re-implementation):
1. src/client.rs — the event channel field reads as a domain noun ('events'); subscribe()/subscribe_account()/subscribe_raw_sip() are verb phrases returning typed receivers. accounts()/call_state() read as 'give me the authoritative account list' / 'give me the authoritative call state' (C021 source-of-truth).
2. src/runtime/reactor.rs — dispatch_event(&client_event_buses, &default_event_bus, event) and process_native_event(&backend, &client_event_buses, &default_event_bus, event, &calls) are named, single-responsibility functions that read as 'dispatch this event to the right bus' / 'process this native event and publish the outcome'; extract_event_ids keeps the id-resolution paragraph separate.
3. src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs — spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout(call_id, method, digit, timeout_ms, event_bus) is a free function returning a JoinHandle, extracting the timer logic so the two-phase semantics (return=accepted, event=sent) read as prose.
4. src/config.rs — DtmfConfig { sent_timeout_ms: u64 } is a domain struct with Default (= DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS) replacing any magic 500 literal with the named constant.
5. Named constants — DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 500 (exists); DEFAULT_EVENT_BUS_CAPACITY = 2048 is used as a literal in client.rs:99 and should be extracted into a named constant; MAX_CONCURRENT_CALLS = 100 for the capacity-sizing comment.
6. src/api/eventbus_receiver.rs — remove the buggy dual_client_dispatch_routes_to_correct_bus (both buses inserted under the SAME AccountId 1 — the second insert overwrites the first, so the test never proves isolation); production dispatch tests in reactor.rs supersede it.
7. src/runtime/command.rs — from_runtime_command() is a single large match; split into per-variant helper functions (dispatch_initialize, dispatch_add_account, dispatch_send_dtmf, dispatch_get_account_info, dispatch_query_state) so the code reads as sequential paragraphs.
8. Outside scope: convert_call_state_with_previous is #[allow(dead_code)] until the FFI bridge wires CallDirection (P3-2); keep the [::STUB::] marker so the deferral is explicit and the function's purpose is documented.

evaluations.reason: C024 postcondition requires 'Status 200 -> RegistrationSucceeded, 4xx/5xx/6xx -> RegistrationFailed' through the RegistrationStateChanged -> GetAccountInfo -> publish flow. The production function process_native_event (src/runtime/reactor.rs:295-327) is tested only for status-200 (reactor.rs:472 process_native_event_registration_200_publishes_succeeded) and backend-Err (reactor.rs:497 process_native_event_registration_err_publishes_failure). No test injects RegistrationStateChanged with a non-200 Ok snapshot: get_account_info_result is only ever configured to Err in tests (reactor.rs:499). The 403/503 -> RegistrationFailed mapping is verified only by isolated unit tests of registration_status_to_payload (src/state/m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs:133, 154), never through the production flow. A test with an Ok(403) snapshot asserting RegistrationFailed published via process_native_event is missing.

If process_native_event's Ok arm (src/runtime/reactor.rs:304) were changed to ignore snapshot.registration_status and hardcode RegistrationSucceeded for every Ok snapshot, no existing test assertion would fail: process_native_event_registration_200_publishes_succeeded (reactor.rs:472) expects Succeeded, process_native_event_registration_err_publishes_failure (reactor.rs:497) exercises the Err arm, and the isolated mapping unit tests (m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs:133) call registration_status_to_payload directly without the production call site. A 403 snapshot processed through production would silently publish RegistrationSucceeded with zero failing assertions, so the C024 4xx/5xx/6xx -> RegistrationFailed postcondition violation is undetectable.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Define and implement the siprs-server crate specification: standalone server mode (ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode), HTTP/WS protocol layer (18 REST endpoints + 2 WebSocket paths + AudioFrameHeader binary protocol), SQLite persistence schema (4 tables via SeaORM + rusqlite bundled), semver/networking reference information (versioning policy, TLS cert info, DNS delegation), and lib.rs module/export declarations — as specified by RFC nodes N0057, N0058, N0061, N0062, N0064, N0066, N0067. This round also closes all 3 newly-flagged ABC inspection gaps (new O-001: u64 sequence-space compile-time assertions; new O-002: ServerConfig Clone/PartialEq/Eq assertions; new O-003: rusqlite bundled-feature manifest test).

### Purpose
This ticket transforms the RFC design for the server crate into concrete implementation artifacts: the config structs and protocol data structures that form the foundation of siprs-server. These types are the layer-5 (API layer) building blocks that downstream tickets (P4-3 route handlers, P4-4 WS handlers, P4-5 SQLite DAO) depend on. Without this ticket, no server-mode code can compile. The type definitions (ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode, AudioFrameHeader, DatabasePool, TlsCertInfo) are the sole deliverable; route handlers and WS wiring live in P4-3/P4-4.

### Motivation
The siprs crate core (layer 1-4) is fully specified and partially implemented (P0/P1/P2-2 accomplished). The server mode is the next architectural layer needed for the zasso ecosystem to provide a network-accessible SIP API. Multiple downstream tickets (P4-series) are blocked on these type definitions. Additionally, the ABC Inspection Pipeline flagged the prior P7-3 closure for 3 un-translated contracts (u64 seq type, ServerConfig Clone/PartialEq/Eq, rusqlite bundled) — each must be closed with a test that exercises production code or the P7-3 spec so a contract violation fails a test assertion.

### Constraints
- Crate uses rusqlite bundled feature (no system SQLite dependency) — reflected in Cargo.toml:61.
- SeaORM migration management must follow the Makefile convention from the mycute project.
- AudioFrameHeader must use repr(C,packed) for ABI stability across Rust version upgrades (compiled size 30 bytes, not 24 as originally specified — spec correction applied; tests pin 30).
- AuthMode enum has exactly 3 variants (LocalhostOnly, ApiKey, Jwt) — variant count invariant enforced by exhaustive-match test.
- ServerConfig must derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, Send, Sync for config file loading (all trait impls test-asserted, new O-002).
- DEFAULT_SIPRS_PORT = 3910 — must match the zasso ecosystem port convention (RT_PORT = 3910).
- ABC closure: every omission test must exercise production code or the P7-3 spec (no inline re-implementations, no message-substring assertions where exact-variant equality exists).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
For the P11-2 ABC re-implementation round, the goal is to close the 5 inspection gaps (O-001..O-005, all minor) so that every contract of the standalone server entry point (C062/C063/C065) is enforced by an executable test. The feature itself — ServerConfig/AuthConfig/AuthMode/ConfigError types, AppState, from_args (cli), build_router + health/shutdown handlers + run_server (server) — already exists and is behaviorally tested since P3-3/P7-1. N0061 (RFC §53) defines this entry point; this round adds only tests.

### Purpose
The ABC inspection proved that 5 real behaviors could be removed without any test failing: sealing build_router's Router return type (O-001), narrowing DatabasePool::open() to &str-only (O-002), dropping the rusqlite bundled feature (O-003), deleting the jwt-secret-required guard (O-004), and #[serde(skip)] on config_file/allowed_origins/jwt_secret (O-005). Each is a coverage gap, not a production bug. The purpose of this round is to make these behaviors test-enforced so future rounds (P4-2 auth middleware, P4-3 full REST/WS routes) build on a provably correct foundation.

### Motivation
This ticket was remanded by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after the P7-1 implementation lifecycle. The prior round shipped behavioral health/shutdown tests but left 5 contract-translation and test-precision gaps. Per the supreme law, "any behavior not covered is considered undefined and fails review" — this final round must resolve all 5 so the ticket converges and the standalone server entry point reaches Definition of Done.

### Constraints
1. No public API change — AppState/build_router/from_args signatures stay as shipped; the round is test-only.
2. All new tests must run under `make test` with the server/cli/sqlite-storage feature matrix; O-002/O-003 compile checks must be cfg(feature = "sqlite-storage")-gated.
3. No PJSIP native init required — the reactor uses MockBackend (src/runtime/reactor.rs:60), so a real SipClient is constructible in tests.
4. No new dependencies — axum/tower-http/clap/tower/rusqlite/sea-orm are already declared.
5. The [::STUB::] at src/api/standalone_server_config.rs:382 (saved-account restoration) stays tracked for P4-3 and must not be implemented in this round.
6. Default features exclude cli/server/sqlite-storage (library mode stays lightweight); feature-gated test modules must compile in their enabled configurations.

testExceptions: **Exception entry 1:** [Item] Full end-to-end server startup with a real PJSIP backend and a real SQLite file (SipClient against pj_init(), DatabasePool open, saved-account restoration, live serving). [Reason — NOT TESTABLE, NOT A DESIGN DEFECT] PJSIP FFI requires native library initialization (pj_init()) that cannot be sandboxed or mocked at this layer; DatabasePool requires the sqlite-storage feature and a writable SQLite file. Full-stack integration is only possible in the future siprs-server crate. This is NOT a design defect — it is FFI dependency isolation; every test in this ticket substitutes the reactor's MockBackend for PJSIP. [Alternative] MockBackend-based integration tests (P1-3/N0053) provide isolated server startup; this ticket's axum::test health/shutdown tests exercise the router with a real (MockBackend-backed) SipClient.

**Exception entry 2:** [Item] Binding a specific hardcoded TCP port (e.g. 3910) in tests. [Reason — NOT TESTABLE, NOT A DESIGN DEFECT] Port availability is non-deterministic — the port may be in use at test time, causing flaky CI. This is NOT a design defect — it is a fundamental property of TCP networking. [Alternative] Bind to port 0, extract the actual port from TcpListener::local_addr(), then make test requests.

**Exception entry 3:** [Item] Exercising the full Axum middleware chain (CORS + JWT auth) beyond health/shutdown without PJSIP. [Reason — NOT TESTABLE, NOT A DESIGN DEFECT] JWT auth middleware (P4-2) and full REST/WS handlers (P4-3) are not implemented in this ticket; the middleware chain beyond health/shutdown requires a PJSIP-backed SipClient for account operations. This is NOT a design defect — it is natural dependency ordering (this ticket is the minimal server framework). [Alternative] (1) health check has NO auth requirement — testable via axum::test in this ticket; (2) JWT middleware tests land in P4-2; (3) Mock SipClient (P1-3 trait) isolates middleware tests.
