tickets.title: Runtime Infrastructure — Command Serialization and AudioWorkerTask

contracts.precondition: Concurrency model established (P0-2): unbounded MPSC channel created (handle::create_channel), CoreReactor thread running, RuntimeHandle available (handle.rs:24-44)
contracts.postcondition: RuntimeCommand enum defined with all 20 variants (12 pre-existing + P0-6 M20 ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect + 4 audio-source lifecycle AddAudioSource/RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource + P7-2 QueryState + P10-3 UpdateAccount + P10-4 CreateTransport). Each variant carries a typed Reply<T> (wrapper around tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender, command.rs:37-61). DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command maps every variant to a backend execution closure or a dedicated reactor dispatch arm (command.rs:341-466).
contracts.invariant: All PJSUA calls go through the MPSC channel — no direct FFI call outside the reactor thread. Reply sender is resolved exactly once per command dispatch.

contracts.precondition: AudioMixer defined with: sources DashMap<u64, Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>>>>, next_source_id AtomicU64, per-source gain map (gains), per-source muted flags (mutes) (audio_worker.rs:144-153)
contracts.postcondition: AudioWorkerTask struct defined with spawn(mixer, call_id, frame_duration) (creates a Tokio blocking-pool task), shutdown() (terminates gracefully), and a frame processing loop (audio_worker.rs:265-327). Source lifecycle API defined as RuntimeCommand variants and functional through the reactor-owned AudioMixer: AddAudioSource (returns source_id), RemoveAudioSource (removes by id), SetAudioSourceGain (updates clamped gain), MuteAudioSource (toggles flag) — dispatched on the reactor thread (reactor.rs:119-151).
contracts.invariant: Sources added/removed at frame boundaries — AudioWorker processes pending lifecycle commands between process_frame iterations. source_id monotonically increases (wraps correctly at u64::MAX via fetch_add). Concurrent add/remove does not corrupt source iteration (process_frame snapshots source_ids, audio_worker.rs:358).

contracts.precondition: AsyncAudioSource trait defined: #[async_trait] trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; } (audio_worker.rs:25-31)
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> per source_id (inside Arc<Mutex<...>> in the sources DashMap). AudioWorker calls next_chunk on each source during process_frame and pushes the mixed frame to out_queue (audio_worker.rs:356-397). MockAsyncAudioSource implements AsyncAudioSource for testing (audio_worker.rs:37-61).
contracts.invariant: next_chunk returns 0 for an exhausted source without panicking. next_chunk fills the buffer partially (returns < buf.len()) for end-of-stream. Implementation is Send + Sync safe.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

Six omissions were confirmed — O-001..O-006 (3 major, 3 minor). Every omission must be fully resolved, and every contract (C011, C035, C036) must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Close the ABC Inspection gaps and make the runtime infrastructure layer provably correct against the CURRENT code state (post P0-2/P0-4/P0-5/P0-6/P7-2/P8-1/P10-3/P10-4): (1) RuntimeCommand covers all 20 variants (12 pre-existing + P0-6 ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect + 4 audio-source lifecycle + P7-2 QueryState + P10-3 UpdateAccount + P10-4 CreateTransport) and is exhaustively mapped by DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command (command.rs:341-466); (2) RuntimeHandle exposes working audio-lifecycle submit methods (handle.rs:214-300) that route through the MPSC channel to the reactor-owned AudioMixer; (3) AudioWorkerTask::process_frame is test-verified end-to-end (next_chunk → gain/mute → mix → out_queue) with exact i16 sample assertions; (4) MockBackend.conf_connect/conf_disconnect record observable (source, sink) side effects (backend.rs:296-307) so the ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect dispatch path is provably wired.

### Purpose
The RuntimeCommand enum is the universal command interface that SipClient uses to drive the SIP stack. Every async public API call on SipClient eventually becomes a RuntimeCommand variant submitted via the unbounded MPSC channel to the single reactor thread, which serializes all PJSUA calls (Send+Sync without exposing PJSUA thread-safety). The Reply<T> wrapper (command.rs:37-61) and DebugBox<T> wrapper (command.rs:68-87) keep the enum #[derive(Debug)]-able despite non-Debug oneshot senders and non-Debug boxed trait objects (P10-4). The AudioWorkerTask enables per-call audio processing on dedicated Tokio blocking tasks (spawn_blocking + Handle::current().block_on, audio_worker.rs:288-313), keeping audio computation off the reactor thread and the async runtime. Source lifecycle (add/remove/gain/mute) is a first-class RuntimeCommand capability that mutates the reactor-owned AudioMixer on the reactor thread (single-writer rule, reactor.rs:70-73).

### Motivation
P0-2 established the concurrency model with the base RuntimeCommand variants. P0-4 added the SipError type and M20 error converters. P0-5 added the EventBus and GetAccountInfo variant. P7-2 added QueryState. P0-6 extended the enum with M20 conference commands and the audio-source lifecycle. P8-1 implemented the dedicated audio-lifecycle dispatch variants and the reactor-owned AudioMixer. P10-3 added UpdateAccount (typed u64 reply for the add_account facade). P10-4 added CreateTransport and introduced the Reply/DebugBox wrappers. The ABC Inspection confirmed that although the implementation exists, the test suite does not detect regressions in the ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect dispatch path (O-001), the AudioWorker mix pipeline (O-002), or the audio-lifecycle reactor path (O-003). This re-implementation exists to close those detection gaps and pin every contract (C011, C035, C036) with behavioral tests.

### Constraints
- Must not break existing RuntimeCommand API (backward-compatible extension; 20 variants are all additive).
- AudioMixer uses dashmap::DashMap (not std::sync::Mutex<HashMap>) for lock-free concurrent reads (audio_worker.rs:144-153).
- AudioWorkerTask runs on Tokio blocking pool — no tokio::spawn on the reactor thread.
- No real PJSIP FFI calls in this ticket — all backend operations use MockBackend (PjsuaBackend conf_connect/conf_disconnect return Err("not yet implemented (P4-2)"), backend.rs:485-496).

ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect map to Execute closures calling backend.conf_connect/conf_disconnect(call_id as i32, call_id as i32) (command.rs:428-435). ### Goal
Final implementation round of the Observability/Security/Platform ticket. The deliverable has two parts: (1) retain every one of the 7 original ABC closures already merged in the prior round — O-001 compile-time #[instrument] source-inspection, O-002 ClientInitialized emission from SipClient::new, O-003 structural metrics feature-gating, O-004 SecretString drop-zeroization, O-005 8-metric zero-check, O-006 platform-doc include_str! enforcement, O-007 microphone-source signature + spec-examples; and (2) close the 2 re-inspection omissions confirmed against the current source tree: **new O-001 (major)** — `SipAccountHandle::new` (src/api/public_api_design.rs:43) and `SipAccountHandle::id` (:48) are public methods without #[tracing::instrument], and the source-inspection test `all_public_client_methods_are_instrumented` (src/client.rs:840) enumerates only 10 of 14 SipClient and 6 of 9 SipAccountHandle public methods, so the C047 postcondition is neither satisfied in source nor enforceable by the test; **new O-002 (minor)** — `platform_docs_contain_os_notes` (src/security/security_platform_diffs.rs:200) asserts only the OS names (Windows/macOS/Linux) and does not enforce the specific build-note keywords (MSVC, CoreAudio, CoreFoundation, alsa, openssl, uuid) the C048 postcondition names.

### Purpose
Observability ensures debuggability of production SIP calls; SecretString prevents accidental credential leaks via log output (investigating an incident should never expose passwords); ClientCapabilities enables consumers to adapt their feature usage to what the runtime supports; platform documentation reduces build friction across three target OSes. The final round exists because the ABC re-inspection proved that the C047 postcondition ("every public SipClient/SipAccountHandle method carries #[tracing::instrument]") is not yet fully satisfied in source and not fully enforceable by tests, and that the C048 platform-documentation postcondition is enforced only at OS-name granularity. Closing these two gaps is the last step before the first production deployment of siprs.

### Motivation
Without tracing, diagnosing call failures in production is guesswork. Without SecretString, any error-format! or Debug-impl on AuthCredentials leaks the password to logs. Without ClientCapabilities, consumers cannot determine at runtime whether ICE, SRTP, or a specific codec is available. The ABC re-inspection confirmed 2 testable gaps remain in the current source: (new O-001) src/api/public_api_design.rs:43 and :48 are public methods without #[instrument], and all_public_client_methods_are_instrumented cannot detect their removal because its checks omit new/id/remove (SipAccountHandle) and add_account/remove_account/account/add_transport (SipClient); (new O-002) platform_docs_contain_os_notes stays green even if the specific build-note content (MSVC, CoreAudio, CoreFoundation, alsa, openssl, uuid) is stripped while the OS names remain. These gaps block the first production deployment of siprs.

### Constraints
Must work with the existing SipClient facade (P0-3) and EventBus (P0-5). SecretString must be zeroize-compatible but optional (behind the zeroize feature). All types must be serde-compatible (behind the serde feature) for WebSocket serialization (P4-4). tracing spans must not change public API signatures — the new #[instrument(skip(self))] attributes on SipAccountHandle::new/::id are attribute-only additions with no signature change. cpal-input is optional and non-default. The re-inspection closures must not weaken any existing test: all_public_client_methods_are_instrumented is extended (more methods asserted), never narrowed; platform_docs_contain_os_notes is tightened (more keywords asserted), never loosened.

tickets.title: Generate PJSIP bindings via bindgen behind the pjsua-native feature once PJSIP headers are available in the build environment, and uncomment the wrapper.h includes

contracts.precondition: Rust FFI required to call C PJSUA library functions. Concurrency model defines reactor thread for serialized command execution. Testable form: the ffi::bindings module must expose pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pj_str_t and pjsua_call_get_info regardless of which body (stub or bindgen) compiles — asserted by the allowlist-membership and stub-fallback unit tests.
contracts.postcondition: PJSIP FFI layer created with: (1) ffi::bindings module generated by bindgen build.rs with a fixed allowlist when pjsua-native is enabled, else the stub aliases; (2) PjOwnedStr safe wrapper for pj_str_t with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing; (3) extern C callback functions enqueue NativeEvent; (4) runtime/ modules use only the safe SipBackend trait. Testable form: feature-detection, header-root-resolution and allowlist-membership unit tests plus a feature-build integration test that type-checks the generated symbols.
contracts.invariant: All unsafe code isolated to ffi/ module. No unsafe keyword in runtime/, client.rs, or config/. Compile-time lint enforces unsafe isolation. Testable form: grep-based compile-time unit test asserts zero unsafe matches outside ffi/.

contracts.precondition: PJSUA C library uses pj_pool_t for memory allocation. Callback parameters valid only within callback scope. Testable form: PjOwnedStr exposes no constructor that adopts a foreign pointer, so a pj_pool_t-backed pj_str_t can never be stored — enforced at the type level.
contracts.postcondition: pj_str_t always has Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>). Native callback pointers not held beyond callback scope. pj_pool_t memory never embedded in Rust structs. Testable form: PjOwnedStr::as_raw().ptr points into the internal Rust-owned Vec (pointer-equality assertion).
contracts.invariant: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory. Original PJSUA ptr only used as source for immediate copy, never stored. Testable form: extended pj_str unit tests assert pointer equality against the Rust-owned buffer after the binding swap.

contracts.precondition: pjsua-native is declared in Cargo.toml [features] (line 17) and in lints.rust check-cfg (line 33). Testable form: cfg!(feature = pjsua-native) toggles which body is compiled — the unit test asserts the compile-time exclusivity.
contracts.postcondition: Exactly one of bindgen-generated bindings or stub aliases compiles depending on the feature flag. build.rs emits OUT_DIR/bindings.rs only when the feature is on, using the fixed allowlist. Testable form: feature-build integration test verifies OUT_DIR output and no unexpected-cfg warning.
contracts.invariant: When the feature is off, the crate builds with no bindgen and no external C library. When it is on, generated declarations replace the stubs exactly once — both are never compiled together. The allowlist is a fixed symbol set so output stays minimal and reviewable. Testable form: allowlist-membership unit test plus the mutual-exclusivity unit test.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 specified the audio format types, PairAligner, resampler and codec policy. During that implementation the build-time bindgen generation was left as stubs in build.rs and wrapper.h because PJSIP headers were not yet available in the build environment. This work item resolves those markers by generating PJSIP bindings via bindgen behind a new `pjsua-native` feature and uncommenting the wrapper.h includes once the headers are present.
### Goal
Make the `pjsua-native` Cargo feature actually generate the PJSIP FFI layer at build time. When the feature is enabled and PJSIP headers are available, build.rs runs bindgen against wrapper.h and emits OUT_DIR/bindings.rs; when it is disabled (the default), the crate continues to compile with the hand-written stub aliases in src/ffi/bindings.rs. This closes the two `[::STUB::] P11-5` markers in build.rs:8 and wrapper.h:6.

### Purpose
Unblock every downstream ticket that consumes real PJSIP declarations — P11-9 (replace hand-coded PJSIP constants with bindgen output), P11-10 (wire real FFI call sites), P11-11 (register callbacks via pjsua_config.cb) — by providing the canonical bindgen-generated `ffi::bindings` surface they all reference.

### Motivation
P4-2 left bindgen generation as stubs because PJSIP headers were not available in the build environment. The headers can now be provisioned (vendor/prebuilt per RFC §28.1 or a system install per §28.4), so the deferred `[::STUB::]` resolution becomes possible. This ticket is `[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]`; this round must complete the build pipeline with no remaining STUB markers.

### Constraints
(1) The default build (feature off) must keep compiling with no external C library and no bindgen — the stub path is first-class. (2) The generated and stub bodies must be mutually exclusive — never compiled together. (3) Cargo.toml [features] and lints.rust already declare `pjsua-native` (added by P10-2); this ticket only adds `[build-dependencies] bindgen` and must not duplicate or reorder those entries. (4) The allowlist must stay a fixed symbol set so generated output is minimal and reviewable (RFC §27.1). (5) C038/C057 must hold — no unsafe outside `ffi/`, `PjOwnedStr` keeps Rust-owned `Vec<u8>` backing.
scope: Changes (path): build.rs (MODIFY) — implement the bindgen build script: `pjsua-native` feature detection, PJSIP header-root resolution per RFC §28 search order, allowlist configuration, OUT_DIR emission
Changes (path): wrapper.h (MODIFY) — uncomment `#include <pjsua.h>`, `#include <pjmedia.h>`, `#include <pjmedia-codec/opus.h>` behind the feature
Changes (path): Cargo.toml (MODIFY) — add `pjsua-native` feature to [features]; add [build-dependencies] bindgen; add `pjsua-native` to lints.rust check-cfg (line 40)
Changes (path): src/ffi/bindings.rs (MODIFY) — gate the hand-written stub aliases behind `#[cfg(not(feature = "pjsua-native"))]` so bindgen output replaces them exactly when the feature is on

Non-change (item): Replacing hand-coded PJSIP constants (P8-18) and wiring real FFI call sites (P8-20) are separate tickets that CONSUME the generated bindings
Non-change (why): The stub-resolution scope is the build pipeline only; constant replacement and FFI call wiring need the generated bindings to exist first and are tracked by P8-18/P8-20
Impact (component): build.rs, wrapper.h, Cargo.toml, src/ffi/bindings.rs. Enabling `pjsua-native` makes the crate build require a system PJSIP install (RFC §28 package lists)
Impact (nature): additive feature flag + build-script behavior. The default build (feature off) is unchanged and requires no external C library
Impact (response): downstream CI that enables `pjsua-native` must install PJSIP headers/libs per RFC §28.3-§28.4 or use the prebuilt/vendored path
Out of scope: PJSIP runtime callbacks, media handling, codec policy (P4-2 content) — unrelated to build-time binding generation
**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**

- [build.rs] MODIFY — extend `fn main()` so that when `pjsua-native` is enabled it resolves the PJSIP header root per RFC §28.1, invokes bindgen against wrapper.h with the fixed allowlist, and writes `OUT_DIR/bindings.rs`; remove the `[::STUB::] P11-5` markers at lines 8/11. Keep the P10-2 prebuilt-lib link directives unchanged.

- [src/build/build_script_bindgen.rs] ADD — new shared, unit-testable module with `BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST_TYPES` / `BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST_FUNCTIONS` / `BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST_VARS` const arrays and `resolve_header_root()`; included by build.rs via `#[path = "src/build/build_script_bindgen.rs"]` and declared `pub mod` in src/build/mod.rs so `cargo test` covers it.

- [wrapper.h] MODIFY — uncomment `#include <pjsua.h>`, `#include <pjmedia.h>`, `#include <pjmedia-codec/opus.h>` (lines 8-10) and delete the marker at line 6; the header is scanned only when build.rs runs bindgen (feature-gated).
- [Cargo.toml] MODIFY — add `[build-dependencies]` with pinned `bindgen = "0.69"`; the `pjsua-native` feature (line 17) and check-cfg entry (line 33) already exist and stay untouched.

- [src/ffi/bindings.rs] MODIFY — feature-gate the stub aliases behind `#[cfg(not(feature = "pjsua-native"))]` and add `#[cfg(feature = "pjsua-native")] include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/bindings.rs"));` so bindgen output replaces the stubs exactly when the feature is on; keep the `pj_str_t::null()` impl and the existing tests reachable in the default mode.
- [src/ffi/pj_str.rs] CONTEXT — `PjOwnedStr` compiles against whichever `pj_str_t` is in scope; expected no change unless bindgen field types diverge (e.g. `*mut i8` vs `*mut c_char`).
- Before → After: default `cargo build` behavior is identical (stub path); `cargo build --features pjsua-native` gains bindgen generation and PJSIP linking.
- API contract: none — the crate's public API is unchanged; `ffi::bindings` keeps the same symbol names.
- Data schema: none.

- Config/env: `CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE` (already the feature mechanism); build.rs gains `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE`, `cargo:rerun-if-changed=wrapper.h`, `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=TARGET`.
- Dependency: adds `bindgen = "0.69"` to [build-dependencies] (build-time only, not in the runtime dep graph).
**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
- Replacing hand-coded PJSIP constants (P11-9) and wiring real FFI call sites (P11-10) — separate tickets that CONSUME the generated bindings; they need the generated surface to exist first.
- RFC §28.3 CMake source-build fallback — a separate build-pipeline concern; this ticket only requires the prebuilt/vendored header root for bindgen generation.
- PJSIP runtime callbacks, media handling, codec policy (P4-2 content) — unrelated to build-time binding generation.
**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**

- src/runtime/ and src/state/ — reference `ffi::bindings` types transitively; the generated types must expose the same field names (e.g. `pjsua_call_info.conf_slot`) so existing call sites compile unchanged.
- src/build/build_strategy_os_deps.rs — continues to own PjsipDetection / BuildFlags; independent of this ticket but consumes the same feature flag.
- CI/build workflows — a `pjsua-native` feature build needs a PJSIP-capable host (RFC §28.4) or the vendored/prebuilt path; the default CI keeps the stub path.

testExceptions: - Item: Executing bindgen itself in a unit test. Reason: bindgen execution is not testable in the default build because it needs a real C toolchain and PJSIP headers, which the default CI build does not install; bindgen execution is exercised only by the integration/build job with pjsua-native enabled. This is not a design defect — the deterministic logic around the invocation (header-root resolution, allowlist, feature gating) is unit-tested in src/build/build_script_bindgen.rs; only the external-tool call is left to the build job.

- Item: Link-level verification that pjsua_* symbols resolve. Reason: we cannot test symbol resolution at the unit level because it requires a live PJSUA shared/static library, which the default build environment cannot link. This is not an architectural defect — the CI feature-build job links the vendored library, and the retained stub-alias unit tests prove the API surface stays callable in the default mode.

- Item: Byte-for-byte comparison of generated bindings. Reason: we cannot test exact generated text because bindgen output varies by clang/bindgen version; tests assert symbol presence and behavior, not exact generated text. This is not a design defect — allowlist-membership unit tests plus a cargo check --features pjsua-native compile gate cover the observable surface.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Adding `pjsua-native` to the feature set with PJSIP headers available causes build.rs to run bindgen against wrapper.h and emit `pjsua_*` FFI declarations into OUT_DIR; `cargo build --features pjsua-native` succeeds and links.
【Happy path】build.rs resolves the PJSIP header root per RFC §28.1 search order (vendor/prebuilt/{target-triple}/include first, then vendor/pjsip source build) and passes wrapper.h to bindgen.
【Happy path】wrapper.h uncomments `#include <pjsua.h>`, `#include <pjmedia.h>`, and `#include <pjmedia-codec/opus.h>` when the `pjsua-native` feature is enabled.
【Happy path】The bindgen allowlist restricts generated declarations to the symbol subset siprs uses (pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pj_str_t, pjsua_call_get_info, etc.), keeping compile times low.
【Error case】With the feature disabled (default), the crate compiles with no bindgen and no PJSIP installation using the stub aliases in src/ffi/bindings.rs — the default build must not fail.

【Error case】With the feature enabled but headers/libraries missing, build.rs fails with a user-friendly error that names the missing dependency and references the RFC §28 per-OS package list — not a raw clang/bindgen error.

【Edge case】The generated bindings and the stub aliases are mutually exclusive: exactly one compiles depending on the feature flag; `check-cfg` lists `pjsua-native` so `cargo check` emits no unexpected-cfg warning.
【Invariant】No `unsafe` appears outside the ffi/ module after the build change (C038); build.rs itself contains no unsafe.
【Happy path】Both STUB markers (`build.rs:8` covering `:11`, `wrapper.h:6`) are deleted, and `make test` is green with the feature off.

【Error case】`resolve_header_root()` returns None (not panic) when no header dir exists; the build script converts that into a non-zero exit with the RFC §28.4 hint, and the unit test proves both branches.

【Edge case】`src/build/build_script_bindgen.rs` is unit-tested by `cargo test` (lib path) even though build.rs itself is not a test target; allowlist arrays are non-empty, duplicate-free, and cover every symbol referenced by the current stub surface.

contracts.postcondition: Two-phase design realized in the reactor — send_dtmf() returns Ok(()) synchronously for command acceptance; RuntimeCommand::SendDtmf carries the method; the reactor SendDtmf handler calls backend.send_dtmf, on Ok spawns spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout per digit (publishing DtmfSent { Err(Timeout) } to the reactor-owned bus after sent_timeout_ms), on Err replies Err and spawns no timer. contracts.invariant: DtmfSent Timeout is published at most once per digit; aborting the retained JoinHandle before the deadline suppresses publication; a failed backend.send_dtmf never produces a spurious Timeout; the synchronous Ok(()) reply means command acceptance only (two-phase C030 preserved).

tickets.background:
### Goal
The reactor SendDtmf dispatch path must invoke `spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout` (src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:78) after `backend.send_dtmf` succeeds, so the C030 two-phase DTMF-sent flow is actually exercised: `send_dtmf()` returns `Ok(())` synchronously for command acceptance, and a `DtmfSent` completion/timeout event is published asynchronously on the reactor-owned `EventBus`.

### Purpose
The two-phase design (C030) was specified in P5-2 and the fallback timer implemented in P7-2, but `spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout` was left `#[allow(dead_code)]` because the reactor had no `EventBus` publish target. This ticket removes the dead-code marker by giving the reactor an owned `default_event_bus` and wiring the function into the SendDtmf handler.

### Motivation
Without this wiring the DtmfSent timeout fallback is unreachable — callers of `send_dtmf()` can confirm synchronous acceptance but never receive the asynchronous completion/timeout notification, leaving the two-phase contract unimplemented. P11-6 was flagged (INSPECTION_FLAGGED) and returned for a final defect-free re-implementation round; all three target STUBs (TS-001/TS-002/TS-004) are already resolved and the remaining crime TS-003 is a resolved/out-of-scope ORPHAN_TICKET_REF.

### Constraints
Real PJSIP send-complete callback wiring stays out of scope (P8-29 / pjsua-native FFI). acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】After `backend.send_dtmf` succeeds, the reactor SendDtmf handler spawns `spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout` so a `DtmfSent { method, digit, status: Err(SentDtmfError::Timeout), pjsip_status: None }` event is published to the reactor-owned `default_event_bus` when no PJSIP completion callback arrives within `DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS` (configurable via `DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms`). `send_dtmf()` still returns `Ok(())` synchronously for command acceptance — the two-phase separation (C030) is preserved.
【Error case】When `backend.send_dtmf` returns `Err`, the handler does NOT spawn the timeout timer and propagates the error; no spurious DtmfSent Timeout event is published.

【Edge case】When the real completion callback fires before the timer (future P8-29), the retained `JoinHandle` is aborted so DtmfSent is published at most once per digit (never a duplicate Timeout) — aborting the handle before the deadline suppresses publication. The EventBus used as the publish target is the reactor-owned bus (per-account when the event account_id matches, otherwise the default bus), consistent with `dispatch_event` routing.

The `JoinHandle` returned by `spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout` is retained so a real completion callback (P8-29) can abort it before the deadline; aborting suppresses the Timeout event. The reactor owns exactly one `default_event_bus`; per-account routing follows `dispatch_event` semantics (matching client bus when registered, else the default bus).

### Goal
Give SipAccountHandle::update_config a real runtime account-configuration update path: accept an AccountConfigPatch, merge it with the authoritative ClientState config, validate the merge (C052 fail-fast), submit RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount through the reactor, and surface the outcome as Result<(), SipError> instead of the historical silent no-op.

### Purpose
Callers (config UI, runtime policy changes) must be able to change a live account's mutable settings — registrar_uri, transport policy, register_on_start, codec/DTMF policy, registration_expires — without tearing down and recreating the account. The patch type makes partial updates explicit, and the reactor round-trip keeps the backend and ClientState in lockstep (C021).

### Motivation
P3-1 defined AccountConfig and its validation rules (C015/C052) but update_config was a `_patch`-discarding no-op because no incremental update path existed (historical public_api_design.rs:146-152). P10-3 implemented the lifecycle — AccountConfigPatch, RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount, SipBackend::update_account, reactor ClientState mutation. This ticket makes that implementation the verified, spec'd behavior, closes the silent-drop gap definitively, and adds the missing error-path tests.

### Constraints
- Public API change: update_config now takes AccountConfigPatch (must be Send+Sync, Default no-op); RuntimeCommand gains an UpdateAccount variant so every exhaustive match (name(), from_runtime_command, Debug) must be updated.
- The merged config is validated before dispatch (C052) — the reactor never receives an unvalidated config (RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount doc comment, command.rs:113-116).
- Real PJSUA application (pjsua_acc_modify) is out of scope (P8-20); only the patch/validation/dispatch/state path is implemented and tested against MockBackend.
scope:
**Scope of changes:**
  - [File/module path] src/config/account_config_spec.rs — AccountConfigPatch type + apply() (modify/verify; already implemented at :306-384)
  - [Action: verify + complete] The type is `pub struct AccountConfigPatch` with 15 Option/Option<Option> fields mirroring AccountConfig, derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Default, and `pub fn apply(&self, base: &AccountConfig) -> Result<AccountConfig, SipError>` which merges each Some field and calls merged.validate() (C052).
  - [What specifically changes] RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount { account_id: u64, config: AccountConfig, reply: Reply<Result<(), ReactorError>> } (command.rs:117-120); DispatchCommand::UpdateAccount dedicated variant (command.rs:323-330); SipBackend::update_account(&mut self, native_acc_id: i32, config: &AccountConfig) -> Result<(), ReactorError> (backend.rs:48) + MockBackend impl (backend.rs:200-208); reactor handler mutates client_state.accounts[aid].config and sends the reply (reactor.rs:278-338); SipClientHandle::submit() awaits the reply (handle.rs:104-192); SipAccountHandle::update_config facade (public_api_design.rs:167-203).
  - [Before → After] Before: update_config was a documented silent no-op discarding the patch (historical public_api_design.rs:146-152). After: a patch is merged, validated, dispatched via the reactor, the applied config is reflected in the authoritative ClientState, and errors surface as Err(SipError) — never a silent Ok.
  - [API contract change] `update_config(&self, AccountConfig) -> Result<(), SipError>` becomes `update_config(&self, AccountConfigPatch) -> Result<(), SipError>`; RuntimeCommand gains the public UpdateAccount variant (exhaustive matches in name()/from_runtime_command/Debug updated).
  - [Data schema change] None — AccountConfigPatch is a pure in-memory Rust struct (no serde persistence); ClientState AccountEntry.config type stays AccountConfig.
  - [Config/env change] None.
  - [Dependency added/removed] None — reuses tokio::sync::oneshot and existing SipError/ReactorError types.

**Out of scope:**
  - [Excluded item] Full AccountConfig schema migration / new persistent fields — the patch exposes a runtime-mutable subset of the existing schema, not a new config schema.
  - [Why excluded] The patch must only expose fields the backend can actually change; the real pjsua_acc_modify FFI application is deferred to P8-20 (PJSIP linkage/bindgen), keeping this ticket fully MockBackend-testable.

**Affected areas:**
  - [Affected component] SipClientHandle::submit() (handle.rs:104-192) — all commands including UpdateAccount flow through the same reply-await path, so reactor errors surface to every facade method.
  - [Nature of impact] API surface (new public enum variant + public patch type), error semantics (no silent success on config change), state consistency (ClientState is the authoritative config source, C021).
  - [Corresponding change needed] No — the reactor UpdateAccount handler already updates ClientState and sends the reply; the existing P10-3 tests remain the executable spec and this ticket adds the missing error-path/no-op-boundary tests.

IT: [Related tickets] P0-2 (RuntimeCommand/reactor foundation and command serialization), P3-1 (AccountConfig definition + C015/C052 validation), P10-3 (prior implementation of this lifecycle — the verified baseline), P8-20 (real pjsua_acc_modify FFI replacement — out of scope).
testExceptions: The real PJSUA account modification (pjsua_acc_modify FFI call) is not testable without live PJSIP linkage — the pjsua-native feature and bindgen headers are not available in this build environment, and the FFI replacement is owned by P8-20. This is not a design defect: the AccountConfigPatch type, AccountConfig::validate rules (C015/C052), RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount dispatch, reactor ClientState mutation, and the SipBackend::update_account interface are all fully unit/integration tested against MockBackend; only the external C-library boundary is environment-gated.

The backend-rejection path (native_acc_id unknown to the real backend) is not testable through the public facade without injecting an artificial inconsistency between ClientState and the backend — a state the reactor normally prevents. This is not a design defect: the error-surfacing mechanism itself (SipClientHandle::submit() awaits the reply channel at handle.rs:191) is tested at the reactor/handle unit level (UpdateAccount for an account absent from ClientState → reply Err), and the consistency invariant is asserted by the existing reactor tests.

The exact set of runtime-mutable fields is a product decision and is not testable as a behavioral assertion — whether a field should be patchable depends on whether the backend can actually change it at runtime, which is unknown until PJSIP linkage (P8-20). This is not an architectural defect: the patch currently mirrors all 15 AccountConfig fields, every merge path is covered by representative tests (default_is_empty, overrides_only_some_fields, handles_option_fields, updates_scalar_fields, apply_validates_merged_config), and narrowing the set is a config-surface decision, not a correctness gap.
acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path]** update_config(patch) merges the patch with the authoritative ClientState config, submits RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount, and returns Ok(()) when the reactor applies it — a subsequent query_state()/accounts() shows the patched config on the same account entry (entry.id unchanged).

**[Error case]** A patch that fails AccountConfig validation (C015/C052) returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig) BEFORE dispatch with the stored config unchanged; a reactor Err from UpdateAccount (backend failure, lost reply) is surfaced as Err(SipError) via the awaited reply channel — never a silent Ok; a missing account returns Err(AccountNotFound) before dispatch.

**[Edge case]** AccountConfigPatch::default() (no-op) is accepted and returns Ok(()) without modifying the ClientState account entry; Option<Option<T>> fields support both set (Some(Some)) and clear (Some(None)); registration state is preserved across an update (C026).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) specified the codec policy but left runtime enumeration deferred. The marker at src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69,187 was left as a stub because the FFI-defined pjsua_codec_info types are not generated until bindgen runs under the pjsua-native feature. This work item resolves it by replacing the placeholder codec list and Codec type with runtime codec enumeration via the PJSIP codec API.

### Goal
Replace the placeholder `available_codecs: Vec<Codec>` (line 69) and the `Codec` struct (lines 187–195) in `src/config/observability_metrics.rs` with runtime codec enumeration backed by the FFI-defined `pjsua_codec_info` type. The result: `ClientCapabilities::new()` populates `available_codecs` from `pjsua_enum_codecs` under `pjsua-native`, maps each entry to `Codec { id, name, clock_rate }`, and sets `opus_available` from the enumerated set, with an empty-list fallback on every non-native/error path.

### Purpose
`ClientCapabilities` is advertised via the `ClientInitialized` event in `client.rs:137` (C047 postcondition, O-002 closure). Consumers read `available_codecs`/`opus_available` to decide media capability. The current implementation always yields `Vec::new()`/`false` — a hand-maintained placeholder with no FFI backing — so capability discovery is wrong until this ticket lands. Runtime enumeration makes the advertised capability matrix reflect the actual PJSIP codec set.

### Motivation
P4-2 specified the codec policy (N0040) but explicitly deferred runtime enumeration because `pjsua_codec_info` did not exist until P8-5 generated it via bindgen under `pjsua-native`. Now that `pjsua-native` is declared in `Cargo.toml:17` and bindgen output replaces the stub aliases (`bindings.rs:22-23`), the blocker is removed and the stub must be resolved (Supreme Law §3 — mandatory stub resolution).

### Constraints
- All `unsafe` stays confined to `src/ffi/` (P3-2 architecture); `observability_metrics.rs` reads strings only through the safe `ffi::bindings::pj_str_to_string` helper.
- The non-`pjsua-native` path must compile without a PJSIP install and yield an empty `available_codecs` (C038 stub surface callable).
- No hardcoded codec list may remain; `available_codecs` is derived from enumeration only.
- C041 (PCMU/Opus only) and C042 (Opus=255, PCMU=254) policy semantics are unchanged — enumeration feeds capability discovery, not policy.
- Uses existing `tracing` (0.1) for diagnostics; no new dependencies.

tickets.investigation:
### Codec capability placeholder (the STUB being resolved)
- `src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69` carries `[::STUB::] P11-8: available_codecs and the Codec type are placeholders pending FFI-defined codec types (covers observability_metrics.rs:69,187)`. The field `pub available_codecs: Vec<Codec>` (line 71) and `pub opus_available: bool` (line 74) are set unconditionally to `Vec::new()`/`false` in `ClientCapabilities::new()` (lines 130–131).
- `Codec` struct (lines 187–195): `{ pub id: String, pub name: String, pub clock_rate: u32 }`, derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize`. No FFI backing, no conversion from any PJSIP type.
- `ClientCapabilities::new()` is invoked at `client.rs:137` to publish the `ClientInitialized` event (C047 postcondition). `tests/verify_spec_p8_2.rs` asserts `ClientInitialized` carries the `ClientCapabilities` defaults — it does NOT assert codec emptiness, so populating codecs is non-breaking.
- Existing tests in `observability_metrics.rs` (lines 421–521) assert limits/features but never pin `available_codecs` to empty; `codec_construct` (line 564) builds a `Codec` literal directly.

### FFI state
- `src/ffi/bindings.rs:22-23`: `#[cfg(feature = "pjsua-native")] include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/bindings.rs"))` — bindgen output replaces the hand-written body exactly when the feature is on (P8-5).
- `src/ffi/bindings.rs` stub_aliases (non-feature): provides `pjsua_acc_id`, `pjsua_call_id`, `pjsua_conf_port_id`, `pjsua_transport_id`, `PJ_SUCCESS=0`, `PJ_EUNKNOWN=-1`, call-state/reg-state constants, `pj_str_t { ptr: *mut i8, slen: i32 }`, a minimal `pjsua_call_info`, and a canned `pjsua_call_get_info` stub (owned by P11-10). There is NO `pjsua_codec_info` type and NO `pjsua_enum_codecs` function yet — they arrive with P8-5 bindgen and must be added to the stub aliases for the non-feature path.
- `src/ffi/pj_str.rs`: `PjOwnedStr` wraps `pj_str_t` with Rust-owned `Vec<u8>`; `new(&str)`/`as_raw()`/`as_str()` exist, but there is no read-only "pj_str_t → String" helper — `Codec::from_pjsua_codec_info` needs one, and the unsafe pointer read must live in `ffi` (P3-2: all unsafe in `src/ffi/`).
- `src/ffi/mod.rs`: declares `bindings`, `pj_str`, `callback` modules. Exposing the codec-enumeration surface here (per scope) is a `pub use bindings::{...}` re-export.

- `typedef struct pjsua_codec_info { pj_str_t codec_id; pj_str_t encoding_name; unsigned clock_rate; unsigned channel_cnt; }`.
- `PJ_DECL(pj_status_t) pjsua_enum_codecs(pjsua_codec_info id[PJMEDIA_MAX_CODECS], unsigned *count);` — `PJMEDIA_MAX_CODECS` is 256.

tickets.title: Replace hand-coded PJSIP constants with the bindgen-generated constants from pjsua.h once the pjsua-native feature enables FFI

contracts.precondition: Audio delivery is part of the public API. AudioFormat is constructible with validated fields via AudioFormat::new(sample_rate: SampleRate, bit_depth: BitDepth, channel_layout: ChannelLayout, frame_ms: u16) and returns Ok for valid inputs.
contracts.postcondition: The audio format model and AudioChunkPair are defined: AudioFormat { sample_rate, bit_depth, channel_layout, frame_ms }, AudioChunk::I16(Vec<i16>) | F32(Vec<f32>), AudioChunkPair { call_id: CallId, account_id: AccountId, timestamp: SystemTime, in_chunk: AudioChunk, out_chunk: AudioChunk }.
contracts.invariant: IN/OUT chunks are paired by a single shared timestamp in AudioChunkPair — there is no separate IN/OUT timestamp field.

contracts.precondition: AccountConfig defines a codec policy through CallMediaPreferences::preferred_codecs (empty vec = auto mode, one or more entries = explicit mode).
contracts.postcondition: Codec enforcement and fallback rules are specified: NegotiatedCodec (Pcmu | Opus(OpusConfig)) and CodecSelectionPolicy (Ordered | PreferOpusFallbackPcmu, Default = PreferOpusFallbackPcmu). Opus is tried first and PCMU is the fallback.
contracts.invariant: Only PCMU and Opus are accepted — no other codec is negotiable.

contracts.precondition: A codec policy (CodecSelectionPolicy) is defined; the auto-mode path has an empty CallMediaPreferences::preferred_codecs.
contracts.postcondition: Explicit vs auto mode is specified: explicit mode (non-empty preferred_codecs) bypasses auto priorities; auto mode (empty preferred_codecs) enumerates native codecs and assigns each a priority.
contracts.invariant: In auto mode Opus=255 and PCMU=254 are assigned invariantly; all other codecs are disabled (priority 0).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) introduced PJSIP-native state mapping, but the PJSUA/PJSIP numeric constants were hand-copied from pjsua.h. These markers were left as stubs because the bindgen-generated constants from pjsua.h are not available until the pjsua-native feature enables FFI. This work item resolves them by replacing the hand-coded constants with the bindgen-generated constants.

### Goal
Replace every hand-coded PJSIP/PJSUA numeric constant in src/error (error_design_siperror.rs:37-43, m20_runtime_command_error.rs:39-41) and src/state (m20_callstate_mapping.rs:60-76) with the constants exposed by src/ffi/bindings — bindgen-generated from pjsua.h under the pjsua-native feature, stub aliases otherwise — so ffi::bindings is the single source of truth and all three P11-9 STUB markers are fully resolved.

### Purpose
The hand-copied constants (PJ_SUCCESS=0, PJ_ENOMEM=-2, PJ_EINVALIDOP=150002, PJ_EBUSY=150003, pjsip_inv_state 0-4, pjsua_call_media_status 0-4) are duplicates of pjsua.h defines that can silently drift from the real values. Routing every consumer through ffi::bindings gives one authoritative source: under pjsua-native the true pjsua.h values are used via bindgen, and the mapping behavior (status → SipErrorKind / SipEventPayload) is preserved exactly.

### Motivation
P4-2 left the constants as hand-coded stubs pending the bindgen pipeline. P11-5 (bindgen FFI generation in build.rs), P8-5 (bindgen output) and P8-16 (pjsua-native feature) are complete, so the FFI constants are now available to replace them. The ticket was additionally flagged for rejection with unresolved STUB markers, so this final round must resolve all three markers and delete the duplicate constant blocks.

### Constraints
- The default build (no pjsua-native) must keep compiling without a system PJSIP install — the ffi::bindings stub aliases remain the non-feature source.
- The exact numeric values are owned by pjsua.h/bindgen; this ticket asserts mapping behavior, not the numeric values.
- Enabling pjsua-native requires a system PJSIP install per RFC §28.1/§28.4; that environment is not available in the default dev/CI build, so the bindgen path is validated by the IT gate, not the default `make test`.
- No public API change: convert_pj_status, convert_call_state, convert_call_state_with_previous, convert_call_media_state, convert_conf_connect_error, convert_conf_disconnect_error, convert_get_account_info_error signatures are unchanged.

testExceptions:
- Item: The exact bindgen-generated numeric values under pjsua-native (e.g. PJ_EINVALIDOP == 150002, pjsip_inv_state values) are impossible to test in the default CI build.
  - Reason: bindgen output exists only when the pjsua-native feature is enabled AND a system PJSIP install is present (RFC §28.1/§28.4); the default build compiles the stub aliases, not bindgen. The numeric values are owned by pjsua.h/bindgen.
  - Why this is not a design defect and not an architectural defect: the mapping BEHAVIOR (which SipErrorKind / SipEventPayload each status produces) is fully testable under both constant sources because the stub aliases mirror the bindgen surface exactly. This ticket asserts mapping behavior, not the numeric values; asserting the exact numeric values is impossible to test only because the bindgen input (PJSIP headers) is an external dependency, not because the feature is deterministic yet untestable.
  - Alternative verification: the pjsua-native IT compiles and runs the mapping suite against the real bindgen constants; BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST_VARS/TYPES tests pin the constant NAMES; the mapping tests pin the BEHAVIOR.

- Item: Bindgen's exact enum namespacing (module name, prefix stripping, constant type width) for pjsip_inv_state / pjsua_call_media_status under the pinned bindgen version is not testable without running bindgen.
  - Reason: the default build has no PJSIP headers, so the generated output shape is not reproducible in CI; bindgen output varies by version and header content.
  - Why this is not a design defect and not an architectural defect: the stub_aliases are required to mirror the bindgen surface, and the implementation verifies the namespacing by (a) the pjsua-native IT gate and (b) the source-routing UT entries that import the exact paths from crate::ffi::bindings — a mismatched path fails compilation, forcing the stub_aliases to be corrected to match. The item is not testable in the default environment only because the bindgen input is an external dependency, not because the design is deterministic yet untestable.
  - Alternative verification: the source-routing UT entries act as compile-fail probes for the expected paths; the pjsua-native IT is the authoritative namespacing check.
acceptanceCriteria: - 【Happy path】With pjsua-native enabled, error_design_siperror.rs, m20_runtime_command_error.rs, and m20_callstate_mapping.rs reference the bindgen-generated constants (PJ_SUCCESS, PJ_ENOMEM, PJ_EINVALIDOP, PJ_EBUSY, pjsip_inv_state, pjsua_call_media_status) with no hand-coded duplicate values, and `make test` passes on the default (stub-aliases) path.

- 【Error case】A constant missing from the bindgen output causes a compile error — there is no silent fallback to a hardcoded value. Verified by the extended BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST test and the compile-fail source-routing UTs that import the exact paths from crate::ffi::bindings.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Replace every canned or unimplemented PJSIP FFI call site left over from P4-2 with real bindgen-generated calls gated behind the `pjsua-native` Cargo feature, so the crate's SIP backend actually drives PJSUA when linked. Concretely: (1) wire `pjsua_call_get_info` so `NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged` reports the real `media_status` read from the `pjsua_call_info` struct, and (2) implement all 16 `SipBackend` methods on `PjsuaBackend` against the corresponding PJSUA functions (pjsua_init, pjsua_transport_create, pjsua_acc_add, pjsua_acc_del, pjsua_acc_modify, pjsua_acc_set_registration, pjsua_call_make_call, pjsua_call_answer, pjsua_call_hangup, pjsua_call_send_dtmf, pjsua_codec_set_priority, pjsua_call_xfer, pjsua_conf_connect, pjsua_conf_disconnect, pjsua_destroy) instead of returning `Err(ReactorError::BackendError("... not yet implemented (P4-2)"))`.

### Purpose
The stub layer (src/ffi/bindings.rs stub_aliases, PjsuaBackend, hardcoded media_status=1) exists only so the crate compiles without a system PJSIP install. The purpose of P11-10 is to make the feature-gated production path real: when `pjsua-native` is enabled and the PJSIP library is linked (P8-16), every SipBackend operation must invoke the actual PJSUA C API, propagate `pj_status_t` results, and surface real media state to the event bus. This converts the canned demo backend into a functioning SIP stack driver.

### Motivation
The previous round left the FFI call sites as stubs because PJSIP headers and library linkage were not ready. Those prerequisites have now largely landed: bindgen generation is wired (P11-5), the `pjsua-native` feature flag exists (P10-2), and wrapper.h includes `<pjsua.h>`. The remaining work is the call-site wiring itself. Without it, `make_call`, `answer_call`, `hangup`, `conf_connect`, and `CallMediaStateChanged` cannot drive a real call, leaving the SIP client non-functional once linked.

### Constraints
- Gate all real FFI calls behind `#[cfg(feature = "pjsua-native")]`; the non-feature build must keep compiling with stub aliases (RFC §28, C058) and contain no `unsafe`.
- Extend `BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST_FUNCTIONS` in src/build/build_script_bindgen.rs for each new FFI symbol (currently only `pjsua_call_get_info` is allowlisted).
- Every `unsafe` block must carry a `// SAFETY:` comment documenting the invariants (non-null, aligned, initialized `pjsua_call_info`).
- Out of scope: build detection/feature flags (P8-16), bindgen generation (P8-5), callback registration (P8-21), and hold/unhold trait methods (deferred with marker preserved).
- Every method must map a non-zero `pj_status_t` to `Err(ReactorError::BackendError)` preserving the status — never a canned `Ok(())`.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Under pjsua-native, pjsua_call_get_info invokes the real bindgen FFI symbol and fills conf_slot and media_status from the actual pjsua_call_info struct; NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged converts the real media_status into CallMediaState (Active/Held/Error) with no hardcoded 1; PjsuaBackend methods (make_call, answer_call, hangup, conf_connect, etc.) call real PJSUA functions and return their actual status.

【Error case】A non-success PJSUA status from a real FFI call maps to Err(ReactorError::BackendError) with the diagnostic preserved — never a canned success; a null pjsua_call_info pointer or an unknown call id yields a BackendError rather than a panic.

【Edge case】Without pjsua-native, the stub aliases remain so the crate compiles; the real-call path is feature-gated. The canned-value tests in bindings.rs are replaced by tests asserting both conf_slot and media_status wiring (or are feature-gated). An unknown/absent media_status maps to a safe default (None / CallMediaState::Error) rather than panicking.

tickets.background:
- 【Goal】Register all 8 PJSUA callbacks into `pjsua_config.cb` via a single `register_callbacks` entry point so the FFI callback bridge becomes real instead of a no-op: `on_incoming_call`, `on_reg_state`, `on_call_state`, `on_call_media_state`, `on_reg_started`, `on_call_redirected`, `on_dtmf_digit`, `on_call_transfer_status`. Each callback enqueues the corresponding `NativeEvent` through a pre-allocated lock-free queue that the reactor drains. Additionally resolve the hold/unhold stub at `src/runtime/command.rs:402` that this FFI-completion ticket owns.
- 【Purpose】The PJSIP → Rust event bridge in `src/ffi/` was left as no-ops (callback.rs:16,30,51,74,91,97 and mod.rs:27) because PJSIP was not yet linked (P4-2 deferral). Now that the bindgen/linkage pipeline exists (P11-5, P10-2, P11-10), this ticket resolves those markers: PJSIP events (incoming call, registration, call state, media, DTMF, redirect, transfer) must flow into the reactor as `NativeEvent`s so the event-driven client surfaces real `SipEventPayload`s instead of dead stubs. It also completes the FFI surface for hold/unhold so `RuntimeCommand::Hold`/`Unhold` stop returning `BackendError`.
- 【Motivation】Every event-driven path depends on the bridge: incoming-call notification (`SipEventPayload::IncomingCall`), registration status (`RegistrationStateChanged` → GetAccountInfo flow), call lifecycle (`CallStateChanged` → CallConnected/CallDisconnected), media (`CallMediaStateChanged` → MediaActive/MediaError), DTMF (`DtmfDigit` → DtmfReceived). The `[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]` background requires a defect-free re-implementation.
- 【Constraints】(1) Callbacks run on PJSIP real-time threads: never lock, never allocate, never `.await`, never call back into PJSUA — the only permitted operation is copying integer/char/bool params into a `NativeEvent` and pushing onto a pre-allocated lock-free queue (callback.rs:6-14). (2) NativeEvent enqueue is loss-tolerant: a full queue drops the event and increments an atomic counter, never blocking the RT thread. (3) The Rust callback signatures must match the vendored `pjsua_callback` ABI (pjsua.h:1311) so the same `register_callbacks` compiles against both the stub mirror and the bindgen output. (4) Stub-mode and `pjsua-native` mode share one code path — `register_callbacks` and the callbacks are feature-agnostic; only the bindings mirror is feature-gated. tickets.investigation:
- `src/ffi/callback.rs` declares 4 `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"` callbacks — `on_incoming_call` (:31), `on_reg_state` (:51), `on_call_state` (:73), `on_call_media_state` (:89) — each body is `let _ = (...)` (pure no-op). The design-constraint comment (:6-14) mandates: never lock, never allocate, never await, never call back into PJSUA; the only permitted operation is copying event params into a pre-allocated NativeEvent and pushing onto a lock-free queue / MPSC. The `[::STUB::] P11-11` marker (:16) covers callback.rs:16,30,51,74,91,97 and expects 8 callbacks total.
- `src/ffi/mod.rs:27` documents the `callback` module but exposes no `register_callbacks` entry point; `pub mod callback;` exists at :28.
- Vendored header `vendor/pjsip/pjsip/include/pjsua-lib/pjsua.h` defines `typedef struct pjsua_callback { ... } pjsua_callback;` (:1311) and `pjsua_config.cb` is a `pjsua_callback` field (:2612). The REAL ABI signatures differ from the current stubs: `on_incoming_call(pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pjsip_rx_data*)` (:1331); `on_reg_state(pjsua_acc_id)` (:1734, single argument — the 4-arg stub is fabricated); `on_call_state(pjsua_call_id, pjsip_event*)` (:1321, state lives in the event); `on_call_media_state(pjsua_call_id)` (:1372); `on_reg_started(pjsua_acc_id, pj_bool_t renew)` (:1715); `on_dtmf_digit(pjsua_call_id, int digit)` (:1461); `on_call_transfer_status(pjsua_call_id, int st_code, const pj_str_t* st_text, pj_bool_t final, pj_bool_t* p_cont)` (:1552); `on_call_redirected(pjsua_call_id, const pjsip_uri*, const pjsip_event*) -> pjsip_redirect_op` (:2048). `pjsip_redirect_op` enum (`sip_util.h:84`): REJECT=0, ACCEPT=1, ACCEPT_REPLACE=2, PENDING=3, STOP=4.
- `src/ffi/bindings.rs` stub_aliases define only the id typedefs, `pj_str_t`, `pjsua_call_info`, `pjsua_codec_info`, status/state consts — NO `pjsua_config`, `pjsua_callback`, `pjsip_event`, `pjsip_rx_data`, `pjsip_uri`, `pjsip_transaction`, `pjsua_reg_info`, `pjsip_redirect_op`. The same callback code must compile against the bindgen output under `pjsua-native`, so the stub must mirror the field names/pointer types bindgen emits.
- `src/ffi/backend_calls.rs` `initialize()` (:23) is `#[cfg(feature = "pjsua-native")]` and calls `pjsua_create()` → `pjsua_init(null, null, null)` → `pjsua_start()` — no config struct, no callback registration. This is the init-time call site where `register_callbacks` must be wired.
- `src/build/build_script_bindgen.rs` — `BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST_TYPES` lacks `pjsua_config`, `pjsua_callback`, `pjsip_event`, `pjsip_rx_data`, `pjsip_uri`, `pjsip_transaction`, `pjsua_reg_info`, `pjsip_redirect_op`; `BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST_FUNCTIONS` already has `pjsua_init`. `wrapper.h` includes `<pjsua.h>`.
- `src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs` — `NativeEvent` enum (:46) has P0 (RegistrationStateChanged, RegistrationStarted, CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfDigit), P1 (TransportStateChanged, IceTransportError), P2 (CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected). No `IncomingCall` variant. `convert_native_event_to_payload` (:87) returns `None` for all P1/P2. RFC §15 (N0021) documents P2 → `None` as intentional (finer granularity than the public SipEventPayload API; RawSIP covers it).
- RFC §27.3 (N0037) specifies the callback bridge: `extern "C" fn on_incoming_call(...) { if let Some(rt) = runtime::global_runtime() { rt.enqueue_native_event(NativeEvent::IncomingCall { acc_id, call_id }); } }` — confirming a dedicated `NativeEvent::IncomingCall { acc_id, call_id }` variant (carries the account because an incoming call is not yet in the reactor CallTable).
- `src/runtime/reactor.rs` — `process_native_event` (:521) and `dispatch_event` (:483) exist (P7-2) but are `#[allow(dead_code)]`; `extract_event_ids` (:570) matches every NativeEvent variant — a new `IncomingCall` arm must be added. P12-7 (reactor wiring) and P12-8 (CallDirection) are downstream; examples note "reactor NativeEvent dispatch pending P12-7".
- `src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs` — `SipEventPayload::IncomingCall(IncomingCallInfo { call_id, account_id, caller_uri, caller_name })` (:338, :185) is the conversion target; `CallId`/`AccountId` `from_u64` reject 0.
- `crossbeam-queue` 0.3 is already a dependency (Cargo.toml) — lock-free `ArrayQueue<T>` with `force_push` on a full queue enables the loss-tolerant no-block design. The reactor's `tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<DispatchCommand>` is a separate command channel, not the NativeEvent queue.
- The ticket's prior-make data is stale: `nodeIds`/`referenceSection`/`default_files`/`contracts` still carry P4-2 audio/codec content (N0030/N0035/N0036/N0040, §21/25/26/29, codec_policy_fallback.rs / audio_format_chunkpair.rs, C031/C041/C042) — none matches the callback-bridge scope; corrected in this re-make.

tickets.title: Uncomment and implement higher-level audio orchestration in the audio module once model/ format types are stable

contracts.precondition: Audio delivery is part of the public API surface; callers supply a (sample_rate, bit_depth, channel_layout, frame_ms) tuple with frame_ms ∈ {10,20,40,60} (Rust struct: AudioFormat::new(SampleRate, BitDepth, ChannelLayout, u16) -> Result<AudioFormat, AudioFormatError>).
contracts.postcondition: AudioFormat validates the tuple and constructs only valid values; AudioChunk::I16(Vec<i16>)/F32(Vec<f32>) wraps raw samples with len()/is_empty(); AudioChunkPair { call_id: CallId, account_id: AccountId, timestamp: SystemTime, in_chunk, out_chunk } pairs IN and OUT under one shared SystemTime.
contracts.invariant: IN/OUT are paired by a single shared timestamp (no per-side timestamp field); every constructed AudioFormat satisfies sample_rate∈{Hz8000,Hz16000,Hz24000,Hz48000}, bit_depth∈{I16,F32}, channel_layout∈{Mono,StereoInOut}, frame_ms∈{10,20,40,60}.

contracts.precondition: Audio pipeline needs alignment; callers push IN (network-origin) and OUT (mixer-origin) frames as (Vec<i16>, Instant) via PairAligner::push_in/push_out with tolerance ≥ 20ms.
contracts.postcondition: PairAligner::try_pair() returns Some((in_data, out_data, ts)) when |ts_in − ts_out| ≤ tolerance, drops the earlier frame when over tolerance, and zero-pads the missing side when only one queue has data past tolerance; alignment_drift() counts zero-padding events.
contracts.invariant: Zero-padding fills the missing side with zeros of matching length; drift is reported as a counter metric (MediaActiveInfo::alignment_drift), not a hard MediaError, until sustained loss.

contracts.precondition: Audio pipeline needs resampling; callers provide distinct in/out AudioFormat values with matching bit_depth and channel_layout (ResamplePipeline::new(in_fmt, out_fmt) -> Result<ResamplePipeline, &'static str>).
contracts.postcondition: ResamplePipeline::new validates the format combination (distinct sample rates, same bit_depth, same channel_layout); interleave_in_out(in_mono: &[i16], out_mono: &[i16]) -> Vec<i16> maps stereo L=IN, R=OUT deterministically, truncating to min length.
contracts.invariant: Stereo output preserves L=IN, R=OUT for every index i in 0..min(len): output[2i]==in[i] and output[2i+1]==out[i]; interleave_in_out is pure and deterministic.

contracts.precondition: AccountConfig defines a codec policy; negotiation receives a remote codec list (&[CodecInfo]) and a CodecSelectionPolicy (Ordered | PreferOpusFallbackPcmu).
contracts.postcondition: Codec selection resolves the negotiated codec: PreferOpusFallbackPcmu tries Opus then PCMU; Ordered uses CodecAutoMode priority order; no mutually supported codec → Err(MediaNegotiationFailed); NegotiatedCodec::{Pcmu, Opus(OpusConfig)} is produced.
contracts.invariant: Only PCMU and Opus are accepted codecs; NegotiatedCodec has exactly 2 variants (adding a third requires updating AccountCodecPolicy and CodecAutoMode).

contracts.precondition: Codec policy is defined; caller passes an enumerated &[CodecInfo] list and a preferred_codecs &[String] selector to CodecAutoMode::apply.
contracts.postcondition: CodecAutoMode::apply returns HashMap<String,u8> of {codec_id → priority}: auto mode assigns opus/*=255, PCMU/8000/1=254, others=0; non-empty preferred_codecs returns an empty map (explicit mode bypasses auto mode).
contracts.invariant: Auto mode always assigns Opus=255, PCMU=254, all other codecs=0; a non-empty preferred_codecs list always yields an empty result map (explicit mode).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 specified the foundational audio primitives: AudioFormat/AudioChunkPair (model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs), PairAligner (model/audio_aligner.rs), ResamplePipeline (model/audio_resampler.rs), and NegotiatedCodec/CodecSelectionPolicy (config/codec_policy_fallback.rs). The audio/ module was commented out in src/lib.rs:64-66 because those format types were not yet stable. This work item uncomments the audio/ module and implements higher-level audio orchestration that composes the model/ primitives into a usable pipeline.

### Goal
Uncomment `pub mod audio;` in src/lib.rs and deliver a compiled, fully tested `src/audio/` orchestration module (src/audio/mod.rs + src/audio/pipeline.rs) that composes the P4-2 model/ primitives — AudioFormat, AudioChunkPair, PairAligner, ResamplePipeline/interleave_in_out — and the config/ codec types — NegotiatedCodec, CodecSelectionPolicy, CodecAutoMode — into a usable align → resample → codec-policy pipeline, re-exported from the crate root.

### Purpose
The model/ layer defines formats, alignment, and resampling as isolated primitives but no higher-level API connects them. P11-12 provides the first composition point: a caller feeds an AudioChunkPair and receives a processed stereo frame (L=IN, R=OUT) with a negotiated codec. This resolves the `[::STUB::] P11-12` marker at src/lib.rs:64 and removes the dead commented-out module block that has blocked the module graph since P4-2.

### Motivation
P4-2 delivered the primitives but left audio/ commented out because the format types were not yet stable. Those types are now implemented, tested (P4-2: 26 tests in audio_format_chunkpair.rs, 15 in audio_aligner.rs, 13 in audio_resampler.rs, 10 in codec_policy_fallback.rs) and re-exported from model/ and config/. This INSPECTION_FLAGGED re-implementation round requires a complete, STUB-free delivery: closing the module-graph gap lets dependent tickets (P5-2 AudioMixer, P2-3 event AudioChunk, P7 audio subscribe) bind to the orchestrated API.

### Constraints
- Reuse model/ and config/ types read-only — do not modify audio_format_chunkpair.rs, audio_aligner.rs, audio_resampler.rs, codec_policy_fallback.rs, or m20_codec_auto_mode.rs.
- No new dependencies: rubato is NOT in Cargo.toml and ResamplePipeline currently validates format combinations only (distinct rates + matching bit_depth/layout); do not add rubato or cpal in this ticket.
- Out of scope: FFI audio capture/playback (P8-26 / P3-2 FFI), AudioMixer/process_frame internals (P3-2), cpal device I/O (P8-7).
- Mandatory process: TDD Red → Green → Refactor; all new code must be translatable (Readability is Translatability) and [::STUB::]-free.

- [Behavior] Before → After: no audio module compiled (audio/ commented out, src/audio/ absent) → `cargo check` compiles src/audio/ and crate root exposes siprs::audio::{AudioPipeline, AudioPipelineConfig, AudioOrchestrationError, ProcessedFrame}.

- [API contract] New public API: AudioPipeline::new(config) -> Result<Self, AudioOrchestrationError>, push_pair(&mut self, AudioChunkPair) -> Result<(), AudioOrchestrationError>, poll_processed_frame(&mut self) -> Option<Result<ProcessedFrame, AudioOrchestrationError>>, alignment_drift(&self) -> u64, negotiate_codec(&self, &[CodecInfo]) -> Result<NegotiatedCodec, AudioOrchestrationError>.
- [Data schema] None — reuses existing AudioChunkPair/AudioChunk/AudioFormat/OpusConfig; no new serialized types.
- [Config] None — CodecSelectionPolicy and tolerance are passed via AudioPipelineConfig; no env/config-file changes.
- [Dependency] None added — rubato, cpal, FFI remain out of scope; reuse existing Cargo.toml dependencies.

**Out of scope (intentionally excluded, with justification):**
- [Excluded item] Actual audio rate conversion via rubato — ResamplePipeline has no resample() method and rubato is not in Cargo.toml; covered by P5-2/P8-26, not this ticket.
- [Excluded item] FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame) and cpal device I/O — covered by P8-26 / P8-7; the orchestration is tested with in-memory AudioChunk buffers.
- [Excluded item] AudioMixer/process_frame internals and runtime/audio_worker integration — covered by P3-2.

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
- [Affected component] src/lib.rs module graph — gains the `audio` submodule; the stale commented-out block is removed.
- [Affected component] Crate public API surface — new `siprs::audio` namespace and 4 re-exported types; existing model/config/event types are untouched (read-only reuse).

- [Nature of impact] Compile-time and API-surface expansion only — no runtime behavior of existing modules changes; dependent tickets (P5-2, P2-3, P7) gain a concrete orchestration API to bind against.
- [Corresponding change needed] No — dependent tickets require no signature changes to model/ or config/; they may adopt the new audio/ API in their own tickets.

testExceptions:
Exception 1 — Item: Actual rubato resampling fidelity/performance (real rate conversion of arbitrary sample buffers).
Reason: The actual rate-conversion path is not testable in this ticket because rubato is not a dependency of this crate (Cargo.toml has no rubato entry) and ResamplePipeline exposes only format validation (ResamplePipeline::new) plus interleave_in_out — there is no resample() method to invoke, so we cannot test real resampling without adding the rubato crate, which is out of P11-12 scope. This is not a design defect — it is a genuine external-dependency gap tracked by P5-2/P8-26, and the orchestration is explicitly designed to reuse the currently implemented validation API.
Alternative verification: distinct-rate format validation and stereo L=IN/R=OUT mapping are covered by UT [C037-Normal/Error/Boundary/Invariant] and the IT pipeline end-to-end test; the orchestration compiles and runs with in_format != out_format without attempting actual rate conversion.

Exception 2 — Item: FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame, cpal device I/O).
Reason: This FFI/cpal path is not testable in unit tests because FFI callbacks and cpal device binding require the PJSIP native library and audio hardware, which are not available in unit-test execution environments and are explicitly out of scope (P8-26 / P8-7); we cannot test it without the native stack. This is not an architectural defect — the FFI/cpal paths have their own tickets (P8-26, P8-7) with dedicated test plans.
Alternative verification: the orchestration layer is exercised with in-memory AudioChunk buffers (UT [Normal-orch], IT pipeline end-to-end).

Exception 3 — Item: Real-time deadline behavior of the orchestration loop under a live PJSUA call.
Reason: This is not testable in a unit test because real-time scheduling under a live call requires runtime/audio_worker integration (P3-2/P8-26) and physical audio hardware, which are non-deterministic and unavailable in the test environment. This is not a design defect — the audio/ orchestration itself is pure and deterministic (verified by UT [Invariant-orch]); only the live-call scheduling wrapper is excluded.
Alternative verification: AudioPipeline methods are pure and deterministic — determinism is asserted directly in UT [Invariant-orch] (same inputs → same outputs), and zero-padding/drift metrics are asserted numerically in UT [C036-Invariant] and IT [Zero-padding propagation].
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】`make check-be` (cargo check) succeeds with `pub mod audio;` uncommented in src/lib.rs and the `[::STUB::] P11-12` marker removed; src/audio/pipeline.rs compiles; crate root re-exports siprs::audio::{AudioPipeline, AudioPipelineConfig, AudioOrchestrationError, ProcessedFrame}.

【Happy path】A full pipeline run on a valid 48kHz StereoInOut I16 AudioChunkPair (IN=1..160, OUT=101..260): push_pair → poll_processed_frame → Some(Ok(frame)) where frame.stereo_interleaved has length 320 and satisfies stereo[2i]==IN[i] and stereo[2i+1]==OUT[i] for all i (L=IN, R=OUT); frame.negotiated_codec == Opus under PreferOpusFallbackPcmu with an Opus-capable remote list.

【Happy path】Zero-padding propagation: when only IN is fed and its wait exceeds tolerance, poll_processed_frame returns a frame whose OUT side is zero-filled (length equal to IN) and alignment_drift() increments — no panic.
【Error case】AudioPipeline::new with in_format frame_ms=5 returns Err(AudioOrchestrationError::InvalidFormat(AudioFormatError::InvalidFrameMs(5))); no partial AudioFormat is constructed.
【Error case】negotiate_codec with no mutually supported codec (remote=[G722/8000/1, GSM/8000/1]) returns Err(AudioOrchestrationError::MediaNegotiationFailed) — never panics.
【Edge case】AudioChunk::I16(vec![]) flows through push_pair → poll_processed_frame producing stereo_interleaved == vec![] (len 0) without panic.
【Edge case】push_pair with an AudioChunk::F32 chunk returns Err(AudioOrchestrationError::UnsupportedChunkKind) and leaves the PairAligner queues untouched.
【Edge case】AudioPipeline::new with identical in/out sample rates returns Err(AudioOrchestrationError::ResampleUnsupported(...)) — same-rate passthrough is rejected at construction.
【Verification】`make test` passes with all UT/IT green; zero new [::STUB::] markers introduced in src/audio/ and the lib.rs stub resolved.

tickets.notes:
- Stub file:line to resolve — src/lib.rs:64 (`[::STUB::] P11-12: audio/ module is commented out; format types exist in model/`) plus the stale comment and `// pub mod audio;` at lines 63-66.
- Implementation steps: (1) RED — write testUnit/testIntegration from this spec against the new src/audio/pipeline.rs API and the lib.rs uncomment; (2) create src/audio/mod.rs + src/audio/pipeline.rs with the Initial Design Artifact header; (3) GREEN — implement AudioOrchestrationError, AudioPipelineConfig, AudioPipeline, ProcessedFrame, negotiate_codec composing PairAligner/interleave_in_out/CodecAutoMode; (4) uncomment `pub mod audio;`, remove the P11-12 STUB marker and stale comment, add crate-root re-exports; (5) Refactor — Boy Scout cleanup, verify `make check-be` and `make test` green.
- Risks: ResamplePipeline has NO real resample() method (rubato not wired in Cargo.toml) — the orchestration must only reuse ResamplePipeline::new for format validation and interleave_in_out for stereo mapping; promising actual rate conversion would be a disguised green. interleave_in_out truncates to min(IN.len(), OUT.len()), so mismatched lengths silently drop trailing samples — accepted per C037 but callers must feed matched frames.
- Caveats: AudioChunkPair.timestamp is SystemTime while PairAligner operates on Instant — push_pair must snapshot Instant::now() once per pair and use it for both IN and OUT so the C031 single-timestamp pairing is preserved; AudioChunk::F32 is rejected (UnsupportedChunkKind) because the native pipeline format is i16 PCM (C036 uses Vec<i16>); poll_processed_frame returning None is a normal state (pair not yet possible), not an error.
- Open items: whether the Ordered policy should honour an explicit user priority list from CallMediaPreferences rather than reusing CodecAutoMode::apply priorities — decided for this ticket: reuse CodecAutoMode::apply, revisit when CallMediaPreferences codec ordering lands.
- Future improvements: wire rubato for actual rate conversion (P5-2/P8-26); connect the orchestration into runtime/audio_worker (P3-2) and AudioTap subscribe (P9-2/P8-8); add F32 chunk support once a float PCM codec path exists.
