tickets.title: DTMF Specification, AsyncAudioSource & Incoming Call/Transfer

contracts.precondition: Call API supports DTMF — pjsua_call_dial_dtmf() can be called with valid native_call_id and digit string; AccountConfig::validate() rejects empty DtmfPolicy::send_methods or receive_methods
contracts.postcondition: DTMF specification defined — DtmfMethod enum has variants for Inband, SipInfo (Info), Rfc4733; DtmfReceivedInfo struct contains method:DtmfMethod, digit:char, duration_ms:Option<u16>, volume_dbm0:Option<i8>; data types implement Clone + Debug
contracts.invariant: 3 DTMF method categories: Inband (RFC 2833 in-band tone), SIP INFO (SipInfo in Info variant), RFC 4733 (out-of-band RTP event). DtmfPolicy always has at least one send_method and one receive_method — validated in AccountConfig::validate().

contracts.precondition: DTMF spec defined — DtmfMethod, DtmfReceivedInfo, DtmfPolicy types exist in the crate; DtmfSent event variant exists in SipEventPayload
contracts.postcondition: DtmfSentInfo and two-phase design — DtmfSentInfo { method, digit, status: Result<(), SentDtmfError>, pjsip_status } defined; send_dtmf() returns Ok(()) synchronously for command acceptance; DtmfSent event fires asynchronously on completion or timeout
contracts.invariant: 500ms default timeout (DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS) for DtmfSent fallback when PJSIP callback unavailable; configurable via DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms

contracts.precondition: Audio subscribe uses sources — AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource+Send>; AsyncAudioSource trait defined with async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize
contracts.postcondition: AsyncAudioSource trait with RPITIT — async fn next_chunk in trait definition (currently #[async_trait] desugaring). ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derived for all T: AsyncAudioSource + Send. SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> provided for synchronous sources.
contracts.invariant: ErasedAudioSource auto-derived for every AsyncAudioSource implementor — blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T must compile. SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send.

contracts.precondition: Call API defined — IncomingCallInfo, ReferRequest, TransferInfo event types exist in SipEventPayload; CallEntry state machine creates entries on incoming INVITE
contracts.postcondition: IncomingCall struct { from_uri, to_uri, display_name, headers, offered_codecs, has_early_media } defined; optional auto-reject timer configurable in account config; ReferRequest { refer_to, referred_by, replaces? } creation from SIP REFER; blind transfer NOTIFY → TransferCompleted event
contracts.invariant: Blind transfer (REFER without Replaces header) is first-class — ReferRequest::replaces is Option; transfer completion always emits TransferCompleted event via NOTIFY subscription state

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

- 【Goal】Define and implement the DTMF specification (DtmfMethod, DtmfReceivedInfo with the method:DtmfMethod field and contract-correct Option<u16>/Option<i8> field types), the AsyncAudioSource adapter types (ErasedAudioSource, SyncAudioSource, SyncSourceAdapter<T>), and the IncomingCall / REFER-transfer types (IncomingCall, IncomingCallConfig, ReferRequest.replaces, TransferInfo) per RFC nodes N0028 / N0032 / N0048. Close the 4 ABC inspection omissions (O-001..O-004) and resolve the TS-003 orphan-ticket crime in src/config/versioning_policy.rs so the ticket survives a full make → plan → start → review → resolve cycle this time.
- 【Purpose】Provide type-safe DTMF signalling primitives for SIP call control (send + receive with DtmfPolicy validation). Enable downstream crates to implement custom async audio sources for AudioMixer via the SyncAudioSource → SyncSourceAdapter bridge and the ErasedAudioSource dynamic-dispatch wrapper. Expose incoming call metadata (from_uri, to_uri, display_name, headers, offered_codecs, has_early_media) and REFER-based transfer capabilities (ReferRequest.replaces, TransferCompleted) to application code as typed SipEventPayload variants.
- 【Motivation】The ABC Inspection Pipeline remanded P8-4 with one critical omission (O-001: ReferRequest.replaces missing and zero tests construct ReferRequest/TransferInfo, so the C049 invariant and acceptance criteria are unenforced), one major (O-002: DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms widened to Option<u64> and volume_dbm0 to Option<i32> vs the contract Option<u16>/Option<i8>, and no None/0/MAX edge tests), and two minor (O-003: no SipEventPayload::DtmfSent construction test; O-004: no 65536-sample SyncAudioSource boundary test). The versioning_policy.rs STUB (TS-003) is an orphaned ticket reference that must be resolved this round. Every contract (C029/C030/C033/C049) must be translated into precise test assertions so that removing any contract behavior fails a test.
- 【Constraints】MSRV 1.95 — RPITIT is stable but the existing AsyncAudioSource uses #[async_trait] for Box<dyn> compatibility in AudioMixer; the ErasedAudioSource blanket impl provides the dynamic-dispatch path without refactoring existing implementors. Do NOT add new crate dependencies — all required derives (Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq) are std. Keep the canonical 4-variant DtmfMethod (Rfc2833, Rfc4733, Info, Inband) from account_config_spec.rs; leave the separate 2-variant DtmfMethod in m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs intact to avoid breaking DtmfSentInfo consumers (unification is an open item, not a forced change). Maintain backward compatibility with existing DtmfReceivedInfo consumers (m20_native_event_conv.rs constructs with None/None, so field-type narrowing is compatible). ReferRequest gains the additive replaces: Option<String> field; all struct-literal construction sites must add it.

FFI wiring needs a live PJSIP stack; RPITIT refactor risks the working AudioMixer integration; attended transfer needs multi-call semantics; DtmfMethod unification would break DtmfSentInfo consumers (P7-2 tests). Each is a separate, larger change better owned by a dedicated ticket.

AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk and ErasedAudioSource::next_chunk return 0 when the source is exhausted and never panic. - 【Invariant on error】DTMF method validation helpers (DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed) return bool and never panic; empty-policy rejection lives in AccountConfig::validate() and returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig). SyncSourceAdapter with an exhausted inner source returns 0, never garbage. - 【Internal state invariant】ErasedAudioSource blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> compiles for every concrete source type — no manual per-type impl required. SyncSourceAdapter<T> implements AsyncAudioSource + Send exactly when T: SyncAudioSource + Send. DtmfReceivedInfo / ReferRequest / TransferInfo / IncomingCall implement Clone + Debug (compile-time verified); DtmfMethod implements Clone + Copy + Debug + PartialEq + Eq. tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvement plan (Boy Scout Rule — leave code cleaner than found):
- Function names as verb phrases: DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed already read as verbs — keep. VersionPolicy methods must be verbs: classify_change(), requires_changelog(), current_phase() — never generic names like process() or check().
- Variable names as domain concepts: DtmfReceivedInfo fields already use SIP domain terms (method, digit, duration_ms, volume_dbm0). ReferRequest.replaces is the domain term for the Replaces header — no generic option. VersionPolicy must name the semver concepts (phase, change_kind, changelog) not raw strings.
- One function one responsibility: VersionPolicy::classify_change answers only "what kind of change" — CHANGELOG gating is a separate method requires_changelog(). Do not merge classification with release automation.
- Hardcoded values as named constants: DEFAULT_AUTO_REJECT_TIMEOUT_MS (incoming_call_refer.rs:36) and DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS (m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:64) already exist — keep. Any new versioning thresholds become named constants in versioning_policy.rs.
- No error swallowing: AccountConfig::validate errors propagate via ?. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes errors on the EventBus instead of log-and-continue. VersionPolicy returns typed errors for invalid classifications.
- Proactive cleanups in touched files: update the stale [::STUB::] P0-1 reference in versioning_policy.rs (resolved by implementation); re-scope the microphone STUB to MUST RESOLVE with the cpal constraint reason instead of leaving a misleading P8-4 reference that would later read as a completed-ticket staleness crime; in event_model_payload_bus.rs, align the DtmfReceivedInfo doc comment with the narrowed Option<u16>/Option<i8> types and add the replaces field doc to ReferRequest.

foundOmissions.recommendation: In dtmf_sent_timeout_fallback_publishes_timeout (src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:111-134), after receiving the event, assert ev.meta.call_id == Some(CallId::from_u64(1)) to satisfy the P8-4 IT test plan item 'assert the event carries the call_id and digit' for the C030 DtmfSent timeout fallback.

evaluations.reason: C030 postcondition requires 'DtmfSent event fires asynchronously on completion or timeout' and the P8-4 IT test plan (Layer-2 DtmfSent timeout fallback) explicitly requires 'assert the event carries the call_id and digit'. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes the event with EventMeta::new(0, None, Some(call_id)) at src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:89, but dtmf_sent_timeout_fallback_publishes_timeout (src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:111-134) only matches ev.payload and asserts info.digit/status/pjsip_status, never inspecting ev.meta.call_id — if the call_id were dropped from the published event (Some(call_id) -> None), every test would still pass. tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal (original)
Establish the siprs crate's public identity as a safe asynchronous SIP audio client library. Define SipClient as the top-level facade that integrates with P0-2's CoreReactor/RuntimeHandle/RuntimeCommand infrastructure.

### Purpose (original)
Provide Rust application code with a safe, async-native facade over PJSUA SIP functionality, limited to audio-only voice communication. This crate exists to eliminate unsafe FFI boilerplate and deliver SIP calling capabilities through idiomatic Rust APIs — Result propagation, tokio async/await, typed events, and structured configuration.

### Motivation (original)
P0-3 is the gateway ticket that establishes the crate's architectural identity before downstream tickets implement specific sub-systems: error types (P0-4), event system (P0-5), FFI layer (P0-6), audio pipeline (P1+). Without a defined SipClient + ClientConfig, no downstream implementation has a cohesive host. This ticket crystallizes the purpose defined in RFC 1 (§1) into concrete public API surface.

### Constraints (original)
- Audio-only: no video API surface (RFC §1, §2). Enforced by compile-time assertions.
- All async public APIs must return Result<T, SipError> (RFC §1 constraint on N0001).
- PJSIP v2.x via FFI only — no raw socket-level SIP stack.
- Single crate with modular internal structure (RFC §6, C009).
- Shutdown must be cancellation-safe and idempotent (RFC §32, C044).
- SecretString for password storage (RFC §35-36, C048).
- Microphone input is optional via cpal-input feature flag (RFC §40, C051).
- MSRV 1.95, OS targets per RFC §4 (C006).

### Goal (re-implementation round)
Make the crate identity verifiable and regression-proof: the facade `SipClient` + `ClientConfig` must exist as typed, validated, audio-only API surface, and the test suite must detect any violation of the 15 RFC §1 contracts. Concretely: all four ABC findings (O-001 `assert_sync::<SipClient>()`, O-002 `metrics` feature presence, O-003 `tls`/`srtp` independence, O-004 `std::thread::JoinHandle<()>` type assertion) are closed by new test assertions, and `make test` stays green (baseline 647 unit + 37 integration + 1 doc-test).

### Purpose (why this exists)
The crate exists to eliminate unsafe PJSUA FFI boilerplate and deliver SIP voice calling through idiomatic Rust — `Result<T, SipError>` propagation, tokio async/await, typed events, structured configuration. This ticket defines and locks the crate's public identity so downstream tickets (P0-4 error, P0-5 event, P0-6 FFI, P1+ audio) have a stable host. The ABC round re-confirms that identity through precise test assertions rather than broad ones.

### Motivation (why now)
The ABC Inspection Pipeline (criteria A contract-translation, B violation-detection, C test-precision) found 4 violations in the prior P0-3 implementation: the `Sync` half of `SipClient: Send + Sync` was unenforced (O-001), `metrics` feature presence was untested (O-002), tls/srtp feature independence was untested (O-003), and the `std::thread` reactor model was not type-pinned (O-004). These are regression gaps, not new features: without them, future refactors could silently break the crate identity. This ticket is remanded to close the gaps and re-verify all 15 contracts.

### Constraints (re-implementation round boundaries)
- Audio-only: no video API surface (RFC §1/§2, C001 invariant) — enforced by compile-time tests.
- All async public APIs return `Result<T, SipError>` (RFC §1, N0001 global invariant).
- PJSIP v2.x (pinned 2.17, RFC §4) via FFI only; no raw socket-level SIP stack.
- Single crate, modular internal structure (RFC §6, C009 invariant).
- Shutdown cancellation-safe and idempotent (RFC §32, C044 invariant).
- `SecretString` (zeroize) for password storage (RFC §35-36, C048 invariant).
- Microphone optional via `cpal-input` feature (RFC §40, C051 invariant).
- MSRV 1.95; OS targets Windows x86_64, macOS arm64, Ubuntu x86_64 (RFC §4, C006 invariant).
- No new dependencies and no public API changes in this round — test-hardening only.

API contract change: New public types SipClient, ClientConfig, AccountConfig, TransportConfig, SipError, SipEvent. These are additive — no existing API breaks. RuntimeCommand config field transitions from String to ClientConfig (backward-compatible via From impl).
Data schema change: RuntimeCommand::Initialize transitions from { config: String } to { config: ClientConfig } — serialization format changes when serde feature enabled.

Config/env change: ClientConfig replaces BootConfig (P0-2). BootConfig::config: String becomes ClientConfig with typed fields. No environment variables introduced in P0-3 — config is programmatic only.
Dependency added: No crates added in P0-3. Dependencies (tokio, thiserror) already declared in Cargo.toml via P0-1/P0-2.

Out of scope: SipClient method implementations beyond new/shutdown (account registration, call make/answer/hangup, DTMF send, audio subscribe) are deferred to downstream tickets P0-4 through P1+. This ticket establishes the facade skeleton only.
Out of scope: PJSIP FFI bindings — deferred to P0-6. Backend trait already defined in P0-2 runtime/backend.rs. SipClient delegates to RuntimeCommand which delegates to Backend.

Affected: runtime/state.rs (ClientState) — SipClient manages ClientState through RuntimeHandle. Nature: API surface (new public facade wrapping existing runtime). Response: No changes to runtime internals needed — SipClient is an additive layer.

**Scope of changes (re-implementation round — ABC closures on the existing facade):**
  - [File/module path] src/client.rs — **modify** (test + helper closure) — O-001: widen `_assert_send_sync` (line 212) to `where SipClient: Send + Sync`, and add `fn assert_sync<T: Sync>() {}; assert_sync::<SipClient>();` to `sip_client_is_send` (line 298). O-002: extend `tracing_and_metrics_specified` (line 383) to also `assert!(manifest.contains("metrics"))`. Before: `_assert_send_sync` constrains only `Send`; `tracing_and_metrics_specified` checks only `tracing`. After: `Send + Sync` both asserted; `metrics` feature presence asserted.
  - [File/module path] src/runtime/reactor.rs — **modify** (test closure) — O-004: in `reactor_spawn_creates_thread` (line 178) add `let _: std::thread::JoinHandle<()> = join;`. Before: only `join.join()`. After: compile-time type assertion pins the `std::thread` model.
  - [File/module path] src/config.rs — **no production change** — existing `ClientConfig` + builder + `validate()` (host non-empty, port != 0, user_agent ≤ 256) already satisfies the boundary contract; only additional boundary tests (`user_agent_256_bytes_boundary`) are added.
  - [File/module path] src/lib.rs — **verify-only** — module declarations for `client/config/account/call/transport/event/error/runtime/api/state/ffi/security/build/tests/model` are already `pub mod`; the new spec re-verifies them against RFC §6 (C009).
  - [File/module path] Cargo.toml — **verify-only** — features `tls`, `srtp`, `metrics`, `cpal-input`, `zeroize` already declared; new tests `features_independently_selectable` (O-003) and `metrics_optional_feature` lock the independence/optionality invariants.
  - [API contract change] None breaking — the facade API (`SipClient`, `ClientConfig`, `SipError`, `SipEvent`) is unchanged; this round only hardens the test suite against regression.
  - [Data schema change] None — `RuntimeCommand::Initialize { config: ClientConfig }` serialization is unchanged.
  - [Config/env change] None — no environment variables introduced; config stays programmatic.
  - [Dependency added/removed] None — no new crates; the existing `tokio`, `thiserror`, `tracing`, `zeroize` dependency set is untouched.

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - [Excluded item] PJSIP FFI bindings (`src/ffi/`, `PjsuaBackend`) — deferred to P0-6; `MockBackend` remains the active backend. Why: FFI requires bindgen + library linkage that is deliberately sequenced after the facade identity is locked.
  - [Excluded item] Account/Call/Transport lifecycle methods (`make_call`, `answer_call`, `hangup`, `set_registration`) — deferred to P3-1/P5-1; their `[::STUB::]` markers remain in `src/call.rs`, `src/account.rs`, `src/transport.rs`.
  - [Excluded item] Event-system semantics (`SipEventPayload` variants, EventBus routing) — deferred to P0-5; this ticket only exercises the `subscribe*` accessors.
  - [Excluded item] Video, Tauri integration, HTTP/WS server mode (RFC §52) — out of crate scope by RFC §1/§2 (C001/C004 invariants).

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - [Affected component] `src/runtime/state.rs` (`ClientState`, `AccountEntry`, `CallEntry`) — Nature: data-format / API-surface adjacency — the facade owns `ClientState` via `RuntimeHandle`; no change required because the facade is additive. Response: N — only regression tests confirm `initialized` flag semantics.
  - [Affected component] `src/error/error_design_siperror.rs` (`SipError`/`SipErrorKind`) — Nature: API surface — `ClientConfig::validate()` and `SipClient` methods return these errors; no change required. Response: N — P0-4 (and its re-make P6-2) owns the error-type surface.
  - [Affected component] `src/runtime/backend.rs` (`SipBackend` trait, `MockBackend`) — Nature: runtime behavior — the facade dispatches `RuntimeCommand` through `DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command` to `backend.initialize`. Response: N — P0-6 replaces `MockBackend` with `PjsuaBackend`.
  - [Affected component] `src/config.rs` re-exports (`AccountConfig`, `TransportConfig`, `ServerConfig`) — Nature: API surface — already re-exported; no change required. Response: N.

testExceptions: Exception: Video API absence is a structural invariant, cannot test as runtime assertion — Reason: The crate purpose explicitly excludes video (RFC §1). No video-related types exist in any src/ file. This is a compile-time property verified by the type system and module visibility. Any future addition of video types would fail the compile-time invariant tests defined in testUnit. This is NOT an architectural defect — the RFC deliberately scopes to audio-only, and the type system enforces this at compile time. Alternative verification: compile-time invariant checks in testUnit (UT: [Boundary] Audio-only API surface, UT: [Invariant] No video types in public module exports).

Exception: SipClient::new returning Result is a type-level invariant, cannot test as individual runtime assertion — Reason: The function signature SipClient::new(config: ClientConfig) -> Result<(Self, Receiver<SipEvent>), SipError> is enforced by the Rust compiler at compile time — every caller must handle both Ok and Err. The Err branch IS tested in testUnit for invalid config. Alternative verification: compile_fail tests in testUnit cover the error path at the type level. This is NOT an architectural defect — returning Result from fallible operations is idiomatic Rust design.

Exception: All public async fn signatures returning Result<T, SipError> cannot test individually at runtime — Reason: This architectural invariant is enforced by the Rust compiler and verified by compile-time tests in testUnit. Runtime testing of each method's specific error return path requires downstream tickets (P0-4 for SipError variants, P0-5 for event types, P0-6 for FFI integration). This ticket establishes the convention and verifies it at compile time. This is not a defect — this is a deliberate design choice for the facade layer.

**Exception entry — CoreReactor::spawn is the single reactor-thread factory**
- [Item] The invariant "exactly one reactor thread exists per SipClient, created only via `CoreReactor::spawn`" **cannot test** as a single runtime assertion: other code could spawn additional threads, and the reactor thread terminates on shutdown, so a liveness check alone cannot assert exclusivity.
- [Reason] This is a crate-wide *structural* property, not a single-function behavior. A runtime test can observe the reactor it spawns (`JoinHandle`, `is_terminated`) but cannot observe threads created elsewhere. This is **not testable** as one assertion, yet it is NOT an architectural defect: the thread *factory* is fully testable (O-004 type assertion + `"siprs-reactor"` thread name), and only the exclusivity of the factory is a source-review property. Stating it is "not a defect" because the testable part is fully covered by testUnit.
- [Alternative verification] (1) O-004 closure: `let _: std::thread::JoinHandle<()> = join;` in `reactor_spawn_creates_thread` proves `spawn` uses `std::thread`. (2) `make stubs` / source review enforces that `thread::Builder`/`thread::spawn` appear only in `src/runtime/reactor.rs`. (3) Integration tests join the `JoinHandle` and assert `is_terminated()` to prove the reactor thread lifecycle.
acceptanceCriteria: [Happy path] SipClient::new is called with a valid ClientConfig — returns Ok(SipClient) with initialized CoreReactor. All five module declarations (client, config, account, call, transport) are active in lib.rs. SipClient::shutdown() terminates cleanly. The compile-time invariant tests pass (no video types, all APIs return Result, SipClient is Send+Sync).
[Error case] SipClient::new is called with empty sip_proxy_host — returns Err(SipError::InvalidConfig("sip_proxy_host must not be empty")). CoreReactor is NOT spawned. No orphaned resources.

[Edge case] SipClient::shutdown() is called twice — first call succeeds (returns Ok(())), second call is a no-op (also returns Ok(()), verifying C044: Shutdown is idempotent). Calling any method after shutdown returns Err(SipError::Shutdown).

**[Happy path] — Crate identity complete; all invariant tests green**
- `make test` passes: 647+ unit, 37+ integration, doc-tests — all green, zero warnings.
- `SipClient::new(valid ClientConfig)` returns `Ok((SipClient, broadcast::Receiver<SipEvent>))`; `client.is_terminated() == false`; `client.handle()` exposes a live `RuntimeHandle`.
- `SipClient::shutdown()` returns `Ok(())` and terminates the reactor within 5s.
- `src/lib.rs` declares all RFC §6 modules as `pub mod` (client, config, account, call, transport, event, error, runtime, api, state, ffi, security, build, tests, model).
- All four ABC closures pass: O-001 `assert_sync::<SipClient>()`, O-002 `manifest.contains("metrics")`, O-003 `features_independently_selectable`, O-004 `let _: std::thread::JoinHandle<()> = join;`.

**[Error case] — Invalid configuration rejected; no orphaned resources**
- `SipClient::new` with empty `sip_proxy_host` returns `Err(SipError)` with `kind == SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig` and message containing "empty".
- `sip_proxy_port(0)` and `user_agent` > 256 bytes are likewise rejected by `ClientConfig::validate()`.
- On construction failure the reactor is NOT spawned: no `siprs-reactor` thread leaks, no command-channel resources remain, and no half-constructed `SipClient` is observable (the `Err` path returns before `Self` is built).

**[Edge case] — Idempotent shutdown and boundary values**
- `shutdown()` called twice: both return `Ok(())`; the second is a no-op (C044 invariant).
- `sip_proxy_port(65535)` (max `u16`) accepted; `0` rejected; 256-byte `user_agent` accepted; 257-byte rejected.
- `subscribe_raw_sip()` returns `None` when raw SIP is disabled, `Some(receiver)` when enabled — the Option boundary is exercised both ways.
- Feature boundary: `metrics`, `cpal-input`, `zeroize` are each selectable without being in `default = [...]`; `tls` and `srtp` are independently selectable (C003 invariant).

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] P0-2 CoreReactor must be initialized before SipClient accepts commands — SipClient::new spawns CoreReactor via RuntimeHandle and blocks until initialization confirms. After successful construction, initialized == true.
- [Error invariant] On SipClient::new failure, no resources leak — If CoreReactor spawn fails or initialization returns Err, all allocated resources (channels, threads) must be cleaned up. No orphaned threads.
- [Internal state invariant] SipClient must hold a valid RuntimeHandle at all times after construction — RuntimeHandle is protected by Arc and cannot be invalidated externally. Drop order: SipClient first, then RuntimeHandle.
- [Boundary invariant] ClientConfig fields must pass validation before construction — sip_proxy_host must be non-empty, sip_proxy_port in [1, 65535], user_agent max 256 bytes, credentials password must use SecretString for zeroization on drop.

- [Normal condition] `SipClient::new` returns `Ok` only after the reactor thread is spawned and `backend.initialize(&config)` succeeds; the returned `RuntimeHandle.is_terminated() == false`. The facade never hands back a client whose reactor is down (C002 precondition).
- [Error invariant] On `SipClient::new` failure (invalid config or spawn error), no resources leak: the `Err` path returns before `Self` is constructed, the command-channel sender is dropped, and no `siprs-reactor` thread remains orphaned (acceptance error case).
- [Internal state invariant] `SipClient` holds `Arc<RuntimeHandle>` + `EventBus` + `ClientConfig` for its whole lifetime; `handle()` always returns a live handle; drop order is `SipClient` first (dropping `EventBus` receivers) then `RuntimeHandle`.
- [Boundary invariant] `ClientConfig.validate()` enforces `sip_proxy_host` non-empty, `sip_proxy_port ∈ [1, 65535]` (the `u16` type makes >65535 unrepresentable), `user_agent ≤ 256` bytes; `AuthCredentials.password` is `SecretString` (zeroized on drop, never visible in `Debug`).

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvements for P0-3:
1. lib.rs: Uncomment module declarations — convert [::STUB::] comments into active pub mod statements. Each module gets a one-line comment explaining its responsibility (noun phrase).
2. BootConfig → ClientConfig migration: Rename BootConfig::config: String to typed ClientConfig fields. This improves reader comprehension because "config" as a String tells nothing about its structure, while ClientConfig.sip_proxy_host etc. are self-documenting.
3. RuntimeCommand::Initialize { config: String } → { config: ClientConfig }: Replace opaque String with typed struct. This transforms a function that reads as "initialize with string" to "initialize with client configuration" — a transparent statement of intent.
4. ClientConfig validation: Extract validate() method with named error variants (InvalidConfig::EmptyHost, InvalidConfig::InvalidPort) instead of leaving validation implicit. This turns "check config" into "validate config structure" — a verb phrase that communicates what happens.
5. SipClient::new constructor: Implement the Builder pattern (already designed in client_config_spec.rs) for optional fields, keeping required fields in a non-optional constructor. This makes the calling code read as SipClient::builder().stun(...).ice(true).build() instead of SipClient::new(config_with_15_fields).
6. Apply the Boy Scout Rule to any runtime code touched during migration: ensure all functions read as verb phrases, all variables as domain nouns, no single-letter variable names, no hardcoded magic values.

### Re-implementation-round Boy Scout plan (test-precision hardening is translatability)
1. src/client.rs `_assert_send_sync`: widen the bound to `SipClient: Send + Sync` and add a one-line comment stating WHY both auto-traits are required (`Arc<RuntimeHandle>` + `EventBus` are Send+Sync; the facade must stay usable across `.await` points and `tokio::spawn`). This turns an ambiguous `Send`-only helper into a truthful `Send + Sync` claim (O-001).
2. `tracing_and_metrics_specified` (src/client.rs:383): the function name already promises "tracing AND metrics"; extend the body to assert both, making the name and body agree — a lying test name is comment rot (O-002).
3. New `features_independently_selectable` / `metrics_optional_feature` tests: extract a helper `parse_feature_section(manifest: &str) -> &str` that reads as "parse the features section" and is reusable across both tests; avoid hardcoded line numbers (O-003).
4. Extract config boundary constants into named consts: `pub const MAX_USER_AGENT_BYTES: usize = 256;` and `pub const MIN_SIP_PORT: u16 = 1; pub const MAX_SIP_PORT: u16 = 65535;` (src/config.rs) so `validate()` reads as prose — "if user_agent.len() > MAX_USER_AGENT_BYTES" — instead of magic numbers; the 256/257 boundary tests reference the same consts.
5. src/runtime/reactor.rs `reactor_spawn_creates_thread`: add `let _: std::thread::JoinHandle<()> = join;` with a one-line comment ("std::thread reactor model is an architectural invariant — C002") so the type assertion documents intent (O-004).
6. Do NOT refactor production behavior beyond these doc/const touches: facade, config, and reactor are already green and translatable. The round is test-precision hardening, so the Boy Scout effort concentrates on making the tests read as precise prose that cannot lie.

tickets.title: Error Design — SipError, SipErrorKind, and M20 RuntimeCommand Error Mapping

contracts.precondition: Public API design in progress — SipClient facade methods (initialize, shutdown, etc.) define return types. Precondition test: compile-time assertion that each public async fn returns Result<_, SipError> (testUnit: "Contract C017 Precondition — API return types").
contracts.postcondition: Error design constrains API return types: all public async functions in SipClient must return Result<T, SipError>. Postcondition test: SipError struct has exactly 6 fields (kind, message, native_status, account_id, call_id, retryable) verified via construction test; SipErrorKind implements required traits (Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug) verified via compile-time assertion.
contracts.invariant: All APIs return Result<T, SipError> — invariant verified via 3 mechanisms: (1) compile-time Send+Sync assertion on SipError ensures it meets async API requirements, (2) struct field count assertion ensures no API-incompatible modifications, (3) exhaustive pattern match over SipErrorKind prevents accidental omission of error cases in API error handling.

contracts.precondition: Error design constrains API return types — M20 RuntimeCommand handlers (ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect, GetAccountInfo) must return errors through the existing SipError/SipErrorKind system. Precondition test: each M20 error converter function returns Result<T, SipError> with the same SipError type used by all other API functions.
contracts.postcondition: No new error kind variants are introduced for M20 commands — all M20 error conditions are expressed using existing SipErrorKind variants (InvalidState, AccountNotFound, NativeError). Postcondition test: exhaustive match over SipErrorKind compiles with exactly 23 variant arms; adding a hypothetical ConfConnectError variant would fail the discriminant count assertion.
contracts.invariant: No new error kinds for M20 commands — SipErrorKind variant count is invariant at 23. Verified via static assertion in test. Additionally, each M20 error condition maps to a pre-existing variant: (1) conf_port unresolved → InvalidState (same variant used for any invalid operation), (2) account deleted → AccountNotFound (standard lookup failure), (3) PJSIP API error → NativeError (generic FFI error fallback).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Complete the RFC §14 N0016 (SipError/SipErrorKind) and N0017 (M20 RuntimeCommand error mapping) design so that all four ABC inspection omissions (O-001..O-004) are closed. The production code already exists in src/error/error_design_siperror.rs (SipError struct with 6 fields, SipErrorKind enum with 23 variants, From<ReactorError>, convert_pj_status) and src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs (convert_conf_connect_error, convert_conf_disconnect_error, convert_get_account_info_error). O-003 is a genuine implementation defect: the M20 converters' non-EINVALIDOP error paths never populate native_status (always None), violating the acceptance criterion 'PJSUA FFI error → NativeError with native_status=Some(1234), retryable=true'. O-001/O-002/O-004 are test gaps: (O-001) no compile-time type-annotation asserts SipClient public async fns return Result<_, SipError>; (O-002) no test pins SipErrorKind Display for the 20 non-pinned variants; (O-004) convert_get_account_info_error's Result<AccountInfo, SipError> signature is unasserted. End state: all 23 SipErrorKind variants print their exact variant name via Display; every non-EINVALIDOP M20 PJSIP error carries native_status=Some(pj_status) and retryable=true; every public SipClient async fn and every M20 converter is compile-time-verified to return Result<T, SipError>.

### Purpose
Provide the unified, type-safe error foundation for the siprs public API so that every public surface returns Result<T, SipError> (RFC §14:612). SipErrorKind's 23-variant semantic classification lets application code handle errors without parsing message strings; the retryable flag guides retry logic; native_status preserves the PJSUA diagnostic code for logging/debugging; account_id/call_id carry the operation context. Under the ABC lens, this Purpose is only satisfied when it is *translated into testable assertions* — O-001..O-004 are precisely the untranslated remnants of this purpose. The re-implementation therefore treats "specification ⇄ test" correspondence as the deliverable, not merely "code compiles".

### Motivation
P0-3's minimal 3-variant placeholder enum (InvalidConfig/RuntimeError/Shutdown) cannot distinguish transient errors (Timeout → retry) from permanent errors (InvalidConfig → fix config). The P0-4 implementation satisfied the type design, but the ABC Inspection proved four gaps: (O-001) if SipClient::shutdown() changed to Result<(), String>, every existing test (client.rs:258, 324 use .is_ok()) would still pass; (O-002) if the Display strings of 20 SipErrorKind variants changed, no test would fail — only 3 kinds are pinned by SipError-level Display tests (error_design_siperror.rs:376, error.rs:43,50,57); (O-003) the acceptance criterion 'PJSUA FFI error → native_status=Some(1234)' is violated by code — convert_conf_connect_error delegates to SipError::internal_error (m20_runtime_command_error.rs:67-69) which hardcodes native_status=None, and no code path anywhere produces native_status=Some from a pj_status_t value (convert_pj_status returns only Option<SipErrorKind>); (O-004) the C018 type-assertion test m20_converters_return_sip_error_type (m20_runtime_command_error.rs:280-289) omits convert_get_account_info_error. Re-implementation is mandatory to make the design provably correct.

### Constraints
(1) AccountId/CallId newtypes are deferred to P0-7 (N0012) — keep the Option<u64> forward-compatible design; the 9 orphaned STUBs (TS-001..TS-010 referencing P0-7 in src/account.rs, src/call.rs, src/lib.rs, src/runtime/state.rs, src/transport.rs) are recorded as false positives for P6-2 and are out of scope. (2) pj_status_t constants are hand-coded sentinels matching PJSIP docs (PJ_SUCCESS=0, PJ_ENOMEM=-2, PJ_EINVALIDOP=150002, PJ_EBUSY=150003 in error_design_siperror.rs:36-42 and m20_runtime_command_error.rs:36-41); P4-2 STUB plans a bindgen replacement. (3) SipError is the crate's public API type — the 6-field struct and 23-variant enum are immutable invariants (C017/C018); this ticket adds no new variants and changes no field types. (4) Pure error design — no feature creep beyond error types; M20 errors reuse InvalidState/AccountNotFound/NativeError. (5) Tests must be written first (TDD Red) and must fail against the current code where an implementation gap exists (O-003).
scope: Change 1 (O-003, implementation) — src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs, convert_conf_connect_error (lines 57-70): the non-EINVALIDOP PJSIP-error branch must set native_status=Some(pj_status) and retryable=true. Action: modify. Before: Err(SipError::internal_error(format!("ConfConnect failed: pjsua_conf_connect returned {pj_status}"))) → kind=NativeError, native_status=None, retryable=true. After: Err(SipError { kind: NativeError, message: format!("ConfConnect failed: pjsua_conf_connect returned {pj_status}"), native_status: Some(pj_status), retryable: true, .. }) — either inline or via a private native_error_with_status helper. API contract: unchanged (still Err(SipError)); only field values change to satisfy the acceptance criterion 'PJSUA FFI error → native_status=Some(1234), retryable=true'.

Change 2 (O-003, implementation) — src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs, convert_conf_disconnect_error (lines 82-94): the non-EINVALIDOP branch must set native_status=Some(pj_status) and retryable=true. Action: modify. Before: Err(SipError::internal_error(format!("ConfDisconnect failed: pjsua_conf_disconnect returned {pj_status}"))) → native_status=None. After: same message, native_status=Some(pj_status), retryable=true. The PJ_EINVALIDOP branch (InvalidState, native_status=None, retryable=false) is unchanged — unresolved conf_port is a state error, not an FFI error.

Change 3 (O-003, implementation) — src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs, convert_get_account_info_error (lines 121-147): the PJSIP-error branch (pj_status != PJ_SUCCESS) must set native_status=Some(pj_status). Action: modify. Before: Err(SipError::new(NativeError, format!("GetAccountInfo failed: pjsua_acc_get_info returned {pj_status}"))) → native_status=None. After: same message, native_status=Some(pj_status), retryable=true. The AccountNotFound branch (127-134: native_status=None, retryable=false) and the P3-1 success-path STUB (142-146) are unchanged.

Change 4 (O-002, test only) — src/error/error_design_siperror.rs mod tests: add sip_error_kind_display_shows_variant_name_for_all_23 iterating a const [(SipErrorKind, &str); 23] table and asserting format!("{kind}") == variant-name string for every variant (InvalidConfig → "InvalidConfig", ..., InternalInvariantBroken → "InternalInvariantBroken"). Action: add. Before: only 3 kinds pinned by SipError-level Display tests; 20 kinds unenforced. After: all 23 individually asserted; a Display-string drift on any variant fails the test.

Change 5 (O-001, test only) — src/client.rs mod tests: add sip_client_new_and_shutdown_return_sip_error containing fn assert_new_result(_: &Result<(SipClient, broadcast::Receiver<SipEvent>), SipError>) {} and fn assert_shutdown_result(_: &Result<(), SipError>) {}, applied to the awaited results of SipClient::new(config) and SipClient::shutdown(). Action: add. Before: shutdown() return type unasserted (only .is_ok() checks); new() error type only indirectly via err.kind. After: a change to Result<(), String> or Result<_, OtherError> fails compilation.

Change 6 (O-003/O-004, test only) — src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs mod tests: (a) extend conf_connect_other_error_returns_native (180-191), conf_disconnect_other_error_returns_native (215-221), get_account_info_pjsip_error_returns_native (237-243) to assert err.native_status == Some(pj_status) and err.retryable == true; (b) extend m20_converters_return_sip_error_type (280-289) with let r3: Result<AccountInfo, SipError> = convert_get_account_info_error(true, PJ_SUCCESS);. Action: modify/add. Before: these tests assert only err.kind; the Ok(AccountInfo) success type is unasserted. After: native_status/retryable and the full Result<AccountInfo, SipError> signature are pinned.
No schema change — SipError is not serialized yet; serde derives are deferred to P1-2 behind the serde feature flag.
No config/env change — pure error-type change; no configuration surface or environment variable is touched.
Dependency: no new crates. thiserror = "2" is already in Cargo.toml (added by P0-3). No new dependencies required.

Non-change 1 — The SipError struct (6 fields) and SipErrorKind enum (23 variants) definitions in src/error/error_design_siperror.rs are NOT modified — they already conform to N0016. Only tests are added (O-002). Rationale: C017/C018 invariants fix the public shape; changing it would break the public API contract.

Non-change 2 — No new SipErrorKind variants for M20 (e.g. no ConfConnectError). M20 errors reuse InvalidState/AccountNotFound/NativeError (C018). Rationale: command-specific variants would break exhaustive-match utility and bloat the enum.

Non-change 3 — No changes to the Backend trait or RuntimeCommand enum (src/runtime/command.rs). RuntimeCommand oneshot replies continue to use ReactorError; conversion to SipError happens at the facade boundary via From<ReactorError> for SipError (error_design_siperror.rs:279-290). Rationale: runtime internals are independent of the public error type.

Affected area 1 — SipClient public API (src/client.rs): the O-001 type-annotation tests are additive and do not change the API surface. Nature: none (test-only). Response: none beyond the added test module.

Affected area 2 — src/config.rs ClientConfig::validate(): already returns Err(SipError::new(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig, msg)) from the P0-4 round. Nature: none. Response: verify via existing tests (client_config_rejects_empty_host at config.rs:370-383, client_config_rejects_zero_port at 386-404) which assert err.kind == InvalidConfig; no code change.

Affected area 3 — Downstream error consumers (P0-5 event system, P2-3, P3-1): SipEventPayload may embed SipError fields in error events (planned). Nature: data format — error type consumed by the event bus. Response: downstream tickets import SipError/SipErrorKind from crate::error; no change required in P6-2. The O-003 native_status fix improves diagnostics for these consumers.

Affected area 4 — Orphaned-STUB audit (enumerate-ticket-targets gate). The former P0-7 STUBs (TS-001..TS-010 in src/account.rs, src/call.rs, src/lib.rs, src/runtime/state.rs, src/transport.rs) were recorded as false positives for the prior round. The P6-2 re-scan shows these markers have since been re-tagged to active tickets (P3-1, P5-1, P4-2) by later implementation rounds, so the enumerate gate reports targetStubs=0 and targetCrimes=0 (serialized as "verified_empty" in Tickets.json). Nature: none — P6-2 owns no STUB/crime entries. Response: no code change; the two P6-2 target files carry only active-ticket STUB markers (P3-1/P4-2/P5-1), which are out of scope for this ticket.
testUnit: UT: [Normal — SipError construction] SipError::new(kind, msg) creates a SipError with kind, message set, native_status=None, account_id=None, call_id=None, retryable per variant (InvalidConfig=false, AccountNotFound=true, Timeout=true, NativeError=false, ShutdownInProgress=false)

UT: [Normal — SipError context] SipError::with_account_id(err, aid) returns new SipError with account_id field set, preserving all other fields; SipError::with_call_id(err, cid) similarly sets call_id
UT: [Normal — SipError Display & Debug] Display outputs "{kind}: {message}", Debug includes all 6 fields (kind, message, native_status, account_id, call_id, retryable)
UT: [Normal — SipErrorKind Display] Each of 23 SipErrorKind variants displays its variant name (e.g., InvalidConfig → "InvalidConfig", AlreadyInitialized → "AlreadyInitialized")

UT: [Normal — pj_status_t conversion] convert_pj_status(PJ_SUCCESS) returns None; convert_pj_status(PJ_ENOMEM) → NativeError with "out of memory"; convert_pj_status(PJ_EINVALIDOP) → NativeError with "invalid operation"; unknown pj_status_t → NativeError fallback

UT: [Normal — From<ReactorError>] ReactorError::ReactorDown → SipErrorKind::ShutdownInProgress (retryable=false); ReactorError::NotInitialized(m) → SipErrorKind::NotInitialized (msg preserved); ReactorError::BackendError(m) → SipErrorKind::NativeError (retryable=true, msg preserved)

UT: [Normal — M20 ConfConnect] convert_conf_connect_error(PJ_SUCCESS, call_id=42) returns Ok(()); convert_conf_connect_error(PJ_EINVALIDOP, call_id=42) → InvalidState with "conf_port not resolved for call 42"

UT: [Normal — M20 ConfDisconnect] convert_conf_disconnect_error(PJ_SUCCESS, call_id=42) returns Ok(()); convert_conf_disconnect_error(PJ_EINVALIDOP, call_id=42) → InvalidState with "conf_port not resolved for call 42"
UT: [Normal — M20 GetAccountInfo] account not found in state → AccountNotFound (retryable=false, permanent deletion); PJSIP API error → NativeError with native_status=Some(code)

UT: [Error — all context fields] SipError with all fields: kind=InvalidConfig, msg="err", native_status=Some(123), account_id=Some(456), call_id=Some(789), retryable=true — each field is correctly round-tripped
UT: [Error — no context fields] SipError with native_status=None, account_id=None, call_id=None correctly returns None for each Option field
UT: [Error — M20 non-EINVALIDOP] ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect with PJ_EBUSY etc. → NativeError with native_status set to the pj_status_t value
UT: [Boundary — empty message] SipError with message="" is accepted (message is String, not Option<String>) — no panic or truncation
UT: [Boundary — zero IDs] SipError::with_account_id(0) sets account_id=Some(0); with_call_id(0) sets call_id=Some(0) — 0 is NOT treated as None sentinel
UT: [Invariant — Send+Sync] SipError implements both Send and Sync (compile-time assertion via fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>()) [covers C017 Invariant]
UT: [Invariant — SipErrorKind traits] SipErrorKind implements Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug (compile-time assertion) [covers C017 Postcondition]

UT: [Invariant — exact 23 variants] SipErrorKind has exactly 23 variants — exhaustive match over all arms compiles; a 24th arm (e.g., ConfConnectError) would fail to compile. Verified via discriminant count assertion [covers C018 Invariant]

UT: [Invariant — struct field count] SipError struct has exactly 6 fields (kind, message, native_status, account_id, call_id, retryable) — verified by constructing with all fields [covers C017 Invariant]
UT: [Contract C017 Precondition — API return types] Compile-time type annotation test: each public SipClient method's Result type is checked as Result<_, SipError> via fn taking &Result<(), SipError>

UT: [Contract C018 Invariant — no M20 variants] Compile-time exhaustive match over SipErrorKind has exactly 24 arms (23 variants + 1 wildcard for future-proofing with compile_error on match) — verified via static assertion

UT: [Normal — O-002 closure] SipErrorKind Display prints the exact variant name for all 23 variants. Build a const table [(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig, "InvalidConfig"), (SipErrorKind::InvalidState, "InvalidState"), ..., (SipErrorKind::InternalInvariantBroken, "InternalInvariantBroken")] and assert format!("{kind}") == expected for each entry. Test name: sip_error_kind_display_shows_variant_name_for_all_23. Fails RED if any of the 20 currently-unpinned Display arms diverges from the variant identifier (the pre-existing suite only pins InvalidConfig, NativeError, ShutdownInProgress via SipError-level Display tests).

UT: [Error — O-003 closure] M20 converters preserve native_status and retryable on non-EINVALIDOP PJSIP errors. convert_conf_connect_error(PJ_EBUSY=150003, 42).unwrap_err() → kind==NativeError, native_status==Some(150003), retryable==true; convert_conf_disconnect_error(PJ_EBUSY, 42).unwrap_err() → same; convert_get_account_info_error(true, PJ_EBUSY).unwrap_err() → kind==NativeError, native_status==Some(150003), retryable==true. Test names: conf_connect_other_error_keeps_native_status_and_retryable / conf_disconnect_other_error_keeps_native_status_and_retryable / get_account_info_pjsip_error_keeps_native_status_and_retryable (or extend the existing *_returns_native tests). UT: [Boundary — O-003 boundary] M20 converter semantic boundary between state errors and FFI errors. PJ_SUCCESS (0) → Ok(()), no native_status leak; PJ_EINVALIDOP (150002) → Err(InvalidState) with native_status==None and retryable==false (unresolved conf_port is a state error, not an FFI error — native_status must remain None); unknown code (-9999) → Err(NativeError) with native_status==Some(-9999) and retryable==true. Test names: m20_converter_distinguishes_state_error_from_ffi_error / get_account_info_account_not_found_keeps_native_status_none.

Fails RED (compile error) if any return type diverges from Result<T, SipError>.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】SipError struct constructible with 6 fields (kind, message, native_status, account_id, call_id, retryable). SipErrorKind has exactly 23 discriminant variants. Both implement Send + Sync for async API compatibility. retryable flag set per variant: transient errors (AccountNotFound, CallNotFound, Timeout, NativeError) retryable=true; config/terminal errors (InvalidConfig, ShutdownInProgress, InternalInvariantBroken) retryable=false. Every non-EINVALIDOP M20 PJSIP error carries native_status=Some(pj_status) and retryable=true (O-003 closure).
- 【On error】Error conversion functions (convert_pj_status, convert_conf_connect_error, convert_conf_disconnect_error, convert_get_account_info_error, From<ReactorError>) never panic. No uninitialized SipError instances. SipErrorKind always from valid set of 23 variants. On error, no code path silently drops the FFI diagnostic code: a non-EINVALIDOP pj_status must be preserved in native_status (O-003). An unresolved conf_port (PJ_EINVALIDOP) maps to InvalidState with native_status=None and retryable=false (state error, not FFI error) — the semantic boundary between state errors and FFI errors is stable.
- 【Internal state】SipError is a pure data struct with no mutable state. Once constructed, immutable (no setters — only with_account_id/with_call_id builder-style constructors return new instances preserving all other fields). SipErrorKind is a Copy enum (no heap allocs). M20 converters are deterministic pure functions of (account_exists, pj_status) / (pj_status, call_id) — same inputs always produce the same SipError field values.
- 【Boundary】account_id/call_id use Option<u64>: None = context N/A, Some(0) = valid non-None sentinel for future newtype upgrade (P0-7). native_status Option<i32>: None = no FFI code, Some(status) = pj_status_t value (PJ_SUCCESS=0 is only ever Some when an error carried a zero status — converters never wrap Ok in Some(0)). message always String (constructors accept Into<String>); empty message accepted without panic. pj_status_t boundary: 0 → Ok/None, PJ_EINVALIDOP (150002) → InvalidState, every other non-zero value → NativeError with native_status=Some(value).

SipError is logged via tracing::error!() in the SipClient facade when propagating errors to callers (client.rs:113-118 maps the reactor-spawn failure, client.rs:200-202 maps the shutdown failure). The O-003 fix enriches every M20 FFI error log line with native_status=Some(pj_status) through the Debug impl (e.g. SipError { kind: NativeError, native_status: Some(150003), .. }). No separate error-logging infrastructure is added in this ticket.

The O-001 compile-time type-annotation tests serve as a static health gate: they guarantee the public API never accidentally swaps SipError for a different error type — a regression that no runtime test previously detected.

tickets.title: Codec Policy, SRTP, Transport Reconnection & Shutdown Command Routing

contracts.precondition: Codec policy is defined in ClientConfig — either preferred_codecs non-empty (explicit mode) or empty (auto mode). Input schema: `codecs: &[CodecInfo]` where `CodecInfo { codec_id: String }` (e.g. "PCMU/8000/1", "opus/48000/2", "G722/8000/1") and `preferred_codecs: &[String]`. enumerate_codecs() returns the available native codecs from PJSIP. Testable form: build a `Vec<CodecInfo>` + `Vec<String>` fixture; empty preferred slice = auto mode.
contracts.postcondition: After `CodecAutoMode::apply()`, each codec in the system has a priority assigned in the returned `HashMap<String, u8>`: Opus=255, PCMU=254, all others=0. When `preferred_codecs` is non-empty, auto mode is bypassed and an empty map is returned (no priorities changed). Duplicate codec_id in the enumeration yields Err(SipErrorKind::NativeError) with message containing "duplicate". Testable form: assert exact map values per codec id; assert empty-map bypass; assert duplicate rejection.
contracts.invariant: Opus always receives priority 255 in auto mode; PCMU always receives priority 254. These values are immutable named constants (OPUS_PRIORITY=255, PCMU_PRIORITY=254). The priority assignment is a pure function of codec_id alone (no state dependence). Priority values are u8: 255=max valid, 254=fallback, 0=disabled. Testable form: iterate the returned map and assert every `opus/*` == 255 and every `PCMU/8000/1` == 254.

contracts.precondition: Transport configuration is defined (TransportConfig enum with UDP/TCP/TLS variants per N0015). SrtpPolicy has one of three values (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory). validate() signature: `SrtpPolicy::validate(&self, feature_enabled: bool) -> Result<(), SipError>` where feature_enabled is the runtime srtp feature flag. Testable form: instantiate each variant and call validate with both flag states.
contracts.postcondition: SrtpPolicy::validate() returns Ok(()) when: (a) policy is Disabled (feature state irrelevant), or (b) policy is Mandatory/Optional AND srtp feature flag is enabled. Returns Err(InvalidConfig) with message containing the policy variant (e.g. "SRTP Mandatory requires srtp feature to be enabled") when Mandatory/Optional AND feature flag is disabled. Never panics — always returns Result. Testable form: assert Ok/Err per variant × flag; assert err.kind == InvalidConfig and message context.
contracts.invariant: SrtpPolicy Disabled is universally valid. Mandatory and Optional are gated by the srtp feature — at the API level, the validate function receives a bool feature_enabled flag that enforces this gate (no #[cfg] in the function body, enabling testability without conditional compilation). Testable form: loop both flag states for Disabled and assert Ok; assert Mandatory/Optional are rejected exactly when feature_enabled=false.

contracts.precondition: Reactor shutdown sequence has started (is_shutting_down == true). A RuntimeCommand is submitted to the reactor for dispatch. Command schema (src/runtime/command.rs, P0-6): `GetAccountInfo { native_acc_id: u32, reply: oneshot }`, `ConfConnect { call_id: u64, reply: oneshot }`, `ConfDisconnect { call_id: u64, reply: oneshot }`. Testable form: build commands with tokio::sync::oneshot channels; pass is_shutting_down=true/false.
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownCommandRouter::classify() returns Permit for GetAccountInfo (command forwarded to execute_get_account_info). Returns Reject(SipError::invalid_state("shutting down")) with kind=InvalidState and message containing 'shutting down' for ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect. Returns Reject(InvalidState) for all other commands (catch-all). When is_shutting_down=false, all commands are Permitted. Testable form: assert Permit/Reject per command × shutdown state; assert err.kind == InvalidState and message contains 'shutting down'.
contracts.invariant: GetAccountInfo is always Permitted during shutdown. ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are always Rejected during shutdown. This classification is invariant per variant — no state or context changes the routing decision during shutdown. ShutdownCommandRouter is stateless; classify() is a pure function of (cmd, is_shutting_down). Testable form: exhaustive match over the 3 M20 variants + a non-M20 variant (e.g. Hangup) asserting the per-variant outcome is constant.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Deliver three independent, fully-tested policy modules in the siprs media/lifecycle layer, all of which already have a concrete implementation from the prior P1-1 round and are remanded solely to close the ABC test-precision gaps: (1) two-layer codec selection (explicit vs auto mode) where auto mode assigns Opus=255, PCMU=254, and all other codecs=0 whenever preferred_codecs is empty — `CodecAutoMode::apply` in src/config/m20_codec_auto_mode.rs; (2) SRTP policy with runtime feature-flag gating (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory) plus a transport-reconnection backoff policy — `SrtpPolicy`, `ReconnectPolicy`, `TransportProtocol` in src/config/srtp_transport_reconnect.rs; and (3) M20 shutdown command routing that permits GetAccountInfo while rejecting ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect — `ShutdownCommandRouter::classify` in src/error/m20_shutdown_routing.rs. The specific deliverable of this round is a corrected test suite that resolves omission O-001 (deterministic-jitter test for jitter_ratio > 0) and O-002 (tightened jitter_ratio=1.0 bound to [0, 2*computed]), while keeping all 3 contracts (C042/C043/C045) at 100% test coverage.

### Purpose
These policies form the core control layer for media configuration and lifecycle management in the M20 extension. Without them: (a) codecs default to PJSIP's built-in ordering instead of Opus-first prioritization, (b) SRTP cannot be controlled via config (always enabled or always disabled), and (c) shutdown behavior for M20 commands is undefined — the reactor would attempt to dispatch media operations during teardown, causing undefined PJSIP behavior. Each policy closes a gap between raw PJSIP capability and intentional application-level control. The purpose of this re-implementation round is specifically to make the *tests* precise enough that a regression in the deterministic-jitter contract or the jitter bound is actually detectable (violation detection: B, test precision: C).

### Motivation
The ABC Inspection Pipeline (criterion B — Violation Detection, criterion C — Test Precision) proved that the prior test suite could not distinguish a compliant implementation from a defective one: (1) O-001 — the only determinism test used jitter_ratio=0.0, which the implementation short-circuits to 0.0, so an RNG substitution in the jitter>0 branch would pass every existing test; (2) O-002 — the jitter_ratio=1.0 test asserted delay <= 2*max_delay (120s for base=1s/max=60s/attempt=5) when the acceptance-criterion bound is 2*computed = 64s, so a delay in (64s, 120s] would violate the spec yet pass the test. These are test-design defects, not implementation defects; they must be corrected in this final round. The underlying modules are preconditions for P1-2 (Security & Platform) and P1-3 (Audio Pipeline).

### Constraints
1. No FFI dependency: configure_codecs_auto_mode must produce a priority map (pure function) rather than calling pjsua_codec_set_priority directly — the FFI binding is deferred to P2-4. 2. SrtpPolicy::validate receives a bool feature_enabled flag rather than using #[cfg(feature = "srtp")] directly in the function body, enabling testability without conditional compilation. 3. ShutdownCommandRouter::classify must be a pure function — no reactor state access, no async, no side effects. 4. No new dependencies beyond the existing crate's Cargo.toml (no random crate for jitter — use a deterministic seed based on attempt number). 5. The `Initial Design Artifact` header in each target file must never be deleted or edited. 6. All 32 targetCrimes are false positives (ORPHAN_TICKET_REF belonging to P0-7/P2-4) and must remain resolved as false positives; the 2 foundOmissions (O-001, O-002) must be resolved by adding/tightening test assertions, never by weakening the implementation or existing tests.

tickets.notes:
Implementation steps:
1. Verify the 3 target files already contain the full implementations from the P1-1 round (CodecAutoMode, SrtpPolicy/ReconnectPolicy/TransportProtocol, ShutdownCommandRouter) with the `Initial Design Artifact` header intact.
2. Add the O-001 test `reconnect_policy_jitter_ratio_positive_is_deterministic` in src/config/srtp_transport_reconnect.rs: construct `ReconnectPolicy::new(1s, 60s, 0.5)`, call `next_delay(3)` twice, assert_eq! both results (catches RNG substitution in the jitter>0 branch).
3. Tighten the O-002 test `reconnect_policy_jitter_ratio_one_produces_variable_delay`: compute `computed = min(1s * 2^5, 60s) = 32s` from the inputs and assert `computed <= delay <= computed * 2` (64s), replacing the loose `delay <= 2 * max_delay` (120s) bound.
4. Re-run the full test suite via `make test`; confirm all existing + new tests pass green.
5. Run quality checks (`run-quality-checks.js`) and resolve any findings by fixing code only.

Risks:
- The deterministic jitter formula (`(attempt * 0x9E3779B9) >> 32` as a fraction) is intentionally non-cryptographic; it must remain a pure function of attempt for the O-001 determinism test to hold. Any move to a real RNG must be rejected by the new test.
- The tightened O-002 bound depends on the exact exponential formula `min(base * 2^attempt, max)`; changing the formula (e.g. full-jitter) requires updating the bound computation, not just the assertion constant.

Caveats:
- `SrtpPolicy::validate` is gated by a runtime bool, not `#[cfg(feature = "srtp")]`, per constraint #2 — the actual feature-gate wiring lives in ClientConfig (P0-3) and is out of scope here.
- The `GetAccountInfo` M20 variant uses `native_acc_id: u32` (not u64) in src/runtime/command.rs — test fixtures must match this exact type.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】When `preferred_codecs` is empty, `CodecAutoMode::apply` assigns Opus=255, PCMU=254, and all other codecs=0 for every enumerated `CodecInfo`. When `preferred_codecs` is non-empty, auto mode is bypassed and the returned map is empty (no priorities changed).
- 【Normal establishment】`SrtpPolicy::validate` returns `Ok(())` when: `Disabled` (always, regardless of feature_enabled) or `Mandatory`/`Optional` with feature_enabled=true.
- 【Normal establishment】During shutdown (is_shutting_down=true), `ShutdownCommandRouter::classify` returns `Permit` for `GetAccountInfo` and `Reject(InvalidState)` for `ConfConnect`/`ConfDisconnect`; during normal operation (is_shutting_down=false) every command is `Permit`.
- 【On error】`SrtpPolicy::validate` must never panic or crash — it always returns `Result<(), SipError>` with `InvalidConfig` kind for feature violations.
- 【On error】`CodecAutoMode::apply` with a duplicate codec_id in the enumeration must return `Err(NativeError)` without partial priority assignment (no map is produced).
- 【On error】`ReconnectPolicy::new` must reject invalid parameters (zero base_delay, max_delay < base_delay, jitter_ratio outside [0.0, 1.0]) at construction time with `InvalidConfig`, never at `next_delay` call time.
- 【Internal state】`ReconnectPolicy` fields (base_delay, max_delay, jitter_ratio) are immutable after construction — no setter methods provided; accessors return construction-time values.
- 【Internal state】`ShutdownCommandRouter` has no mutable state — `classify()` is a pure function of (cmd, is_shutting_down) with no side effects.
- 【Internal state】`CodecAutoMode` is a stateless unit struct; `apply` has no side effects and no dependence on ambient state.
- 【Boundary】Codec priority values are u8: Opus=255 (max valid priority), PCMU=254 (fallback), others=0 (disabled). These exact values are invariants backed by named constants `OPUS_PRIORITY` and `PCMU_PRIORITY`.
- 【Boundary】jitter_ratio must be in [0.0, 1.0] — values outside this range are rejected at construction.
- 【Boundary】`ReconnectPolicy::next_delay(attempt)` with jitter_ratio=1.0 produces a delay in [0, 2*computed] where `computed = min(base_delay * 2^attempt, max_delay)`; the same (attempt, policy) pair always produces the same delay (deterministic jitter even when jitter_ratio > 0).

Evidence gathered from the RFC graph (N0041, N0042, N0044 + parents N0040, N0043, N0015) and source inspection (src/config/m20_codec_auto_mode.rs, src/config/srtp_transport_reconnect.rs, src/error/m20_shutdown_routing.rs, src/config/codec_policy_fallback.rs, src/runtime/command.rs, src/error/error_design_siperror.rs, src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs, src/config.rs, src/error.rs):

1. Current source state — all three target files are FULLY IMPLEMENTED from the P1-1 round (not stubs): m20_codec_auto_mode.rs (267 lines, 7 tests), srtp_transport_reconnect.rs (389 lines, 13 tests), m20_shutdown_routing.rs (247 lines, 8 tests). Each carries the `Initial Design Artifact` header. Module declarations exist: `pub mod m20_codec_auto_mode; pub mod srtp_transport_reconnect;` in src/config.rs and `pub mod m20_shutdown_routing;` in src/error.rs.

2. RFC N0041 (§29 Codec Auto Mode): two-layer selection — preferred_codecs non-empty = explicit mode (bypass), empty = auto mode (Opus=255, PCMU=254, others=0). RFC code calls `ffi::pjsua_codec_set_priority`; constraint #1 defers FFI to P2-4. Parent N0040 (codec_policy_fallback.rs, already implemented) defines `NegotiatedCodec` (Pcmu/Opus) and `CodecSelectionPolicy` (Ordered/PreferOpusFallbackPcmu). `CallMediaPreferences.preferred_codecs: Vec<Codec>` is the config field consumed by auto mode.

3. RFC N0042 (§30 SRTP & §31 Transport Reconnection): SrtpPolicy (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory), feature flag default OFF, feature-disabled → Mandatory/Optional = InvalidConfig. ReconnectPolicy = exponential backoff `min(base * 2^attempt, max) * (1 + jitter)`. Transport: UDP stateless (no reconnect), TCP/TLS connection-oriented (reconnect). Parent N0015 defines TransportConfig (Udp/Tcp/Tls). Actual transport lifecycle deferred to P2-4.

4. RFC N0044 (§32 Shutdown Command Routing): three M20 RuntimeCommand variants — GetAccountInfo (permitted, read-only), ConfConnect (rejected), ConfDisconnect (rejected). Uses `SipError::invalid_state("shutting down")`. Parent N0043 defines the idempotent shutdown state machine (stop accepting commands, BYE/CANCEL calls, unregister, drain audio, pjsua_destroy).

5. Supporting types (verified): `RuntimeCommand` in src/runtime/command.rs has `GetAccountInfo { native_acc_id: u32, reply: oneshot }`, `ConfConnect { call_id: u64, reply }`, `ConfDisconnect { call_id: u64, reply }`. `SipError { pub kind, pub message, pub native_status, pub account_id, pub call_id, pub retryable }` with `new(kind, msg)`, `invalid_state(msg)`, `internal_error(msg)`. `SipErrorKind` includes InvalidConfig, InvalidState, NativeError.

6. ABC violations to resolve (foundOmissions): O-001 — determinism is only tested at jitter_ratio=0.0 (short-circuited to 0.0 at srtp_transport_reconnect.rs:181), so an RNG in the jitter>0 branch is undetectable; the fix is a new test calling next_delay(3) twice with jitter_ratio=0.5 and asserting equality. O-002 — the jitter=1.0 test (line 356) asserts delay <= 2*max_delay (120s) when the spec bound for base=1s/max=60s/attempt=5 is 2*computed=64s; the fix computes the bound from the inputs.

7. Verification command: `make test` (Makefile `test:` target). Quality gates: `run-quality-checks.js`; stub/crime scan via `.claude/scripts/tickets/scan-crimes.sh`.

Translatability improvements applied to code touched by this ticket (verified against the current implementation):

1. Function names as verb phrases: `apply()` (applies auto-mode priorities), `validate()` (validates policy against the feature flag), `classify()` (classifies a command during shutdown), `next_delay()` (computes the next retry delay), `needs_reconnect()` (answers whether the protocol requires reconnection). All are imperative verbs that read as sentences at call sites.

2. Variable names as domain concepts: `codec_id` (not "id" or "codec"), `preferred_codecs` (not "pc" or "list"), `jitter_ratio` (not "j" or "r"), `base_delay`/`max_delay` (backoff parameters), `native_acc_id` (matches the existing RuntimeCommand field), `is_shutting_down` (boolean with is_ prefix per coding standards).

3. One function, one responsibility: `CodecAutoMode::apply` only computes the priority map (no FFI, no state mutation); `SrtpPolicy::validate` only validates (no side effects); `ShutdownCommandRouter::classify` only routes (no execution); `ReconnectPolicy::next_delay` only computes a delay (no timer scheduling). `assign_auto_priority` is extracted as a single-codec mapping helper so `apply` reads as "for each codec, assign its auto priority".

4. Named constants: `OPUS_PRIORITY = 255` and `PCMU_PRIORITY = 254` replace magic numbers; the priority semantics (255=max, 254=fallback, 0=disabled) are documented at the constant site.

5. No error swallowing: all fallible functions return `Result<_, SipError>`; error messages carry diagnostic context (policy variant for validation, parameter name for ReconnectPolicy::new, "duplicate" + codec_id for enumeration errors, "shutting down" for routing rejects).

6. Omissions-driven cleanups this round: (a) the O-002 test must compute its assertion bound from the inputs (`min(base * 2^attempt, max)`) rather than hardcoding a loose 2*max_delay, so the bound and the implementation formula cannot drift apart; (b) the O-001 test documents why jitter must stay a pure function of attempt (deterministic seed) at the test site. Existing code outside these files is left untouched (Boy Scout within reasonable scope).

Source ticket P3-2 (PJSIP FFI Layer, Runtime State & AudioMixer Architecture) defined the CallEntry state machine (C027) and ClientState with a calls map keyed by CallId (C046). SipAccountHandle::make_call was left returning a hardcoded Ok(1) because the MakeCall reply did not yet carry the assigned CallId. testUnit: UT: [C027] make_call with a mock reactor replying Ok(42) returns 42.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】make_call() awaits the MakeCall reply and returns the CallId assigned by the backend reactor — the hardcoded Ok(1) at src/api/public_api_design.rs:142 is removed.
【Happy path】The returned CallId matches the CallEntry.id recorded in ClientState.calls (C046), so subsequent Hangup/Hold operate on a valid id.
【Error case】When the reactor replies Err(ReactorError), make_call() maps it to a SipError (e.g. SipErrorKind::InviteFailed) and does not fabricate a CallId.
【Error case】When the reply channel is dropped before sending, make_call() surfaces an error (oneshot recv failure) instead of returning a hardcoded value.
【Edge case】Backend-assigned CallIds are unique across consecutive MakeCall commands — no two calls share the same returned id.
The MakeCall reply is sent exactly once, preserving the RuntimeCommand reply discipline.

Source ticket P3-2 specified AudioWorkerTask with a Tokio JoinHandle for the blocking-pool worker. The handle is stored as `Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` (src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:279) and marked #[allow(dead_code)], so the worker's task lifecycle is not actively managed. This work item replaces the unused Option<JoinHandle> with a non-optional active JoinHandle and integrates shutdown so the handle is always awaited on shutdown.
scope: - src/runtime/audio_worker.rs - change `handle: Option<JoinHandle<()>>` to an active non-optional `JoinHandle<()>`; integrate shutdown to always await it
- src/runtime/mod.rs - verify re-export/compile
- Out of scope: FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort) remains deferred until FFI audio integration is available; AudioMixer behavior unchanged.
- Impact: AudioWorkerTask always owns a live worker task; shutdown deterministically joins the worker.
testUnit: UT: [C034] AudioWorkerTask::spawn returns a worker whose handle field is non-optional (compile-time).
UT: [C035] spawn -> shutdown() completes and is_running() becomes false.
UT: [C035] spawn with a mock source -> process_frame produces frames -> shutdown stops production.
UT: [Error] Double shutdown returns promptly without panic.
UT: [Boundary] handle.is_finished() is false immediately after spawn (task still running).
UT: [C038] runtime/audio_worker.rs contains no unsafe keyword (grep test).
testIntegration: IT: [Lifecycle] Spawn N workers concurrently, each with its own mixer, add sources, and verify independent shutdown with no cross-contamination.
IT: [Shutdown] A worker whose task panics (via a panicking source) still resolves shutdown() without hanging.
testExceptions: FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame) is deferred to when FFI audio integration lands; the worker lifecycle is verified with MockAsyncAudioSource only.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】After spawn(), the worker holds a non-optional JoinHandle - no Option unwrap needed to observe the running task.
【Happy path】shutdown() sets the shutdown flag and awaits the JoinHandle; after shutdown returns, is_running() == false and the worker task has terminated.
【Happy path】A worker with active sources keeps producing mixed frames until shutdown, then stops cleanly.
【Error case】shutdown() called twice is idempotent - the second call does not panic and returns promptly.
【Edge case】If the worker task panics, shutdown() still resolves (the join returns Err which is logged, not panicked).
【Edge case】spawn() from a tokio runtime context always yields a running JoinHandle (handle.is_finished() == false immediately after spawn).

tickets.title: Implement PhaseTimeout handling for per-call timeout tracking during shutdown

contracts.precondition: SipClient has been initialized (initialize() completed successfully); reactor is running and accepting commands
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownSpec orchestrates idempotent shutdown: (1) atomic is_shutdown_started swap prevents re-entry, (2) all active calls are BYE/CANCELed, (3) accounts unregistered, (4) audio worker drained, (5) backend.shutdown() called, (6) reactor loop exits
contracts.invariant: Shutdown is idempotent: first call executes full sequence and returns Ok(()); second and subsequent calls return Ok(()) immediately without executing the sequence again

contracts.precondition: ShutdownSpec.is_shutdown_started() returns true after first atomic swap
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownCommandRouter.classify() correctly routes commands during shutdown: GetAccountInfo → Permit, ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect → Reject(InvalidState), all others → Reject(InvalidState). Reactor applies this routing before command execution.
contracts.invariant: GetAccountInfo is always Permitted during shutdown (read-only state check). ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are always Rejected during shutdown (media mutation is unsafe during teardown).

This marker was left as a stub because CancelCalls iterates calls with no deadline and no per-call timeout accounting. This work item resolves it by implementing PhaseTimeout handling for per-call timeout tracking during shutdown.
scope: - src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:144-146 — remove #[allow(dead_code)] and consume the timeout field
- src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:217-261 — execute_phase (especially CancelCalls) applies the per-phase timeout; a phase that exceeds it produces ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout
- src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:232-239 — per-call hangup deadline tracking (deadline per call and an overall phase deadline)
- src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:87-90 — ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout becomes reachable
- Out of scope: ShutdownCommandRouter command gating (P4-3/C045); audio drain coordination (P4-3/C050).

UT: [Error] a backend hangup that blocks beyond the timeout yields ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout with the correct phase and timeout.

testExceptions: Deterministic wall-clock timing cannot be asserted in unit tests without sleeping; tests use a timeout-aware backend (or a MockBackend configured to report hangup as pending) and assert the PhaseTimeout error type and the continuation behavior rather than exact durations. tokio::time::timeout keeps the async tests fast.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】A phase that completes within the configured timeout returns Ok and records no timeout (existing shutdown tests stay green).

【Error case】A phase (e.g. CancelCalls) that exceeds the configured timeout produces ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout { phase, timeout } — and, per C044, subsequent phases still execute and the first error is returned.
【Edge case】The timeout is applied per phase boundary (per-call deadline plus an overall phase deadline), not as an unbounded per-call wait.
【Edge case】A zero or very small timeout does not panic — it degrades to an immediate PhaseTimeout for slow backends.
